Wow wow wow, this place has some amazing ice cream options! I am all about the fun flavors. They have a sampler for 4 scoops of different types of ice cream ($4ish dollars, such a good deal!) so I could try a few flavors! My favorites were the graham central station and the coconut cream pie for originality and some awesome chunks of yumminess mixed inside. Will definitely be back!
Very unique ice cream and the cutest stickers! I'm sad the original place closed down; regardless, the ice cream is very yummy!

I don't really like to give reviews unless I've tried something more than once. After 5 visits, I've decided that their macarons are my least favorite out of their selection of desserts. Once you've had macarons from Paris & NYC nothing else compares

My family went there last night, party of six, and Mary Coyle's did not disappoint. Service was great and the ice cream was as delicious as the original Mary Coyle's on Thomas. We have been following the Mary Coyle's restaurants numerous times since the '60s. So glad they reopened on Central Ave. Keep it up!

Hidden gem behind the escalator at the Venetian. Coffee is delicious and their pastries OMG. The macaroons are very sweet but perfect texture and the almond claw is so good. Definitely would recommend it.
This place always has fresh pastries and great coffee. The staff is amazing and treats you like family treats you like family.

More like 2.5 just rating the experience. Cons: 1) Line was long and slow moving and not well organized. 2) Product description does not tell you which ones have nuts and which don't. 3) Staff did not seem knowledgable when questioned about their products and gave incorrect info. Pros: 1) You can watch bakers at work while waiting in line. 2) The prices were not as outrageous as I would have expected from a TV famous bakery. 3) Staff was friendly. Will update when we eat the baked goods.

Loved it! As soon as you walk into the building, you smell the buttery cones. The ice cream is flavorful, creamy, just altogether fatty. I chose the duo and ordered banana cream pie and the dark roast coffee. I think this was a great combo and I enjoyed every last bit of it. The banana cream pie had chunks of banana and pie crust, it was just like eating the pie itself. If I lived in Cleveland, I would only buy Mitchell's, they're THAT GOOD. Mitchell's has some seating available in their brightly lit shop and the line goes fairly quick. I'm pretty sure that everything Mitchell's offers is delicious and rich. My only con is that they don't offer crumbled waffle cone as a topping. How do we try and get a store opened up in NOVA?

We went here for the 1st time as part of our family double date. There was a 45 minute line! People behind us said they stood in line a previous time but didn't get in on time so here they were again. Glad we didn't give up. We tried all these pastries & none failed us (picture will be posted in pink box): strawberry cheesecake, chocolate mousse cake, Tiramisu, cream puff, dark chocolate mouse cake, & large chocolate chip cookie. All were amazing but dark chocolate mousse cake was heavenly!! Even though it was good, I'd skip the cookie because it wasn't worth $4+. Downfall, pricing is steep for diabetes proned baked goods - even though they did good, nothing was too sweet except maybe the cookie. All this came out to $50...I am coming back for the dark chocolate mousse. I read other people's reviews & want to try their lobster tail, cannoli, & crumb cake next!! CAN'T WAIT, going again this weekend!! :-D

Donut Bar is local favorite and sells out nearly every day. RESTAURANT: The restaurant is small because it is used mostly for to-go orders. However, there are some chairs to dine-in. The restaurant is always clean and the vibe is very fresh. SERVICE: The servers are extremely friendly, efficient, and quick. I always walk out feeling better than when I walked in. FOOD: There are traditional donuts, but also eye-catching donuts, which come in unique flavors and huge sizes. If you go during happy hour, which typically around noon, you can buy a dozen donuts for $10. I think it is one of the best donuts in town. However, I feel the donuts are a little too dry and dense. I also find the frosting to be a little hard. ALL STAR DEAL: Happy hour.

My wife saw Milk Bar all over social media and had to try. Overall the presentation was nice and it is in Cosmopolitan, so don't expect decent pricing. We ordered the soft serve with and without the corn flake topping, 4 cookies, and the birthday cake balls. We were disappointed, all I can say is that it tastes like super salty dessert. Just overloaded with salt. We weren't expecting great things, but few things are more frustrating than paying a lot of money for bad food. The cookies and cake balls were ok, but again, too much salt and you can get better desserts else where in Las Vegas, like Crumbl or try one of the many bakeries in China Town. I'm giving two stars because the soft serve with the corn flake topping was good, but it was horrible without the topping. We ended up throwing away half of what we ordered, it was not good and waayyyyy too salty. If you like salty desserts, then by all means, but it wasn't for me. There are so many better places in Vegas for desserts, I will never go back to Milk Bar.
Get the peanut butter and add a scoop of chocolate. I did and it was delicious. There a nice spot out back where you can sit in the shade.

Worst cupcake I have ever eaten. We were in Vegas for a week and this was on my list of places to visit. I consider myself a dessert connoisseur and was sad that I was so disappointed. I wanted them to be good. I had the Valentine trio special. It was stale and tasted like purse sugar. I have never given just one star, but this review was important enough that I do. I will not return nor waste my money. Feel free to try them for yourself and make your decision as to whether or not they are all they're hyped up to be.
No skim milk. Overpriced.
Cute little ice cream parlor with friendly staff and delicious ice cream for something small or for a whole group. Comfortable, clean and not too busy to enjoy.

I pulled in the lot at 10:55 PM on Saturday night on the first of august my sons birthday to get some treats for me and my family. When I went to the doors a bit later, they were already locked. I checked my watch to make sure, and it was 10:57 PM. This is NOT OKAY WHEN IT IS NOT THE CLOSING TIME THAT IS ADVERTISED! We drove by the drive thru, and it was closed as well. While driving by the car at the window, we heard in the background, "We aren't doing that 11:02 shit anymore!" This is very unprofessional to hear at what is supposed to be a family friendly establishment. This was the last straw for me, and I will not be coming back because of the issues I had experienced.

Got the rose milk latte, which was delicious. I'm glad this place started serving boba! We got a small, I believe, for ~$5. Tables were sort of filthy, so we had to wipe them down ourselves before sitting, but I believe there was only one person working behind the counter at the time, and he was understandably very busy with orders by himself. The flavors are pretty unique, so I'd go again!

Very pissed, DO NOT ORDER TRUFFLES on Uber eats, just pait $13 for one truffle advertised as nutella truffles, it was my bad for assuming it would be more than one, but it was also advertised in the pleural and I couldnt believe they would charge $13 for one truffle, they did.

My friends and I had just finished an amazing dinner at Windsor and we were full but my friend insisted that go get some ice cream next door. The inside of this shop is adorable. It reminds me of a old soda shop. The ice cream is homemade and they had all sorts of candy and other homemade goodies. I tried the Oh my Affogato which was a coke/ coffee ice cream float. My first time trying the Affogato and it was delicious!!! I'll defiantly be coming back next time I'm in the area :)
Don't miss much about my country. But when I occasionally do, this the place I go. A great blend of french taste and American humour. Merci!

The consistency of the ice cream is pretty great, it's thick enough to not be runny but still thin enough to be soft serve. I got the Crack Pie and the Cereal Milk as a twist. Both flavors are good in my opinion but I wouldn't say anything special. Same with the Cornflake Crunch, I think it complements the ice cream very well but it's nothing too outstanding. Overall, a little overpriced for what it is ($6-7 for a small cup). I think a part of it is that you're just there for the name because it's a famous place that started in New York (?)

Absolutely by far the BEST ice cream I've ever had. It is so mouth watering creamy and flavorful. Tons of delicious flavors. I'm not normally an ice cream person and I got 3 scoops it was SO good! I recommend this place as a must for desert or treat!!! Yumtown!!

The cookie cup was delicious! Two scoops of Gelato with a homemade toasted marshmallow on top of an almond macaroon! The service was excellent as well, we were welcomed by friendly staff. Great place for a sweet treat, we will definately be back!

Wow, the reviews did not lie about this place! I drove from Tempe to stop at this gem after a particularly disheartening afternoon. It was empty at 4 pm to my luck so the girl at the counter gave me a few samples and said to take my time as she described the flavors and combinations with such passion! A connoisseur just like me! I was without a doubt made to feel better by her benevolence as well as the incredible flavors of the S'mores ice cream sundae I indulged in. I paired it with chocolate and peanut butter (but probably should have gone with the vanilla that she recommended due to chocolate overload). I'm not a fan of marshmallows, but it seems they make them there (or have a magical vendor) and let me tell you...it was delicious as was the entire concoction! That definitely turned my frown upside down. I also took a pint to go like a fat kid.
Good place for ice cream on a nice day. The line can get pretty long, but it typically moves quickly.

First, this is a very small stand with no tables. Second, the cake I bought was dry and not fresh. Maybe it was better on the morning, but I could not finish it and threw it away. My mom is a professional baker, so I am a little spoiled, but this one is definitely not a 4-star bakery.
We tried the Cheese Danish w lemon. Creamy, flaky and not overly sweet. It was fantastic. Chocolate croissant was yummy too!

"Paris is always a good idea they, say!" This line coined by Audrey Hepburn! Bouchon is the slice of Paris here in Las Vegas! The French know simple, delicious, elegant flavors of food customization options. Best kept secret in Las Vegas is Bouchon, order your food from the restaurant and dine down here by the cafe. Their is always seating, and the views are amazing. Watch the gondolas on the canals as they sail along. The endless tourists and enjoy themselves as they pass your table. Once in a great while someone will wave hello. Be polite and wave back. Your in the most beautiful spot. Umbrella over head, the beautiful Las Vegas spring breeze on your shoulder moving and messing up your hair. Let the wind toss your hair around. That coffee in my hand stimulates my mind and relaxes me. As the morning moves along I decided to have a Mimosa too. Nothing like treating your orange juice to some Champagne. Our most recent visit was for breakfast. The waffles that we enjoyed were covered with strawberries. These waffles we're so fluffy that my fork just melted all the way through as I cut them. The whip cream pairing on the side was nice since one can add as you go along. Those strawberries were fresh cut that day. Their is no butter needed on these waffles as it would break that delicious flavor balance. What is more shiny the sparkling pastries that are behind the glass shining back at ya or the smiles from the staff here. Let's easily say both. The warmth is overwhelming as you order since the staff here make the store glow with such light. I frequent Bouchon when ever in need of fabulous individuals that make me smile. The pastries are beyond irresistible. The feeling of the staff is such an incredible plus as they provide such alluring food with fantastic service. I have heard the staff here take a beating from tourists from all over. They smile and keep going. The light in the staff here never stops glowing. What an incredible place to be apart of? No wonder the pastries taste so unbelievably yummy it's all that love that is created among the employees. At least the negative comments that they receive here never take away from anyone's experience. They enhance and provide so much joy every time I visit here! What good here do many ask? Bouchon's pastries are intoxicating with such unavoidable temptation. One should watch out, truly! Once you answer the beckoning call, no other pastry will ever measure up. One of my favorites is their cheese Danish. We can of course, Salut, the French for the dough that took the world by storm because the baker made a mistake . It's all in the butter that baker so long ago forget, and ended up with a light, airy, fluffy crust that we long for so much today. The Europeans love their danish cloud and fluffy which is always full of flavor. The lighter the dough the better the taste anyways. Bouchon has not forgotten their French roots and deliver that delicious airy design pattern of making pastries that never quits. Their cheese Danish has a delicate, lightly sweetened inner core and the outer shell is breakable and cloud like. Put it together and it's a soft delightful masterpiece of exquisite expression. The primary pastries offered here practically never change, such as cheese Danish, croissant, macaroons, cinnamon rolls, donuts, and other traditional offerings. On a good week Bouchon offers Beignets that are a masterpiece of delicious happiness all in a single hole. When you can find them. The Beignets that are made here do not last very long. Truly they sell out incredibly fast. If you are ever up early with a raspberry craving now you know where to satisfy that satiating hunger. The little Beignets devils are so tempting that sin never tasted so soulful. The Beignets are filled with raspberry rouge cream that as you bite into that hole your senses tingle and twinkle a little. Sensational truly. The Beignets are sold in doubles, twice the fun. These little cinnamon and sugar coated beauties are $3.5 ! Such perfection at a cost that will leave some change for the lovely joyful crew serving up your daily love and happiness. Find you right balance. The simplest things are always the best in life. For those that crave that French way of enjoyment with the simplicity of coffee and Beignets with a beautiful view look no further. The cappuccino is fantastic here in the morning with substitutes allowed for those of us who enjoy almond milk. The crew is always in a wonderful mood provides smiles for free with the incredible deliciousness cut with a fork!

Woke up feeling like death and wandered downstairs for any form of sustenance. The first thing that I see...Bouchon Bakery. Ordered a Ham and Cheese Panini, Pistacho Macaron, Strawberry Croissant and a Coffee. Macaron was pretty expensive, but considering the size, it's actually pretty worth it. Nonetheless, one of the best macarons that I've had. Panini, was meh. + for location.

Page's is a Pittsburgh staple. Best soft-serve ice cream out there. I especially love their blueberry soft-serve and pumpkin soft-serve in the fall. The cash-only aspect is a bit inconvenient, but it's worth a stop at the ATM

This is not Starbucks! Perhaps they will make that change some day and then everyone will be able to enjoy a nice afternoon coffee/tea with pastry!

Yum...super delicious ice cream in the Roosevelt neighborhood! Quaint shop serving up many different flavors - we tried the pineapple and peanut butter and many of the others looked great too. We'll be back!
This place has best homemade ice cream. If your ever in the Cleveland area, I would recommend coming here. There are so many choices of ice cream. You can try samples if need be.

It's no longer right by the main entrance but it's the same great Babcock Dairy ice cream! Lots of daily flavors to choose from, I had vanilla with a rhubarb swirl. I think there's an ordering process that I failed to see until seeing some pics on Yelp: 1. Dish/cone, 2. Size, 3. Flavor It's a University of Wisconsin tradition, and it's the best, Jerry, the best!

Great service. There was no line. My husband and I tried the cannolis. I have nothing to compare them to, as this was my first one, but it was good.
This place is so cool! Went there w my siblings on a late night adventure and their treats were delicious! I got the donut ice cream sandwich and my siblings got regular cones. 10/10!

My favorite place to stop by whenever I'm at the linq! I order a scoop of chocolate ice cream with dark chocolate fudge & it always hits the spot especially on hot days. Staff was friendly, service was quick & ice cream was delicious!

First off, 85* is not a bad bakery. Some of their pastry items are good like the egg tart and milk breads. I also love their Black Tea with Sea Salt Cream and my husband loves their Thai Tea. That being said, the service here is absolutely horrendous. Talk about under staff and SLOW workers. I get it, 85* is popular and Vegas has been anticipating its grand opening for a while now. I'm not surprised that it's constantly crowded but it seems like everytime I come here they're always backed up and out of pastries. The cashiers do multiple tasks instead of just checking customers out. This makes the whole payment process inefficient because it takes up too much time. They not only have to count the pastries and input it into the system, but they assemble cardboard carrying boxes and individually place each pastry item into plastic bags before arranging them into the box. This whole process can take up to 5 minutes and that's before they even begin to collect money. I've been to many of the 85* in California and I know this is pretty standard for how they check out, but with the large amount of customers visiting this single location, I just don't think it's a smart use of time. At least assemble the carrying boxes in advance or omit individually packaging the pastries all together to speed up the process. Also, the register girls work so slow. I get that everyone is new, but still, have some sense of urgency for the crowd. It's toture watching the girls take their time in a line that wraps around muitple loops, especially since you've been waiting for over 30 minutes just to check out. The last time we came my husband ate 1 pastry while we waited because he was hungry and the line took so long. We also witnessed a guy literally drop his tray full of pastries onto a nearby counter and left because he didn't want to wait any longer. I wonder if the staff threw the pastries away or if they put it back into the shelves for sale. Either way, that was a loss of money for the business. Of course, we told the cashier my husband ate a pastry (the wrapper was still on the tray) but I wonder how many people munched on their items while waiting and don't bother to tell the cashier. With the amount of crowd, it's really easy to go unnoticed. Also, while my husband was waiting in line, I went to the self-order kiosk and got us drinks since it came quicker from a separate counter. The screen advertised Thai Tea that was buy 1 get 1 free from December until early January. I order the Thai Tea but didn't see a prompt for a free drink so I decided to ask the register. She seemed confused at first and then she said "Oh, we don't have that promotion here because we're grand opening." I asked her then why is it advertised on the screen if you don't honor it? Her reply was "We can't take it off the screen. Sorry." I just left it at that. This is not against the girl. She was polite and only doing her job, but if you're going to advertise something and you're a franchise then at least state that it's not valid at this location or something similar to that effect. Otherwise, that's just false advertising and unethical business. If it's not a valid promotion then it should be taken down, otherwise it should still be honored if it's advertised. Either way, I'm not fussing about a free Thai Tea, but I just thought that was strange. It really adds to the whole unprepared, under staffed and poor management of this place. Hopefully, they'll figure things out in the future. Like I said, 85* is not a bad bakery.
Ice cream is always delicious churn has some really good flavors. I always get the iVietnamese Coffee and the German chocolate.

We got these one time as a surprise for a group of friends and breakfast with family which are now basically the same thing, thank you for your fast and friendly service and we really enjoy the food, you are excellent and accomodating.

When I was browsing Instagram stories I came across this Cafe and I knew immediately that I needed to come to Charlotte and try out this place for myself. As a lover of Matcha and everything Matcha, this place definitely hit the spot for me. The Matcha used was barely noticeably bitter, which means that it is "ceremoniously grade Matcha" or "High-Quality Matcha", which is unlike most places in North Carolina. The Cafe is decorated to match the Holiday season so it is definitely a spot to get your instagrammable foodie pictures as well as try out high-quality Matcha desserts! I'd definitely recommend this place to anyone!

My friend and I had been anticipating coming to Villani's for our love of cannolis, and it was everything we expected and more. The cannolis had a light cinnamon flavor and an excellent creaminess. Along with our cannolis, we got four macaroons- mint chocolate, pistachio, birthday cake, and mocha. They are definitely some of the better macaroons I have had in Charlotte. They were a great size, where you can really try many of their creative flavors. I can't wait to go back to try more.

We got the chocolate cake malt. It was an okay drink. It tasted like chocolate with chunks of like a cookie dough/chocolate chip chunks in it. The malt could've also have been more prominent. For 10$ I was expecting something special. I guess the price is just because the place is on the strip. The malt I make at home are much better than what they gave us.I would not go back.

It's a staple of Charlotte and this is the original location. And it's open 24 hours. Being the original, this is the busiest location I've been to and it's for good reasons. From sandwiches to fresh salads to delicate desserts and my favorite coffee, Amelie's delivers on quality food and dessert. My most recent trip was on a Friday night. It was packed. On this trip, we were looking for a tasty treat. Between the two of us, we got a couple of macaroons (chocolate, lavender and lemon), a chocolate cake and a twice-baked almond croissant. Simply heavenly! I'm a sucker for plain chocolate and there's is a more dark chocolate, so it's not over the top sweet. I love the seasonal lavender lemon macaroon. A light flavor with a citrisy kick. I wish I had ordered tea with it. The cake was rich. The layers were light, but that chocolate ganache is to die for. The croissant was okay. It picks up an almost cake like texture, but this was hubby's choice. I highly recommend the chocolate croissant which is my usual go to. If you are ever craving soup or salad, they have excellent choices. This location does get a bit crowded. The line moves fast, though. And shout out to the girls working the dessert case who can help explain everything and share every macaroon flavor. We actually found a quiet table to sit and enjoyed ourselves.

Drool. This place offers up some damn decadent options for ice cream lovers. I went with the S'mores and my wife got the Toffee Banofi, and we couldn't decide which was more delicious. I'll definitely be back here next time we're in the neighborhood. Sharing a sundae is totally doable, they are huge. Not saying you'll want to share, though :)

We lucked out because we were planning to visit their regular location, but their "food truck" was conveniently in the "food court" of the Arizona Centennial Celebration. We were quite excited since we had seen them on TV, but I think perhaps our expectations were a little bit too high. It's good ice cream, but nothing all that spectacular, nothing that I could necessarily go out of my way for. We had the bananas fosters and salted caramel. Just like others have mentioned, it's kinda expensive for what you get.
This isn't your ordinary ice cream shop. Come prepared to try something new. Just go.

This place is the bomb.com. Those Yum-ee Buns will give you life! I am a huge fan of dessert. If I had it my way, I would eat dessert for breakfast, lunch, & dinner. When I stumbled upon this place, I couldn't believe they were serving ice cream in warm donuts (Yum-ee Buns). I mean what genius came up with this? But in all seriousness, this spot is probably one of the best dessert places I have been to in my life. The menu selection is huge & very unique! You can order anything from ice cream, milkshakes, Yum-ee Buns (they are huge!), macaron ice cream sandwiches, cookie dough pops, & so much more. You can even order ice cream with your favorite cereals mixed in! I ordered the Cookie Monster Yum-ee Bun with cookies & cream ice cream, oreos, & Cookie Crisp cereal. My husband ordered the Peanut Butter Galore Yum-ee Bun with chocolate ice cream, peanut butter drizzle, chocolate syrup, & Reese's cups. The Cookie Monster was absolutely delicious! I would highly recommend this if you are unsure of what to order or if it is your first time. The Yum-ee Bun is priced at $5.95 & each additional topping costs 50 cents. It's on the pricer side for dessert, but can easily be split between two people. I wish I would have known that before ordering my very own Yum-ee Bun! Expect a wait. When we arrived, the line was out the door. My husband & I waited about 25 minutes before we got our buns, but it was absolutely worth it. We will definitely be back in the future!

I love Sprinkles. Their cupcakes are consistently delicious, so you never have to worry about them having an off day. I also liked that this location has their new ice cream shop. I haven't tried it yet, but want to soon. They do sundaes with bits of any flavor of cupcake you want folded in, cookie sandwiches, shakes/malts, frozen hot chocolate, even red velvet cones! Um, sold. The selection at night is pretty scarce so try to come earlier in the day if you can. We stopped by after ridding the High Roller (which is next-door) and got two mini cupcakes (lemon and vanilla). Their vanilla is my absolute favorite as is their triple cinnamon, banana, sprinkle, and vegan red velvet. As someone who is not a vegan, that says a lot. There is always fun seasonal flavors too (right now it's caramel apple and pumpkin) and they also make doggy cupcakes which our girls go nuts for. They now have a free rewards program as well with a ton of cool perks such as a complimentary cupcake on your birthday, any free menu item of your choice each time you hit 15 points, access to exclusive events, bogo deals, and skip the line passes. The ice cream line is always longer here than the cupcake one (being a desert and all), so you should be able to get in and out fairly quickly if cupcakes are all you're after.

I saw hopscotch at farmer's market last year and bought lavender honeycomb and baby cake from their stall. I liked the honeycomb but did not like baby cake. Now, after a year, I thought of trying it again as I found it located inside art mart. I bought walnut caramel bar, brownie, champagne baby cake and gooey butter cake. I wanted to try a few before writing a review. My review of each item is as follow: Walnut caramel bar(2/5): it was not overly sweet, which I liked. Had good amount of walnut. But, the overall taste was not that good. Brownie(3/5): again not too sweet, was more on bitter side. Liked the caramel on top. Overall, good. Champagne baby cake(2/5): too sweet, was not moist, felt heavy. Gooey butter cake(1/5): extremely sweet. And that's the only thing I could taste. I couldn't eat it more than one bite.

Delicious ice cream flavors, cute shop. Came in around 6 pm earlier today with my two cousins, tried a few samples then a big group of people came in, so we kinda felt a little pressured to hurry, since there was only one employee working at the time. I hate how small it is inside, wish it was bigger, other than that the employee was super sweet and very nice. good pricing as well
Churn has some of the best ice cream I've ever had! What an amazing, nostalgic and fun spot.

Mason's is a real treat! Delicious, quirky, fun - my favorite ice cream place in Cleveland. Always serving a variety of different and unique flavors - all delicious. Egg waffle adds a certain flair. The fact that it becomes a Ramen shop (also super delicious - I recommend) in the winter an added bonus! Love coming here!

It is a quick walk from the downtown area and pretty easy to find as there is a nice large sign outside. They have a great selection of unique donuts and the staff are extremely friendly. We were super excited to try the French toast and grilled cheese donuts. They both were exceptional, but you do need to eat them while they are still hot. With that said you do need to get there early because they do sell out of things. But after trying their food today I can easily see why they constantly sell out. If you are in the downtown area it is a great place to get your donut fix!
I can't even emphasize how this is the best ice cream I've had. I've been having it since I was a kid, the taste of blue cosmo and pistachio brings me back to innocent times.

Overall: great variety, fluffy donuts, great atmosphere This place is right by the smoothie place we went to for breakfast, so we decided to stop here for a treat after. They have a great variety of donuts and unique flavors like creme brulee. We got the blueberry lemon cake donut and the creme brulee donut. The creme brulee donut had a bruleed sugar top and a vanilla pastry cream filling. It was amazing! The donut was a perfect fluffy texture, and the filing was very creamy, and the bruleed sugar had a nice crunch. The blueberry lemon donut was great as well. I find that sometimes cake donuts can be dense, but this one was perfectly fluffy and had the perfect amount of icing on the top, so it was not overly sweet and sugary. To top it off, their bathroom has the cutest murals of Homer Simpson and his pink sprinkle donut!

Food: only tried the dessert items: assortment of cookies and crack pie. Have made several of the cookies from the cookbook. Not impressed. All of this might be better if if was freshly baked. Like my own versions better. Service: it was a walk up counter. Atmospher: it was a walk up counter. Visited on 2.24.18
Always great. Appreciate this place for their high quality and delicious combinations.
Cookie Monster and the Madagascar Vanilla are the real deal

One of my favorite Netflix original series is Chef's Table. When they showed an episode featuring Christina Tosi I was hooked even though I'm not a cereal guy. Just had to bide my time for the opportunity to be in Vegas and head out to the Cosmopolitan, 2nd floor next to Momofuku, another one I had to get too. The line can get long here but it goes down quickly. The menu board could get intimidating offering cookies including gluten and sugar free, cakes by the slice or whole, crack pie, breads, milksquakes and milkshakes, soft serve and fancy drinks. It took us a long time to decide what to get but we finally made our choices. Staff is super friendly and knowledgeable. They will give you a little more information to assist your decision making. To start, we had cereal milk soft serve with flakes and another one with fudge. The soft serve tasted exactly how I remembered eating my Kellogg's Frosted Flakes getting to the bottom of the sugary milk. Ah those memories. This is just the first trip here. And I can't wait to come back to try more.
The butter pecan and salted caramel topping is incredible. Gotta check this place out when in town.

NOT ice cream! Gelato and sorbet. Boba tea drinks. Coffee drinks. The positives: best strawberry cheesecake gelato I have ever had. Not too sweet with the right amount of fresh strawberries and a touch of cheesecake. All my kids enjoyed their flavors and toppings. Service was fine. Cons: kids size scoop is measly for $3.29. Each topping is $1 and literally a mere sprinkle of a spoon which amounts to about 5 cents. We eat a lot of good ice cream gelato and sorbet in the Phoenix metro area. The prices here are exorbitant and the portions are small. If the atmosphere was nice or the store was located in an upscale place I could justify the costs--sort of. It's not a family friendly place so I won't be returning with my kids. Too out of the way, too expensive, and not enough ice cream per serving.
Love the crepes. Really surprised me. Strawberry flavor is better than mango. Also tried durian ice cream that was just ok

When I was at the Vegas Venetian, the sales clerk told me that if I bought 5 large macarons, I would receive a set of (5?) mini macarons. Great, I thought...I was going to get some for family so I bought 15 large ones, expecting 3 sets of mini-macs. When I got back to my hotel room in another hotel down the strip, I realized the sales clerk gave me NO mini-macarons...NONE. I was going to catch a plane in about 1.5 hours, and to walk back there might have been pretty tight. I called over and left a voicemail. I expected them to at least call me back, but I never heard a word. Boy, was I sorely disappointed at the customer service. I love Bouchon NYC, and like LA very much. I was a big fan of Bouchon. But after this experience, I am pretty "meh" now on the brand...no matter how much I liked their macarons. Sigh. Really disappointed.

Overblown, hyped up spot. I can't believe people were standing in line for a half-hour to get into this place. This is another example of how much people can lose their minds at the prospect of getting anywhere remotely close to a TV personality. (Carlo wasn't there, by the way.) We came early in the day before the hungover tourists came to crowd the place up. If I'd have waited in line to get in here I would've kicked myself later. It's not that the baked goods here are terrible, they're simply average. My wife and I got some cookies here and honestly, they're no different than anything that you would get in any baked goods section at Wal-Mart. Hype, hype, HYPE! Save your money and buy some cookies at Walgreens. There are plenty of them around the Strip.

This place is just nasty. The employees here can be so rude. They use disgusting ingredients on top of it too like high fructose corn syrup- ish! I ordered a sandwich and it was put in wrong. It took me almost a half hour to get it sorted out only to be met by a sarcastic cashier tell me, "we are REALLY busy" when he was the one who screwed my order up in the first place. They took my sandwich back in the kitchen, put an egg on it and brought it back to me. I had ordered a bacon, egg, cheese croissant and was given a BLT, they put an egg on the BLT, lettuce and all and slopped it back in a to go bag. No thanks. Will NEVER eat here again. My first experience here was ordering a birthday cake that literally had two inches of butter cream in between two tiny slivers of cakes. Literally everyone at the party threw it out. I emailed to complain and wasn't even offered a refund! Thought I'd given them another shot- nope. Still nasty.

Just came across this place randomly and really glad I did, this place has some of the best hidden Ice cream in Las Vegas, a must go if you are out by the area. I will be coming back and the prices are really reasonable

Vegas's infamous Ice Cream parlour located in The Venetian is straight out of a fantasy world or the Wonderland. The dÃ©cor is super cute with pink walls, twinkling chandeliers, moving trains and magical glass bathrooms.They also have two little adorable pets. They looked unreal first but, when we saw them closely, they were actually breathing lol. We checked out this place after dinner, but didn't have the room for an ice cream. So, i settled with their Dark Hot Chocolate. It was perfect for the ones whose palate requires low level of sweetness. Great service from all the staff and the best butter pecan ice cream I've ever had!!!

Having unfortunately moved away from the Valley a few years ago, my first and only experience at SR was last week. OMFG I am in love! My girlfriend took me here literally first thing after picking me up from Sky Harbor. Hell, they weren't even open yet, but the lovely lady (my friend said one of the owners?) let us in and served us right away anyways. I had (don't laugh) the basil lime sorbet, pineapple sorbet, watermelon sorbet, and the mango margarita (I think that's the name). SOOOOOO good, with the added benefit I can pretend it was a healthy "lunch" since they are fruit sorbets, not ice cream. Side Note: (For anyone who's been to, and raved about Jeni's in Columbus, OH, you have NOT yet tasted amazing sorbet)
I mean where else can you get a jar of cookie dough with icing?! So many good treats! They also have GF cookie dough!
Came down for the "soft" opening, great desert, good vibes atmosphere fits the name! Creative flavours and great people, will be back next time im in the downtown area :)
I wish you guys were closer. I miss your blood orange doughnut.

This place is so cute! French themed and they take many safe precautions so I felt good walking in here. My friend and I got basically a baked goodie box, we got the Smores and Pecan Macaroons, the salted caramel brownie (THE STAR) 2 different almond flour cakes (apple & smore again i think) and the pumpkin cheesecake. All of them met both of our different taste needs. I dont typically like macaroons but the ones here were not too sweet so I enjoyed it. Hands down, the STAR of the box was the salted caramel brownie! The bakery highly recommended it and they were right to!

Great ice cream, great donuts. They give you the option to add toppings into your ice cream. Staff is very informative and let you try as many flavors you want. Location is kinda hidden in a cool lot with a few other small businesses.

A very addictive place to have ice cream. The "Toffee Banofi" is better than any thing I have eaten in Arizona. I sampled the Bleau Cheese ice cream & thought I found heaven. I also purchased some "Bacon Brittle".The bacon is something that needs to tried out & stored in packages for disaster prepareness. Forget about the essentials, You need the Bcaon Brittle.
Disappointed these donuts have no taste what's so ever They are only Big ,good looking and over priced Have tasted better.

What the huh? I got all kinds of excited to see the cake boss bakery. Didn't know it was there. Walked in and I saw the line and I thought this must be some good shit. Plus my wife said his shop on the tv has a line a mile long so I waited and I waited and did I mention I waited. Had no idea what they served because I just jumped in line. Then I thought what if I don't want anything but I stood in line for 45 minutes. I'll be damned if I don't get something. I ended up getting one caramel cupcake, 1 yellow with chocolate icing cupcake and a half a pound of cookies dipped in chocolate. So my wife can't have them because of her peanut and tree nut allergy I gave them a big bite(I didn't eat them all in one setting). The cupcakes were Meh! Not much flavor. The icing was good but wasn't what I expected. Guess I was thinking it would be rich but wasn't. The cookies were better but I wouldn't stand in line like I did for them. Pretty pricey too but it's vegas.

Excited that they opened a Ghirardelli store back in Vegas again. Came here on the weekend for 1 mission and that was to get their 50 pc ct of dark peppermint bark. I was a bit bummed that they didn't have the sale price like the online store did but oh well. I definitely want to come back and try their dessert. As for the location, it really sucks if you park at The Quad or Flamingo. Next time I come back, I would probably park at Mirage or Caesars palace and walk across. Saves you from spending more than half an hour trying to find a space like I did.

Stopped by the new 36th Street location and it's really nice! The concept is the same as the original Amelie's, but a few more designs. The Eiffel Tower replica is a hit! There are macaroons and other dessert designs on the ceiling and it's really nice! Plenty of seating areas inside and a few tables outside. Great place to grab some really good food, desserts and coffee/tea! Give the new location a try!
I loved the location and the ambiance!!!! Service can definitely be improved!

God, I love this ice cream. The flavors aren't like,, wild, but they're quality. They have depth, they've got dimension. Mitchell's has been a staple in my life in Cleveland for like 6 years and anyone who visits Cleveland HAS to stop by Mitchell's. Even their super simple flavors like cookie dough are amazing. In fact, that's my favorite. BUT if you like chocolate and fruit flavors, the bing cherry chocolate chunk is stellar

Definitely one of my favorite spots in Cleveland. I pass by Presti's almost everyday and it's so hard to not go in and get something. Presti's is a bustling bakery in the heart of Little Italy that offers a wide variety of pastries, desserts, bread, coffee, gelato, as well as hot food (mainly Italian). There's ample indoor and outdoor seating, making it a great place to hang-out or study. Unless there's no line there, make sure to first take a number by the door and wait until it's called. Then someone from behind the counter will take your order. It can get pretty busy so I would avoid coming in during the lunch rush if possible. Now onto the food. The pastries and desserts are BOMB and definitely their best . My favorites are the tiramisu (perhaps one of best I've had), chocolate mousse cake, and the cannolis. I'm warning you now: it's going to be hard not to overindulge. They also make a darn good mocha (my gf thinks it's the best she's ever had) and have a selection of hot food, such as pastas, sandwiches, and pizza slices, that hit the spot. Also, sometimes they provide you utensils but sometimes you have to get it yourself from the concession stand so make sure to double check. The prices are on the more expensive side but I think it's worth it for how good the pastries and food are! Overall, Presti's is an established and reputable place that has never disappointed. It'll always be worth stopping by and picking up some tasty treats from here!

I'm going to start this review with a bold statement. THE BEST DONUTS IN VEGAS. Seriously, the best. Ever. After moving here, I felt like I would never find another good donut again but then I stumbled upon Donut Bar and all my donut dreams have come true. Donut bar just doesn't serve regular plain donuts-- you know those shops that only have cake donuts but they all have different colored frosting. meh. No, this place is the Willy Wonka factory of donuts! Some of my creative favorites are the creme brulee, homer's donut, butterbeer and the big poppa (poptart). Big giant donuts that are completely shareable with some friends, unless you are on that donut diet like I am. If you see a crazy long line, don't leave! The line moves quickly and the customer service is on point. I strategically plan my visit during their happy hour, when they are about to close. You can fill a box for $10 and get all the donuts. Parking can be stressful since it is mostly street parking. Get ready to parallel. But no worries, a cup of their nitro cold brew will make all of your parking troubles go away.

Stopped at Milk Bar after dinner at Momofuku. The line was long but it moved quickly. There were a lot of menu choices and opted for crack pie and a latte. The crack pie was memorable and tasty. I'll definitely stop by next time at the Cosmopolitan.
i did not like this place at all the food was okay but i can make better stuff at my house . The staff was very rude and the bathroom was dirty and had no towels

The ice cream was good. The two stars are for the cranky employee who served us. First, he wouldn't give me a sample of their Ice cream flavors, I wanted to try the Carmel Apple. He said it was due to the the long line (line was only 5 people deep after us with 3 windows open), but then he said, "Just one sample". When he returned with the one sample, I was there with 2 other people that were too scared to even ask for a sample, because the employee was so snappy. Secondly, when we ordered, one of my people said, she wanted the salted Carmel Ice Cream in a cone. The employee said the ice cream is somewhat melted and suggested a cup. We asked for a sugar cone on top of the cup so she could crunch the sugar cone into the ice cream. We did that also with the Carmel Apple and the cookie dough ice creams. Finally, to my surprise, the employee charged me for the sugar cones! .25 each, not nice to charge you on the back end of 2 buck Tuesday (where the single scoop is two bucks) deal. There goes your tip, Mr. Cranky employee!! Also, remember, Mr. Cranky, you were the one that said the ice cream was melty and suggested a cup. So, I guess two buck Tues is not really two bucks, if people are charged for the sugar cone. On the other hand, their ice cream was good, creamy and actually had good apple flavor and ribbons of carmel. If you do go, just be warned the sugar cones are .25 more if you get your ice cream in a cup.

Great desserts.. love the atmosphere! Bet ya didn't know everything in this amazing french bakery was recycled or found at goodwill? It's awesome eclectic mix makes for a living room like environment. Love that it's 24 hours too.

This place is really good! It took me awhile to find but i did find the place. The parking lot is much to be desiered. The place is small but decent. They were extremely friendly and helpfull in letting me make a choice on what i wanted. I ended up getting cookies and cream, with a red velvet macaron and a toasted marshmellow. Yum! Ive never had a macaron before so this was my first time and i loved it! The toasted marshmellow was to die for.. the outter shell it made and breaking it open to find the gooey fluff just ooze out. Ugh, perfection! I could have had 4 of those on my ice cream and i would have been good to go. I will say they are a bit expensive. Mine came out to $8 which, the ice cream was good, but i dont think its good enough for $8.. Its worth a shot and make sure you use your check in offer!

Yum yum! I loved the feel of the store and the flavors are unique and fun. Reason for four instead of five stars are the kids cones were fairly small for $4.25. This is definitely a spot for a special treat.

Absolutely loved this place. Yummy pastries, and a really cool space to just chill in (saw a couple people just sitting around playing board games, sipping on coffee and eating pastries). It's easy to see why it's so popular, and at least the line moved quickly when we were there. By far my favorite was the salted caramel brownie!!

We stopped in after lunch last week looking for something sweet. I tried the homemade black raspberry ice cream based on the staff's recommendation and it was quite tasty. Excited to come back and try the peach ice cream this summer. The portions are huge and the prices are reasonable - you could do some serious damage if you ordered their banana splits or other super large items.

I can't believe I didn't see Jenny L's review before I went! $12 bakery basket?!?! Sigh! (BTW...You probably already know this but I heard from Darlene K that they opened one in LA...I looked it up and it is in Beverly Hills to be exact! Let's go next time you're up in town!!!) I LOVED the macarons. They reminded me of the ones from Laduree - Paris... I think these come closer than even Boule's! They were perfectly chewy and moist on the inside with a delicate shell...bursting with flavor. I tried the lemon & coffee(?). I bought a box for a friend and she let me try the strawberry. (Very tasty although a few days later, they did dry out. The trick, I learned from her, is to put them in the freezer!). The red velvet cupcake was a disappointment...too dry. Although I did like the filling in the middle which is like Black Bottom cupcakes. I also got the TKOs which were adorably shaped like snowmen for the holidays. They were so rich and chocolatey that you can only handle a single bite for a few hours until your taste buds settle down. However, if I were to go back, I'd stick to the macarons. And maybe this bakery basket Jenny L. speaks of... : )

I've been to Sloans at the Village by Topanga Mall. I Love their triple chocolate chunk cookies! I went to try their other location at the Venetian. Located on the second floor near the bridge infront of the Canaletto restaurant. This one is a bit smaller but it did not lack any goodies! The window presentation was so inviting. Their large donuts and chocolate covered apples looked so yummy!! I had to buy 2 triple chocolate chunk cookies and a few other goodies. It was as amazing as I remembered! One of my favorites cookies, a definite must, specially if you have a sweet tooth. They had such fun toys, adorable purses, amazing selection of candies and they even have dog treats! The cashier was friendly as well. I will be back!!

The best donuts in Cleveland. My family has been going here for 20+ years and the donuts are as good now as they always been. Personal favorites are the cake Donut with chocolate frosting and white topping and the Cinnamon Twists. Seriously awesome donuts!!

The outside sign and hanging signs inside weren't the most inviting, BUT, I got the captain crunch ice cream and wow, no regrets. It looked like vanilla with rare rainbow spots, but it definitely tasted like captain crunch. A small size was the perfect serving size.

Good ice cream, a lil' bit different with some spicy kick to if if you want to try something new. Good fluff cottony softness, decent flavor. But if I judge by the classic staple flavors it really doesn't compare to other homemade ice cream places I've been. Still really good, not great.

Such a fun little shop! The candy/decor on the walls makes it feel so fun inside. The staff was super friendly and the flavor selections were pretty good. The line was running out the door, but the staff working kept a positive attitude and got through the line very well, while still chatting with everyone. I had the milk and cookies flavor and it was to die for! It truly tasted like milk and cookies and was definitely some of the best ice cream I've ever had. Definitely worth stopping in (and waiting in line!).

This place is an absolute joke. In the matter of 3 minutes they lost 8 customers due to the embarrassing amount of donuts, or lack there of, in the cases. Why do you stay open all day when you have 3 donuts to offer customers? I'm no business person, but it doesn't take much intelligence to know that you're actually wasting money trying to pawn off the few stale donuts left from the morning while you are paying employees. I will never return. Yuck.
Great Customer Service! Ice cream is on point and they have some awesome seasonal flavors. Staff is super sweet

One of the Coolest French Bakery, and Coffee Shops in the Southeast. Nobody comes even close to the amount and variety of fresh breads, pastries, and cookies. There are several rooms for seating. Each room is very different and eclectic. If you are in the area, don't miss it.

Ok, I may be the only person who does not get the whole cupcake craze. I thought the cupcakes were ok, nothing special. We had to wait in a line outside, which was weird but I understood why they were doing it. The thing is there was no communication with the line being for the ice cream part of the store. If you just wanted cupcakes, you could just go into the other side of the store. They staff may want to let people know that. There was noone in line for the cupcakes. It was a little overwhelming when 2 to 3 gals asking what you wanted or if ive been helped. I think the customer service was great but still a bit much. I got 4 mini cupcakes, my friends got something with ice cream. Again, nothing really special. I dont think I would come back, just because I dont like cupcakes.
If you are in the Phoenix area, this place is a must try! Quirky little combo of ice cream, macaroons and toasted marshmallows make a fun treat. We always stop in when we visit the area!

Literally the best place in Pittsburgh to get ice cream. They have something for everyone, including multiple soft serve flavors, sundaes, banana splits, cookie sundaes ft. Nancy B's cookies, scooter crunch topping, shakes, and so much more! Be prepared to wait in line. It moves quickly, but there is normally a wait. FYI- this place is cash only (I'm almost positive), so bring some cash with you. I honestly can't sing Page's praises enough... if you've never been... make sure you stop here this summer!

My husband ordered a sundae...easy right? HA! He said worst sundae he has ever had & I tried it an agree. The ice cream was tasteless & the hot fudge congealed to the ice cream and was almost solid in texture not hot & creamy. At the prices at this place they should be embarrassed.

Hands down the best ice cream I've had in Madison, WI. The best is yet to crumb especially was heavenly. Not sure where the idea of carmelized bread crumbs came from but they were a delicious touch to the vanilla flecked jam packed ice cream. The waffle bits have a delectable crunch and I will definitely be back to try more flavors in the cute setting.

Wow! That is what both my wife and I said when we walked into the Donut Bar! We viewed some of the most interesting donuts and pastries we have ever seen! We wanted to buy one of everything! We found ourselves drooling at these beautiful creations because we had arrived early for brunch next door at Carson's Kitchen and they weren't open yet. Sometimes it pays to be early! The two ladies behind the counter were very nice and helpful with suggestions. We have discovered that the cinnamon rolls are a must at the Donut Bar! The salted caramel donut was very good as was the creme brulee. We are looking forward to coming back to try the Oreo Donut and a delicious-looking creation with fresh strawberries on it!
Thank u for existing Very good spot Believe they have more chains of this But this is my favorite that I've been to for sure .

Omg this place, it's everything glittery delicious and wonderful. You need to go, even if you're not into dessert, just for the experience. The entire place is perfectly themed, and there's an outrageous thing called "everything and the kitchen sink" (forgive me if I mis-quoted the name) that is literally served in a sink. Plus the amount of flavors and variety of dessert options go on for days!
Sampled the Captain Crunch ice-cream and all I can say is YUM! Very rich and dense, and oh-so-yummy! Took an oatmeal cookie to go. Didn't care for it much. Wanted to try the cupcakes... next time!

I am a sucker for bakery goods and was excited to try this bakery in Vegas. It's a little pricey but not above what you would expect from Vegas. I bought 3 macarons (Large vanilla, small chocolate, small pumpkin) a latte, and a ghost shaped chocolate sandwich cookie for my son. I didn't care for the pumpkin macaron, but the other 2 were soooo delicious. The latte was perfect and the ghost cookie was surprisingly yummy and not too sweet. The staff seemed a little distracted and the guy said he needed to "go upstairs" to get the box for my macarons, which seemed to take forever. I don't understand why the boxes aren't kept in the bakery but that's the only issue I had with this place.
The line was a little long, but the pastries were good. It is a little pricey but it is Vegas! Great place to visit, but would love to go to the original.

I did not believe my eyes when I saw these cupcakes arrive!! They were about 48 cupcakes per box and the variety was perfect! I didn't even k ow they delivered! Their cupcakes are delicious! I loved the salted caramel and the red velvet is not to be ignored either! They are super rich and didn't finish the frosting - but are perfect for birthdays!

This little kiosk exists right at the entrance to the Phantom theater. They offer paninis and muffins and other assorted treats, but the reason to stop is the macaroons. There are several flavors including chocolate, raspberry, and pistachio. If you buy five you get the sixth free, and you can pick your own flavors you do not have to get the pre-made sampler packs. The coffee brewed here is drinkable, so if you need an energy boost the have ice cold Red Bull, and even champagne splits which go quite nicely together. Only in Vegas can you enjoy a classic French macaroon while sipping champagne and Red Bull and not be the oddest character in sight.

I stumbled upon Bouchon Bakery by accident and have no regrets for trying it out. In order to find Bouchon, you pass Carlo's Bakery inside the Venetian, head to the nearest doors that lead outside, and once you're outside, you make a left turn to Bouchon Bakery. I ordered the chocolate almond croissant and a cheese danish, both priced at $4 each. The croissant was flaky on the outside and moist on the inside, and the cheese topping on the danish had the perfect texture and sweetness.

Walking on the Strip as I was passing by the Venetian hotel, I spot Bouchon Bakery. I walk in and ask if they have Kouign Amann- a puff pastry creation- there is one left! Wow today I'm having a streak of good luck!! There's a cute little patio area to enjoy your coffee and pastry. Delicious!

I liked the cherry ice cream, but the service and the price are not the greatest. Was given an extremely small one scoop of ice cream, and I had to joke if this was a kid's cup they were providing me. The employee returned with supposedly more, but to be honest it was still meager. For that price, I'm ok with sticking to my Sweet Republic for my gourmet ice cream needs. Better service, better location, better seating.

Nice staff at the counter, large selection of drinks and yummy looking goodies, cute ambiance... The greatest downfall and why I'll never return? Got three quarters of the way done with my pastry (salted brownie) which was great until I took one of the last few remaining bites and proceeded to pull a long dark hair from my mouth... YUP I found a hair in my food. My hair is blonde and short. 'Twas not mine. I was mortified. Sorta wanted to puke. My first and last visit. Though I'm sure it hasn't happened that much before....

Best ice cream I've ever eaten. Two, large scoops of honey pecan (called butter pecan at most ice cream stores) at Honey Hut costs $3.00 ($2.25 for one scoop) which is not only a terrific bargain but the absolute best product offered in the area (taking Mitchell's Ice Cream into consideration), as on the honey pecan, Honey Hut beats Mitchell's, both on quality and price). Go to Honey Hut this summer!

I must first say I'm ashamed I've lived in this area for like 6 years and I've never stopped here . Wow what a nice surprise I haven't been this excited over donuts in years. Wow the selection is great they have any flavor combination you can think of. I was astonished when I tasted the donuts nice buttery, tasty, mouth watering goodness . I see why they have been in business as long as they have. The price was a little more then competitors but very well worth it. Kudos Jack Frost!!!!!!
Great service and great ice cream. The staff explained the process and were very passionate about the ice crean they create. Definitely coming back.

I went for the salted caramel brownie. It was very good. The brownie was soft and creamy with a thick layer of salted caramel. Melted in my mouth. I also tried an apricot pastry. There wasn't much apricot in it though it was flakey. A cute place with tables inside and out.

We happened upon this place by chance and it was probably the best luck I've had all week. This place is UNREAL. The ice cream itself is standalone (honey lavender, tangerine, etc), but paired with their famous "dough melt" (a donut ice cream sandwich) made it even better. And toppings were cereals like cookie crisp, lucky charms marshmallows, Reese's puffs... Plus it's in a really cool area of Phoenix! The little plaza it's in is the cutest place. If you're in the area you HAVE to go. It's so worth it.
Great selection of donuts, if you can think it they got it. You have get there early tho, some donuts tend to run out in the first hour or so! Yeah there are that good!!

This place is an absolute must when visiting NC! The decor is so amazing and so unique. Staff members are kind and welcoming. The macarons were perfect and so tasty. $2+ for a macaron was a bit much but I will say that it was worth it. The Noda location is pretty big but it was busy during the Saturday lunch hour, leaving very little sitting areas. AmÃ©lie's is the perfect place for a cute bridal shower, perfect place for studying, & perfect for a little dessert any time of the day!

Yum X 1,000! Had to come here for dessert & coffee after a dinner. I've never had an espresso so now was the time! I had a delicious vanilla cone with salted caramel and a shot of espresso. Loved the outdoor atmosphere. Amazing music & calm people.
The employees were the sweetest people! And the shakes were bomb asf 10/10 recommend.
Had the coffee n it was smooth n delicious Best coffee I've ever had. Will pick up bakery items tomorrow

Great little spot to stop for ice cream! They have a special that is a scoop of ice cream, a macaroon, and a jumbo marshmallow on top. They let us sample a few flavors before we decided which was great! We will definitely be back!

Great breakfast! Got a butter croissant and a chocolate croissant for my boyfriend. Both were flaky and soft. The beignets were AMAZING. We split a chocolate and a berry, and both were great. Fluffy, fresh, taaaasty. The chocolate was quite heavy, so maybe better as an afternoon snack than a breakfast, but great with a cup of coffee. I wanted to go back the next day and try the bread pudding, but didn't make it. I will definitelly be trying the Napa one next time I am there since it's closer to me than Vegas.

Love this place! Way more than a bakery, although their baked goods are delicious and baked on site every day! Things we've enjoyed include sheet pizza by the slice (try the artichoke pizza), stromboli and antipasto salad. We come here twice a year when we come to Cleveland to visit my husband's family.
I can only speak on the birthday cake but I'd make sweet, sweet love to that thing. Actually, I'd let it make love to me if it so desired.

Most think of Amelie's for the bakery but these salads were amazing!!!!!!! It was only $2 more to add on Salmon or Portobello mushrooms. They were very fresh. I got a champagne vinaigrette dressing which was flavorful. We also got to sit outside and eat. I love this place for meetings or just to come work for a couple hours.

Absolutely fantastic. Even if everything behind the glass does not appeal to you, it is all done with care and professionalism. Susan Detering is not only highly qualified in technique across different regions of the country, pressure systems, how they affect dough, what types of dough need more or less kneading, etc...but she is a genuinely nice person who is heavily invested in her community and product. I had the ham and gruyere croissant and bought a pain au chocolate for later. Great quality and flavor. Do yourself a favor and go early while everything is warm!
This is by far my favorite place in Las Vegas!!! Ya wish they had one closer to Texas so I could come more often. Highly recommend if you want something sweet and at a good price!

Summer in Madison is not complete without getting ice cream here and eating it on the terrace. My favorite is the Mocha Macchiato and my kids like the Cotton Candy and Blue Ammon flavors. The line can get long at times, but the ice cream is definitely worth the wait.

This place is busy!!! We didn't get a chance to try the lobster tail at the restaurant, so we saw some more being sold at the bakery across the hallway (why they wouldn't deliver more to the restaurant is beyond me?), so we got in the looong line. The wait was about 30min and there is a guy with an ipad taking orders way head of you seeing all the pastry cases, which is super annoying. I know they are doing this for speedier service, but I had no chance looking to see what is down the line, so I simply ordered the lobster tail and that was it. He was pretty pushy too, so I missed out on some other things that looked good when I later came all the way down to pay. If you are interested in buying things, walk along the side and check out the display cases first and then go in line or let your hubby wait in line while you check out what they have.

Highly recommend the ice cream sandwich! It is homemade creamy ice cream squished between two freshly baked cookies, which are selected by your choosing. It creates a cannot be missed texture and flavor combo!! Please try!!

Stopped in after a bad dinner. Service: quick, friendly, efficient. Excellent over all Flavors: great selection, creative and not too sweet Texture ( amount of air in ice cream and creaminess): excellent Price: Fair

This was my second visit. Had the traditional taho. Brought me back to my childhood. Also, it was perfect for a rainy day. They also have excellent halo-halo. They do their own ice cream and the selection is great. They've only been open since August. Hope they'll be around for a while.

Had a ice cream sandwich. Snicker doodle with cap'n crunch. I liked the overall feel of the place they had a cupcake ATM which I thought was adorable. I heard the cupcakes were good going to have to try them on my next time round. Overall pretty impressed with the quality of the ice cream and the flavor variety definitely a spot I would check out again.

Get here early if you have a specific donut you want. We got here around 10:30 and they were down to one vegan kind left and only a handful of regular flavors. We got the salted caramel and cake batter. You can't go wrong!

Closed more than 45 minutes before 9pm. Said the woman packing away unsold pastries and macaroons, "We just decided to close early." Annoying after planning our last night on the strip around a stop for sweets.
The custard here is amazing. I reside in Chicago, and I'm really contemplating if I should make the drive down to Urbana just for another scoop/dip. It's worth every calorie.

Another 5 star review for world class service and world renowned ice cream. It is SO. GOOD. and with a donut? Ugh amazing. I wish I took a picture first to post on here but I'm sad to admit the second it goes in my hand it's gone so quick. This place is a GEM.

I cannot put in words how excited I was to find out that 85'C was opening in my city. I checked frequently and even had people notify me when it was officially opened. I would have wanted to attend the grand opening but was able to get in soon after. It was a bit hectic everyone wanted to be there. But overall managed to get almost everything I wanted excited milk pudding (which is a swirl bread with vanilla custard inside) and I usually get multiples of those to go. Service was efficient despite how busy it was and I look forward to going back. I'm glad now that a trip to 85'C doesn't involve trekking all the way to LA. The bread side is a little smaller than what I remember but would love to see more options as the bakery continues to grow. I have high hopes as 85'C rarely disappoints

Pretty much what we expected to be. But the desserts were amazing we got so many I don't even remember all of them. You must try a chocolate covered strawberry and a mini cheesecake. They are definitely what it's all cracked up to be.
Just okay. We had some kind of cereal ice cream. Humphry slocomb is better!
Went for cannoli and sfogliatelle. Also picked up some pizza. Good stuff. I couldn't wait for the next feast. I dont often come this part of town.
Employees are not wearing a mask. This should not be optional. Ice cream was great as always. Service was average at best.

Well, we stayed in line for 1 hour and 10 minutes... was it worth it... hmmmm.... I would say yes... but, if you truly have some time to kill in Vegas... or really need to stay in one place not to make a full of yourself walking drunk all over the Vegas strip. Definitely delicious! The famous "Lobster Tail" pastry is worth the wait. But if you are going to stay that long in that line, load up on them! Other items on the menu are just like in many other bakeries... but with better presentation. To help you stay sane while standing in line, you have a chance to see how a professional cake decorator puts together some of the cakes that you see on the shelves as you enter the bakery. Quite fun... even if you are an adult.. even more fun if you have already had a few (or a dozen) cocktails before getting to the bakery... (just make sure you are not drooling all over the window)...

My mind was blown today when I tried these delicious donuts. I came in near closing time so there was only three options: coconut, blueberry,and poptart. We went with the giant coconut and split it between 3 people. It was incredible! By far one of the best donuts I have even had in my life! The customer service was pretty friendly for a hipster place and the service was fast. I also tried the Americano coffee and it was EXCELLENT!!! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND this place and I will be sending my hotel guests to this amazing place.

We were downtown today and had pizza at Pizzeria Bianco for #MickeyFriendsgiving. Looked up ice cream and couldn't ignore the reviews on this place. Definitely an accurate account! Great service explaining the options and going over the choices with our kids. Socially distant markers were in use and great safe experience. Ice cream was amazing. Finding a place that al five of us are satisfied is tough to do these days but this one crushes it. We opted for the chocolate, strawberry, doughnut sandwich and cherry cobbler. All amazing and would recommend it to anyone. Worth traveling into the city for!

We all scream for ice cream! This place is on point if you want some quality ice cream! I recommend the banana split! Also, the banana cream pie oh my! So many options to choose from. This place can get very busy so beware of that. Also, this place in similar to sonic in the sense of you don't go inside. One bad thing about this place is that there is no order to the lines. It's just a bunch of windows and everybody looking around to see who is next. If they had like dots to stand on or numbers to stand on, that would help.

The best macarons I have ever tasted! Make sure to try the caramel and coffee....They are amazing. They are $3.5 a piece but bigger than regular macarons. I also bought the vanilla eclair with whipped creme and custard, which was good too. I did not try their bread and danish but hopefully next time! The service was friendly too. :)

I've never been a big ice cream person, especially when it comes to the "gourmet" variety as it has never lived up to the hype for me. That completely changed when I after my first visit to Jeni's! I was on my way to a pub nearby and was walking to my car when I saw a line wrapped around the bldg. That caught my attention. I asked my friend at the pub about Jeni's and they said totally worth it, so I went after my meal for dessert there. Thankfully, the line had died down a little bit. I have to say, from the minute you are greeted it's just a great experience! The friendliness of the staff, especially when you tell them it's your first time, is just fabulous! They let you sample to build your "dream cone" and make solid recs based on your tastes. I have to say, I was not disappointed when I devoured my cone! The flavor and texture just spoke to the quality of the ice cream and I left with a smile on my face. Definitely my new ice cream go to in the Queen City!

I love sprinkles but holy moly is this a poorly designed store. Customers have no idea where to go, for the ice cream flavors are by the exit so you have to try to reach over the people paying to grab a menu a rope and maybe an employee giving menus would work. Second complaint, tons of workers and only 2 people ahead of me yet it took over 15 mins to get them, the ice cream line was a bit better. Instead of doing a good job employees just kept apologizing for their screw ups. Cupcakes great as usual, will just use ATM from now on if I ever go to this one again.

Had a coffee macaroon and a chocolate eclair. They were alright. Nothing to write home about. The macaroons are larger than your usual size, but since it didn't taste particularly good, $3.50 is still a rip off.

My friend flew me back three macarons from Bouchon Bakery, and even eaten a day later, they were phenomenal. The macarons here are definitely sizable to the point where you may feel a cavity after finishing just one. However, there is a perfect ratio of cream to cookie and the texture are pretty perfect. Probably some of the best macarons I have had since coming back from Paris last year! I had the pistachio and strawberry lemonade, both of which were delicious. My fiance had the coffee, which he reports had a strong coffee flavor, which he loved. If you're a macaron lover, I definitely recommend Bouchon! Yet another point to prove that I should never doubt Thomas Keller.

The macrons here are massive! At 17.50 for a box of 6 (buy 5 get one free), who can complain? The salted caramel was pretty good but I really loved my strawberry with white sesame seeds on it. The one star deduction is for the packaging. I got these as a gift to go and the way they packaged it, almost half were smushed before I even made it back to the hotel! When I added more tissue paper and cushion myself, the macrons made it back to Virginia (major turbulence and all on the place) perfectly

Horrible customer service by Ingrid. Ordered some milkshakes, 1 cookie and 1 slice of cake. She was acting as if we were ordering the most complicated stuff in the menu! Rolling her eyes and giving us attitude. The milkshakes and cake were good.
Always delicious.. a very cool place

What can I say! Excellent food, we tried so much and it was all delicious. Service was friendly a little on the slow side only because of the line, and the restaurant itself was adorable. Great place to sit and talk for a while with chairs and couches and tables all over the place. This is a must stop if you are in downtown

Came into Amelie's around 8 am with a slow crowd ordered 3 quiche to go. I waited about 10-15 min for them to be heated and upon delivery 1 was served with a dark brown burnt top. I returned the burnt quiche and proceeded to wait an additional 10 min. As a restaurant industry vet it's highly disappointing to see that type of neglect when there are 3 customers in the cafe. Will only be returning if I have 40 min to spare.

Was extremely disappointed in this place. The gelato flavors were not unique and the texture was more on the watery side. I was hoping for a nice creamy texture but nope not here. I got the cookie cup of course because why not since that's what they are known for. Thought it was a little on the pricier side and the marshmallow was way too salty... did not expect that at all. So if you're not the type that likes sweet and salty, you're in for a huge shock like me. Pros: + you'll get a nice picture for instagram + the macaroon cookie was nice and chewy Cons: -parking was not the best -expensive - SALTY

Staff was very friendly. The items at the bakery weren't any better than I could get at a local shop. Be prepared to wait. The line goes out the door because of the name recognition. The bakery isn't any better than an average run of the mill place. It's definitely not worth the long wait in line.
Quaint stop for deliciously moist cake & rich coffee. If near this area, add this to your list. Even the flavor combinations were special.
Kind service! Helped me on my first trip Soft Serve was crazy and its just different (in a good way) worth the drive

Just went to Jarling's after lunch at Yellowfin. Urgent update: They now have gummy bears. I'm going to pretend that they started carrying gummy bears just because Jarling's loves me. Regardless of the real reason, I will now have a mandatory once-a-week Nerds and gummy bear snowstorm (made with strawberry custard). THANK YOU, JARLING'S. Pardon my brevity, but I need to go start shopping for some bigger pants.. Something with an elastic waist, perhaps...

I don't even what to know what my trip to the dentist will be like after a stop here. Novel Ice Cream sure knows what they are doing. These flavors are packed with a punch and always rotating. Their specialty is jam-packing a donut with your flavor and topping, toasting it and bringing it to you so you can enjoy a donut sandwich. After testing ALL the flavors, you will be in a conundrum as to which one to pick, but don't worry the staff is amazing and has insight. If they are still toasting up the Leslie Knope: waffle sandy with a scoop of ice cream...I don't know why you wouldn't get that.

Stopped in for something sweet. Everything that our party had was excellent. The vanilla eclair and the macaroons were out of this world. Not a lot of seating, so may be right at peak times. Will definitely go back again.

Place is always well maintained a clean. The bread products are never a disappointment. The staff is very friendly and they have a nice chalkboard that let's customers know what days there favorite bread products are available. The bread themselves are simple but full of flavor. I recommend that you either cook the bread with a pasta or some dinner entree and know that you'll est it alot. Because it's fresh it does go bad quickly. The breads are buttery but not so much so that there's a nasty after taste in your mouth. I totally recommend this place to people both living and visiting Madison.

Ummm, I had such high expectations of Carlo's Bakery. Not that a SUPERfan of the show, ok more like a mini-fan; but I used to watch on the regular from time to time. Now the show will end the same way, not only a display of a beautiful cake but also DELICIOUS...right? Like that one place that starts with a F - and ends with - 'S, I eat the crumbs its so good, but this is not a review about that bakery, this is about Carlo's Bakery. I'm not saying that it was bad, but it wasn't good...to me, and yes I had THAT LOOK on my face because I was sadly disappointed. We order a canoli and some kind of coconut cookie. Let's start off with the COOKIE, toasted coconut shortbread cookie; toasted coconut and shortbread, you can't go wrong. Wrong, actually you can go very wrong with this. A very pretty looking cookie, golden brown, with a nice dollop of chocolate smack dab in the middle of the cookie.
