Just me personal opinion, maybe if it was a chocolate ganache it would've helped with the dryness of the cookie. Yes, shortbread is a dry cookie but you definitely get the butter taste on the palate when you eat it. This is a tea/coffee type of cookie, to me it was just bad all over. Super dry, we try to break the cooking in half to split, cookie so hard that when we finally broke the cookie in half, from the force of trying to break the cookie I dropped 1 half on the nasty strip sidewalk. No 5second rule here, that will just have to sit there. Flavor, well I could taste the toasted coconut and the chocolate was just there, that's all I have for that. Traditional Canoli: Once again, I promise I don't know what was up with yesterday's batch, but the 2 items that were purchased were hella overbaked and super hard. Canoli should be a light crisp, hard enough to maintain structure to absorb the filling and not soften the shell but not where your back molars might be cracked after taking a bite. We looked like a hot mess trying to share this canoli on the strip, we pretty much just blended in with the other tourists. Now, the CREAM FILLING now that was DELISH! A nice velvet cream, with a hint of cinnamon, so light - oh I would go back for the cream filling and cream filling only, give me a spoon and a bowl. As for me going back, meh....maybe, since the bakery is mainly known for their cakes then maybe I should a slice of cake instead of the other delectable delicatessens in this shop. The RED VELVET cake did look good, but.... ....let me think about this one, hmm - Red Velvet Cake, huh?

Yoooo, Mitchell's is the BEST. It's family owned, heavily involved in the community, & makes the best ice cream in town, hands down. Their pralines & cream ice cream is so freaking good, with caramelly ribbons spun through each scoop. The shop is always clean, its staff always friendly, & it's always cool to peek behind the scenes through the glass dividers to see exactly how the ice cream is made.

Chocolate lovers dream! It's a cold night in Vegas and we were walking around soaking in the sights when we spotted the Ghirardelli store. We decide to check it out mostly to get out of the cold air without our jackets that we left in the hotel. It is located in the alley by the Linq and the Linq high roller Ferris wheel is located at the end of the alley. We order the sea salt hot chocolate that comes with a little sea salt Ghirardelli square on top. Perfect! It was the perfect thing to drink while walking back to our hotel. I made a decision to order the brownie that looked killer to nibble on later in the day, they warmed it and it was devoured before we even left. Very rich! There was a island of the mini packets of Ghirardelli that you can grab a bag and fill with the different flavors you want to try, as well as already packed bags. There was several employees walking around giving samples of these mini squares. There was a cute little ornament they were selling and the employee told me they were selling a bag with a full bar of the peppermint chocolate flavor for the same price. Side note: I have to make so much effort to not gain $30 lbs because this is my favorite flavor! We ended up leaving with so much free chocolate! During hitter months they sell ice cream which I still saw so many people ordering even with it being cold outside!

A-MAZING!!! Best to drive and park in back, or Uber, walk from Fremont street was fine but a little ways, however, it's a must!!!! All the donuts we got were delicious. We cut them all up and shared and that was worth it to try all of them. Paired with a nitro brew.....WOW, we were in heaven. Staff is beyond nice, helpful and offered perfect suggestions. Get here early, we came at 1030ish and selection was getting small, but plenty for us. When your done head down the street to the container park!!!!!

I really wanted to like this place but for some reason the two cannolis I ordered yesterday 5/16/2022 (1 original and other was chocolate) both of the fillings were semi bland and gritty. Super bummed and hope it was just an off day but I don't think we'll be back anytime soon and rather go to black tap for dessert.

CRACK PIE. There's a reason why it's called crack pie. It's just filled with butter and sugar, but its addicting. A little pricey, ~$6 a slice or $56 a whole pie, but totally worth trying... over and over again... LOL. I love their cookies too, it's more expensive in Las Vegas than New York, but you can't blame them. I really enjoy the blueberry & cream cookie. I like it when it's warm, so microwave it for ten seconds. I also enjoy their soft serve. They do split flavors too. I got the regular cereal milk and the crack pie soft serve served with some salty topping. It's delicious, although the salty topping gets tiring after a while. It is so hard not to spend a lot of money here. I always end up walking away with more than $75 worth of goodies. I just wish it was cheaper. Hurts my health and my wallet every time I buy cookies and crack pies from here, but worth trying at least once!

I followed Hopscotch's buzz before ever tasting its baked goods. When we first moved to CU in 1993, there was only one upscale bakery in town and we longed for more and different. Now, we have a few to choose from, but more and different is always good. Hopscotch is a new take on the upscale bakery, a hipster one, with a particular decor style that is at once vintage and subdued with a modern twist. Think de-colorsatured roses, flattened, or cakes barely iced with embedded contrasting grit. I like this aesthetic -- it seems fresh and understated to me. I first tasted Hopscotch's products after purchasing them at a local arts pop-up. I bought a brownie and some kind of brown sugar butter bar. The brownie was truly phenomenal if you like fudge (rather than cake) style brownies, and I love them. The chocolate was so dark and dense it was like having my tongue immersed in a deep chocolate groove. The brownie had a soft, chewy bite and wasn't overly sweet. The other bar had good taste: brown sugar meets browned butter, but it was dry and crumbly. When Hopscotch opened in the new Art Mart space, I tried another brownie, and it was as good as the first. So, high marks on consistency. I recently went back and tried a strawberry baby cake for me and a white chocolate brownie for my son. I loved the baby cake itself as well as the fresh strawberry compote on top. The cake was moist and tender, the compote had great strawberry flavor. Neither was overly sweet. I did not like the disc of heavy buttercream frosting that sat on top of these. It had the texture of refrigerated butter and did not eat well with the more tender components. Although I suppose my standard for all such strawberry cakes is the enchanting cassata, a softer frosting would move this baby cake toward perfection. My son did not like the white chocolate brownie, although he loves both brownies and white chocolate. He thought the brownie was greasy and salty. It had moved from a fudgy texture to a fatty one without enough flour to support a good bite. Embedded in the bar were bits of white chocolate, which he said was the only positive note. Given Hopscotch's stiff prices ($8 for a baby cake, $4 for a brownie), one expects products to be truly exceptional, without any missteps. I believe there's real quality here and that products are sometimes worth the price. Hopscotch uses carefully sourced, superior ingredients; good technique; and a refined aesthetic. There's a great deal of potential here, but all of the products are not quite yet perfected. And, to be fair, I haven't yet tried many of Hopscotch's other products, although the case is full of tempting options (full sized cakes, meringues, and more). I will also add that I had one encounter with the owner (Kaya Tate) that disappointed me. When her new website went up, she asked followers on Facebook for feedback. I provided some, much of it positive, especially about the website's look & feel and navigation. However, I also said that I thought the landing page should open with something about the deliciousness of the products rather than ethics, originality, etc. The Hopscotch owner wrote back to defend her choices. I replied that I understood why she'd made those choices -- I get how important food ethics and authenticity (localism, etc.) are to the hipster culinary scene -- but stood by my point that what I want first in a bakery is tasty products. How the products get that way can follow. The owner replied again to defend her choices. To me, this was a misstep in a customer interaction. She had every right to disagree with my feedback, but she should have simply thanked me and moved on. Despite this rather sour interaction, I am rooting for Hopscotch.
Love their house soup! They ate doing a good job keeping everyone 6ft apart. They do have outside seating. Treat yourself and get some desserts for Thanksgiving!

Oh wow, go hungry. Not like me who started full and left almost sick. It's so worth it - don't stop eating! We went around 8pm on a Saturday so of course the line was way out the door. Flavors seemed pretty standard and not a massive selection. I got a sundae with chocolate and vanilla ice creams, chocolate chip cookie, hot fudge, and whipped cream. The hubs got a s'mores freezie (which is like a blizzard). The warm marshmallow fluff on the snores is AMAZING. But be prepared with your napkins... We probably could have shared but yeah no. Back patio was pretty packed but we found a place to sit easily anyway. I'd do it again. Maybe I'll try the peanut butter ice cream next time. With 1/2 a peanut butter cookie and chocolate covered pretzels. Yeah, I think so.

I have been to the Batchmaker multiple times. It is a great place to pick up goodies for the office, grab a coffee and muffin for breakfast (or hang out and Eat it there) or to get a great birthday cake. The peanut butter cup chocolate cake is crazy good. If you need a cake, make sure to plan ahead when ordering but it will be worth the wait.
Love this place can't say enough about it friendly staff clean location Donuts amazing highly recommend you should stop in and try a donut

Page's Dairy Mart is a Pittsburgh classic. It sits in somewhat of an odd location slightly outside Southside, but it is worth the drive. Page's has a massive selection of ice cream, desserts, and even food such as burgers or fries (although I believe most people go for the ice cream only!) My usual go-to is any of the arctic swirls, which are similar to blizzards that you get at Dairy Queen, except they're better. If you're looking for something larger to split, I recommend their cookie sundae; it is delicious. The best part about Page's besides the quality? The price! Everything you can get there is very reasonablly priced, and the portions are generous. The sad part is that they are only open early spring to mid fall.. there are times where I crave it on a cold day.

Our daughter moved to Charlotte from Ohio and this was her first birthday away from family. I phoned Cristina and asked if it was possible to have a cake delivered. She sent a quick response, made a beautiful cake and delivered it on a weekend in which she was swamped with Mother's Day orders!!! Our daughter was surprised, thrilled, and said it was one of the best cakes she's ever eaten! I love that this small business caters to the requests of their customers. Cristina is very sweet and great to work with. I would HIGHLY recommend this bakery to anyone wanting to make a celebration extra special. We will definitely be returning!!!

A cute little sweet shop. Ice cream was creamy and some fun flavors- Vietnamese coffee and peppermint (not too minty, not too sweet). Try their seltzer caramel on the coffee ice cream! I loved all their fun candies- I stocked up for Christmas stocking stuffers! And they had a nice little selection of baked goods like cookies and brownies. "Kids" behind the counter were engaging and enthusiastic, perhaps a tad over-enthusiastic. The only thing I really didn't like was the lack of parking (who does valet for ice cream!?) and I really disliked eating with a wooden stick- may I please just have a normal spoon??

The presentation of the ice cream at Melt is so cute. Chinese take out boxes with fortune cookies! And the flights! Five flavors and fortune cookies served in muffin tins! Perfect. But Melt is not just about the presentation. The ice cream is great. Located in the Roosevelt district, it's easy to walk or drive right by Melt without noticing it. Definitely take a moment and stop in. The ice cream flavors are creative and delicious. Numerous choices suitable for adults and for kids. The shop itself is very small, but there is a small outdoor patio in which to enjoy your choices.

Staff at Novel Ice Cream are amazing! They have ice cream flavors that I've never heard of. We got a sampler of 5 different ice creams and were not let down. Each flavor is so delicious. We had: chocolate, butter pecan, Madagascar vanilla, black cherry, Cookie Monster, and got an extra scoop of cucumber lime. Everyone needs this place in their lives. So amazing!
Compost cookie + cereal shake = 'nuff said.

Good food and very friendly staff. Used a hooked deal for buy 1 get 1 50% off to buy milkshakes for my friend and I. On my way out, I accidentally dropped one and it splattered everywhere. I went back into the store and the servers made me a 2nd one for free. Was a damn good milkshake too.
Awesome place & wonderful options. Customer service was great, too. We will be back for sure. Our kids love stopping by after school.

I have been to Butterwood three times. The ambience is cozy and luxurious and I really appreciate that they are open late. The reason I give this place three stars is the lack of consistent quality of their desserts. The last cake I had (it was their standard chocolate) was very dry and crumbly like it was weeks past its prime. I was so disappointed! If I am going to splurge on something like this it must be perfection every time.

My go-to ice cream place in Scottsdale! No one does it quite like them! You have to come here and get a fat daddy to truly understand but even if you just got one scoop of ice cream you would be hooked! Their captain crunch ice cream is my personal favorite, but all of their flavors are out of sight! If you are having a sweet tooth craving stop by here. I found them on Yelp and my bet is if you are reading this you just found them on Yelp too!

This was on my list of "must hit" places during our very short stay in Charlotte, so despite the fact that it was pouring rain, we took a bus from uptown to get there. Arrived around 10:15 on Saturday morning only to learn that...gasp...they had no almond croissants. MAJOR bummer. Decided to try an apple turnover, which was pretty mediocre, and got a cheese danish and chocolate & almond croissant to share the next morning. The cheese danish was decent, not great, and the croissant was excellent. If we had only ordered the chocolate & almond croissant, I would most likely be giving a 4-star rating. Maybe there are other "wow" items that we just didn't select...not sure...or maybe we're spoiled having been to Paris & other excellent French bakeries in the States.

I'm an ice cream aficionado and chin is pretty high on the list of places to go. Expect a wait in line here. Don't worry, it's well worth it. I love the smores Sunday, but even a scoop of their ice cream without all the toppings holds up by itself. Bonus: cool place with lots of niknaks from your childhood.

I don't have a single negative word to say about this place. Fresh, delicious and novel ice cream that never disappoints. Their banoffi sundae and campfire s'more sundaes are amazing. I'm sure the other sundaes are pretty good too but I haven't bothered straying from those two. If you're just getting a scoop their belgian chocolate and salted butter caramel are awesome. The latter was a bit of an acquired taste, but I can't get enough of it now. It's always busy, but they always try to be quick and efficient and that's all I ask. Service is friendly and prompt and you never feel unwelcome. Whenever we have people in town this is always one of the places we go, and it's always one of the things they talk about after we send them back home. Great stuff!

Very good ice cream. Taste homemade. I got the pecan toffee and it was amazing! I will have to go back to try other flavors. They had a pickle flavor and I didn't try it, but I guess there's something for everyone.

The donut tastes SO GOOD and its soft and warm. The I dream omg it tastes like heaven. Come here every weekend. The place is so cool as well very nice to come with your friends to hang out and have a delicious dough melt.

Goddamn I miss this place. Cold Stone Creamery has got nothing on Custard Cup. I have so many awesome memories of friends and family gathering here on hot summer days and nights. The only bummer was that it would shut down at the end of the season and we'd have to go without these delicious treats for a whole 6 months. Smart choice on their part. Because as soon as those doors opened at the beginning of each summer, the line never ended til the end of Sept.
The cookie cup is so very tasty! Fell in love right away. The portion is a bit small, but I guess it's healthier for you? Lol

My first time here since they took over from the old O face. I have to say I am very impressed!! When first walking in the environment is hip. The smell is so amazing and could be smelled from a block away!! We decided to order a dozen to make sure we all got try everything we wanted. We ordered almost every kind or at least the kinds that we wanted to. My favorite is the French toast, so amazing and super fresh!! They make it right when you order it!! That could be breakfast alone. Price point was not bad for the size of the donuts you get! The staff was friendly and the chefs talked to us as we checked out. Check in on Yelp for your free expresso!! What a wake up call. We will be back soon enough!!

Good donuts! My favorite was Butterfinger. I think they're more known for their yeast donuts, so definitely check those out! We got cake batter, which was tasty. Parking across the street was $3.00 for an hour. We did 15 mins for $0.75. We went at 10 AM on a Sunday (MLK weekend) and they were already sold out of French toast donut

We had just had dinner and were craving something sweet; we saw their sign and decided to stop in. We were greeted with smiling faces and we felt so welcomed! We tried a few flavors. I decided on the Vernonni(sp?) it was a coffee flavor - delicious! My boyfriend had the Unicorn Poop he loved it and made the comment "if someone never had ice cream before, I would have them try this flavor." All of their ice cream is made locally here in Phoenix and their flavors are so creamy and delicious. If you're in the area, definitely stop in (especially if you have a sweet tooth)! Next time I'm trying the halo halo! We'll be back!
Used to come here as a kid when they were off of Thomas. Haven't been here in many many years... Sadly they no longer offer food... Ice cream still on point.
Very unique and delicious combo. Took my family for dessert after dinner and it lived up to all the hype. Will never go to Phoenix without stopping in.

First off, the thing that caught my eye about this place was how it looked so much like a movie theatre from the outside! My husband and I decided to spontaneously check it out and we were impressed. It was very spacious and lots of seating, even on the second floor where you can look out to the production floor of the staff making the ice cream. I ordered the Chocolate Peanut Butter Cup and it was just okay for me, it was a bit too sweet but props for adding real PB cups to the mix. I would definitely like to check out their other flavours in the future.

Uhh if you're on a diet than don't even think about it. Come here early because they run out pretty fast! You MUST try their maple bacon and pumpkin. They only take cash but seriously you can buy several donuts from the change you will find in your couch. Go home, eat the mouth-watering donut(s), weep, and then get on that treadmill.

Service was fast - order in, order out. We ordered the fruity cereal milk soft serve with added cornflake crunch and a slice of crack pie. The soft serve was creamy and tasted exactly as described but wasn't overly sweet. But, the added cornflake crunch was not what I'd expected. It had a saltiness to it that didn't really mesh well with the soft serve. We ended up scraping it off. Now, the crack pie. Ohhhhh, the crack pie. I'm obsessed with it. It reminds me of a pecan pie, without the pecans, but more dense. It was rich but not heavy. You could taste the butter in every bite. My only regret was not getting another slice for the ride home. Crack pie. Just do it.

So yummy! Located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan, Milk Bar has a wide selection of treats ranging from cake truffles to cookies to milk shakes. The cake truffles come in packs of three for $7.95(?) and are worth every penny. They have a slightly crisp exterior followed by OMG melt in your mouth goodness. I had the birthday cake flavor my first day and enjoyed the grasshopper chocolate flavor on my flight home. Many have raved about the crack pie and I will add on to that! I had the crack pie milkshake for lunch another day and it was amazing. Big chunks of the famous crack pie throughout the shake, like a Dairy Queen Blizzard on steroids. No need for booze in this shake, although they do offer it! There is no seating at Milk Bar, but there are numerous small tables and chairs/sofas located on the 2nd floor, especially by neighboring Egg Slut and the Chandelier Bar.

Cereal milk soft serve topped with cornflakes FOREVA!! So let me preface my review with 'The Before'. I practically rolled myself out of Momofoku looking like Violet Beauregarde after indulging in an unbelievably incredible and massive dinner. I was SO full you guys and that is genuinely an understatement! I overestimated the allotment of stomach space I thought I saved to try Milk Bar's soft serve afterwards - when judgement time arrived I failed myself and my taste buds and sadly commenced my foodie walk of shame... past Milk Bar. *tear* FFW a couple of hours and viola - I found myself back at Milk Bar, feeling like a champ!, around 1am to claim my prize! Mind you, I was still full so I decided to split an order with my friend. As soon as it hit my lips, my god, the heavens spoke to me! That serving, even if just half, was everything in a dessert I never knew I wanted until then. I know it's a bold statement, but I think I experienced nirvana you guys, who knows? I just know that it was me, that cup of soft serve and those cornflakes for a good 10 minutes and nothing. else. mattered. Anyway, we ate at Wicked Spoon for lunch the next day and you best belie' I beelined it back to Milk Bar afterwards and ordered my OWN cereal milk soft serve w/ cornflakes... yuuum! It was just as heavenly as the first time. Bummed their only locations are NYC, DC, Toronto, Las Vegas. Here's to hoping they open one in L.A. sooner rather than later, until then, I'll just be over here daydreaming of that magical encounter.

I found this place listed on Sunset Magazine's 15 Best Ice Cream Shops in the West. I was a little disappointed that they didn't have more ice cream flavors to choose from. The cool thing is there are many ways you can have your ice cream like an ice cream sandwich, milk shake, or even in a pretzel cone. I got the Vietnamese Coffee with a coconut macaroon cookie which was the only gluten free option. It was good but I wouldn't say extraordinary. There is seating in the front and plenty more outdoor seating at the back of the shop to enjoy your ice cream.

there's a reason this place has 600+ reviews with almost all of them being 5 stars. it's AWESOME SAUCE! our family stopped by novel ice cream while we were in phoenix for a weekend vacation. some places have a lot of hype, but don't deliver... that is not the case with novel ice cream. it's located in and among some others stores, restaurants, bars. the shop is pretty small with no indoor seating, but there are plenty of outside seating. there's even a park down the street as well. the parking on site is limited, but we just drove down the street a few blocks and was able to find street parking. after a short walk we arrived. since it was around 6:30p on a weeknight the line was pretty short. i bet it's much longer on the weekend and later in the evening. they offered us all the samples we wanted and we took them up on their offer. the owner was there and super helpful in explaining the different flavors and all the ingredients in them. they've won multiple awards for their ice cream. we make ice cream at home and they've inspired me to up my game. my kids ended up choosing the cookie monster and butter pecan. i got the dough melt (ice cream sandwiched between a warm glazed donut) with their award winning chocolate. i forgot what my wife ordered, but she loved it. the price point is higher than you're going to pay at thrifty's or mc donalds, but the quality is so much higher, it's not even fair to compare. there was definitely the standard sugar rush and subsequent crash, but we loved this place. i asked them to open a store in tucson, but maybe it's a good thing they haven't done that quite yet.

So I can't comment on the food from here but the service we received here today was nothing short of inexcusable. I'm not one to post rant reviews as I'm in the service industry out here and realize most are bs. We came in I the bakery and pulled a ticket. Looking in the case at all the baked goodies and literally 30 seconds had gone by and they called the number before we could see what number we where. We asked a question about something in the case and the clown behind the counter turned in to a ass responding in a aggressive tone, "I have already called that number three times what do you want". Now mind you we have been in the store a whopping 3 minutes. The guy proceeds to be a dick with the manager standing right beside him and acts like everything is fine. When she realizes we are unhappy her only response was, maybe he is having a bad day. I get it, you don't reprimanded employees out on the floor but you don't pretend like nothing is wrong. I could care less if your having a bad day. Welcome to the tourist industry buddy put on a smile and pretend to be nice to the people that come in to spend money. We had family that came into town a had two things she wanted to do while she was here. One was to go to this place. Shame on the clown behind the counter and shame on the manager for not being able I do her job.

My biggest gripe: The employees either need to step up their game or management needs to hire more employees. It is the middle of summer and I would expect an ice cream shop to be up-staffed in anticipation of the increase in customers. For the amount of foot traffic that the Chocolate Shoppe gets between 7-9PM on a warm summer night, they are seriously, seriously understaffed. I'm not one to complain about standing in line for 15-30 minutes for a scoop of ice cream (especially if I'm craving it), but unfortunately, Chocolate Shoppe doesn't really deliver. There are many flavors, yes, but I feel like the quality of the ice cream they serve is way too commercial (read: overly processed). I could probably pick up a no-name pint of the same flavored ice cream at the Copps down the street and not be able to tell the difference. Given the other options in the area (including UW's own Babcock Hall Dairy Store), it will be a long while until I'm back.
Some of the best french bread outside France.
Wow! The most amazing Cream stuff doughnut I've ever had, actually the first I've ever had!!! Delish!!

I visited Donut Bar last weekend, recommended by a friend. I stopped in for an early morning treat before due to a craving, and let me tell you it was perfect! The staff was extremely friendly and cheerful. There isn't much light in the cafÃ©, but the service was prompt and the interior was very clean. They were willing to help out with my choices as I had never been there before. They gave us samples of the fillings to try; some of the options include strawberry split or PB and J and even DB's Nutella donut. The atmosphere was warm and pleasant. The coffee there is outstanding and there are also a lot of choices. It came with an awesome flavor and acidity. It was definitely one of the best I have ever had since I moved to Vegas. The only short of negative thing I would note is that when it gets busy you have to wait in the line to order for quite a long time. Even though it gets pretty crowded, I guarantee you the wait is worth it!
The best bakery in town. My daughter watched the shows and she couldn't wait to try it!!!

My first time here and I had to start with the mini daddy. It comes with a macaroon cookie (almond flour), a torched marshmellow and ice cream. I tried 4 flavors and they were all good! Some creative flavors here along with the classics. Most importantly it has the one thing every ice cream pace needs-- water! For after the ice cream of course. Really like that detail.
The ice cream is great. They have monthly flavors so every month is a new adventure. Also don't forget about their Tuesday special. If u haven't been you are missing out!!

Not what we expected from an Italian bakery! Cold bread for sandwiches because they have no toasters! Chicken salad was inedible- clearly not made that morning. Plus a server with a real attitude with 'yes' & 'no' clipped responses to any questions. He clearly didn't want to be there and in retrospect neither did we.
So many Yummy options you cant go wrong! Great service great place!!!!

You know what you need to get? A frekkin' cannoli!!!!!! My husband and I decided try a handful of items and we both agreed that the cannoli was bombastical. Everything else was just alright. We stopped by after our dinner at Giada's so there was no line. Despite it being the end of the night, they still had a wide selection of stuff to choose from. We ordered: Strawberry shortcake- it looked so pretty and mouth watering, so I had to order it. The strawberries were sweet, the cream just right. The cake part was spongy, not a biscuit like pastry. Chocolate biscotti- pretty standard and not mind blowing. We decided to pick one because there was a variety of flavors. Figured they might be a special thing. Raspberry cookie- shortbread double cookie with raspberry jam in the middle. It was okay Chocolate cream puff- this was suggested by a patron in line. Very creamy, decadent, pretty. Taste was good. I dunno if it would be my go to item though. I will repeat this... Holy cannoli. They have two different sizes. I choose the mini and wish I had ordered the full size version. If I come back, that's what I would order, hands down! Overall, if you're comparing prices to an 85 degrees or Portos, yes- it's more expensive and not as worth it in my opinion.
Great home-made ice cream. Honey pecan in a waffle cone is my absolute favorite. All of these reviews ring true!

I went with my friend 2 days ago and I gorged on so many items... every item was worth gorging on!! And they even had a great deal on buy three get one free chocolate covered strawberries!! They have great prices!! I'll be going back regularly to see what items they have because they change daily!

What's not to love about this place? I enjoyed some great coffee and some pretty good macarons really late on a weeknight. They are pretty mediocre as far as macarons are concerned, but they hit the spot. There was a bit of a wait, but it was worth it. Even at the off time, it was hard to find a seat. They definitely need more seating. This is a great place for people watching.

I just..I mean how can I..well it's...Delicious! A jewel of a location in Charlotte. I only had a day in Charlotte and I visited here twice...really. I grabbed a quick croissant to go after hitting town from Raleigh. After my first bite & then a post on Facebook that generated several comments...such as get the salted caramel brownie and many others I knew I would be stopping by on my way out of town. I did. And had beautiful sugar shock during my drive back. Macaroons, fruit tarts, and that brownie...I tried a little of each and saved some for another day. Open 24 hours. Really.

Yum, yum, yum! Never have I been so excited to eat a donut! I parked at the meters on 6th street and the walk was not bad at all. You just turn the corner and all the donuts are staring at you. You walk right in and the prices of the donuts are to your immediate right. They may have different donuts depending on the season, but majority of them are the same. They're all very delicious though! I just got a variety of donuts, choosing the ones that looked good. You NEED to get the Birthday Cake donut with an surprise Oreo inside. I was so excited for it. I heard a lot of hype for the creme brÃ»lÃ©e donut because of that *crack* when you break it... I tried doing that while recording it... fail. LOL. It's harder than it looks, literally. And I wasn't a big fan of the taste of it. So I went back to enjoying my birthday cake donut. YUM. Come early because I've heard that donuts sell out quick and once they're gone, Donut Bar closes. Enjoy!
This is a unique place that feels like home which my husband did not like. The food is very good and the pastries are delicious.
their banana ice cream is still my favorite thing....because it actually tastes like bananas and not banana flavoring. so glad they're open again!

Whoever doesn't give this place 5 stars is off their rocker. (And that comes from a professional psych nurse ;-) Perfect cookies. Ice cream samiches :-) Devil's food cake cones. Amazing cupcakes. It's the almost too sweet but not quite sweet enough perfection. Decadence in its finest.

I wish I was giving this place just 2 stars because of the kind of terrible service I had,but the ice cream just isn't that great either. The flavors are not creative, and the ice cream is just mediocre. Absolutely nothing special here. The last time I was there the service was very slow, and it seemed obvious that the employees did not enjoy their jobs. I ordered a one scoop in a sugar cone, and she dropped half of the scoop into the freezer, then plopped the half of a scoop lopsided on the cone. I tried to ask her for a bowl to put it in, but I was clearly bothering her. I got the attention of another employee who gave me a bowl, then asked her to clean up the mess, yet didn't offer me an apology - or the other half of my scoop. I probably will not be visiting again. Don't mess with my ice cream!

Had to try this out since it's so close to my workplace. Got there 10 min before opening and there were already 3 other people waiting in their cars for the store to open up. The store is well maintained and nice and bright inside. All the donuts are beautifully displayed in the front. Like other reviewers have noted, the donuts are not I got 1/2 a dozen donuts for $8.50 (cash only). I just asked them to give me their favorite donuts because I did feel a bit rushed with the line forming behind me. The donuts all looked SO cute and actually tasted really good. They are smaller than your regular sized donuts- which I liked. Definitely not the BEST tasting donuts in cleveland, but i would return again because these are the perfect donuts to take to work.

best lavender ice cream!! softest cookies ever!! i came in for a quick minute to check it out & im glad i did. its amazing there. easy access, obviously very busy in the summertime. weekends are full with families and kids hanging about. everything is handcrafted and local! cant beat that! i would recommend this place to anyone and everyone needing a quick sweet treat. you won't regret it.

MACARONS!!!! I've died and gone to heaven. They are so light and fluffy. A little crunch on the outside and chewy on the inside, not to mention the filling! YUMMMM! I think I've pretty much tried all the flavors. Vanilla, pistachio and coffee are my favorites. I even tried the seasonal orange, which was delicious as well. Good thing Vegas is the closest Bouchon bakery to me or else I might be buying them every week! Definitely a must try if you're visiting Vegas.

I expect a coffee place to serve coffee in ceramic coffee cup instead of a use and throw paper cup. We drove 30 mins just to try out this place and there was no coffee in my mocha. Yeah, no kidding!! What I fail to understand is why will a place that is open 24/7 will serve coffee to it's customers in a to-go cup unless asked for it? I would rather recommend you to go somewhere else, especially if you live far away.

I've only had the macarons here. I stopped by after breakfast (this place is sort of hard to find, it's underneath escalators) at Bouchon to pick up some macarons for my sister before driving home. I would have gotten more, but they had ran out of a lot of stuff! They even only had one chocolate macaron left, so getting there earlier is a must. Regardless, the macarons seem pricey, but they're about as big as my palm, so it's well worth it. They have pretty tasty macarons, but I wouldn't go as far as to say they're the best you can find -- maybe for Vegas though. I was considering giving this place four stars, but I couldn't really justify it. But I still feel like five is a lot, so for accuracy, I'll say it's four-and-a-half stars.
Good ice cream. Nothing out of the ordinary. Everyone was friendly. Pretty busy but line moved fast.

Every so often in life, you're blessed to stumble across an establishment that makes you smile, that makes your heart sing, and that makes your stomach happy. Ladies and gentleman, this is such a place. Service: I cannot tell you how much the owner loves people and his shop. He's always kind, helpful, and willing to tell you about what makes each flavour special. I've been here twice since moving to Phoenix and I can't say enough about how welcome I feel every time I visit. The diversity in the clientele is incredible with people from all walks of life enjoying these treats. Food: Donut and ice cream. And ice cream and ice cream. The ice cream is made with love. It is fresh and so darn tasty. The prices are also incredibly reasonable. You can easily share a $4.50 double scoop. We had the taro and Thai tea the first time, and the strawberry and Cookie Monster the second time. Delicious. The only thing that outshines the ice cream is the service. See above. Ambiance: the shop is located in a cute neighborhood of Phoenix off of Grand. The diagonal-ness of Grand ave scares me, but not enough to not come to Novel. There's lots of seating area under the string lights. Come here, come for a date, just find a way to taste the ice cream. Also, don't be scared by the lines, they move quickly and the ice cream is worth every minute of the wait.

Don't waste your money. Just pick up some prepackaged stuff from a grocery store and you'll be better off. Ordered a brownie, a white and a dark chocolate mousse, and a Cookies & Cream Cake Slice. Nothing bad about the mouse, nothing great. The cake slice could have easily been one thawed from the frozen section of a supermarket. The brownie was much worse than things I picked up in a grocery store for half the price; stale and flavorless aside from the whole pecans throughout. Pair that with the fact that their partnership with DoorDash as a delivery service took over 90mins to give us a "40min" delivery (to deliver to a hotel less than 1.5 miles away); simply awful. Calls to the store meet an automated message saying they have left for the day (while well within business hours). Worst $50 ever spent!!

Delicious crepes!! I tried the savory Montreal crepe with beef brisket and swiss cheese. The brisket was tender, juicy, and flavorful. The portion size was also generous for only $6! Best yet, Crepe De Luxe is very efficient with take orders and making crepes, so the line moves fairly quickly :)

I stop by there after dining nearby, they really had the social distancing stuff going on I thought that was pretty cool. I realize though that part of the ice cream experience is the social aspect of it. However I cannot take away from the deliciousness of the salted caramel milkshake that I got. It actually beat out the peanut butter milkshake that I used to get about three hours south of here. Overall I say to snaps up Mitchells
Great ice cream & worth the wait even in the face of the usual lines of loyal customers.
Soo good! I recommend the coconut macaroon so far! Even though I'm not a coconut fan this little thing was to die for!

Yummmmmmmmm. This place was good. I had the four scoop sampler which is a pretty awesome idea. Graham central, chocolate peanut butter brownie, monkey business and ore-dough. I'd get them all again except maybe would swap the ore-dough. It wasn't bad by any means but I think the others were just sooo good they overshadowed it as it was a simpler flavor. Also the guy working when we swung by on a Friday afternoon was friendly so I didn't gave a bad customer service experience as others have mentioned. I'm bummed that I don't live in state to go back here but my jeans will probably be happy about that!
Amelie's never disappoints. Even when there's a line around the corner, it really moves and the lattes and desserts are always tasty and delicious.
In three words, Amelie's is: delicious, cool and amazing.
A 'burgh favorite for a reason. The Yinzer is locally sourced and delicious. For a little slice of not-so-well-known Pittsburgh history and taste, Page's is the ice cream shop to visit.
Absolutely terrible. We threw away the cookies and cupcakes we bought because they tasted so bad.

Came for the Cannoli and shockingly they wren't that great! but everything else is spectacular. The cheesecake is perfections and the biscotti mamamia! There's a lot of mouthwatering and deliciously looking items to choose from, been trying two two each time I am there. Definitely a must try when in Las Vegas, just skip the Cannoli and go for anything else! Oh and sometimes there can be a little line so be patient.

This may be a case of where the celebrity reputation is the main thing that a business has thing for it. We went as a family to try some delicious Italian treats, like we saw on their TV show. The presentation and shop was very nice. But the taste as quality of their goods was only "so so". We had a slice of their salted caramel chocolate cake, a canoli, a lobster tail, and a pecan chocolate cookie. The cake was moist and beautiful, but tasted like Betty Crocker mix. The other treats were just OK. The prices were reasonable, considering this was in Vegas and at the Venetian, no less. Not really worth it.

This is one of those places where I can't tell if I don't like it because of my poor menu choice or if it was just that bad. They have macaroon ice cream and ice cream sandwiches made of apple fritters or donuts. They also had a selection of shakes and other items. I simply wanted to check out the ice cream. I got birthday cake ice cream in a cup. It literally tasted fresh out the generic carton. It wasn't creamy, rich, or fresh to me. I wouldn't recommend coming here if you just want ice cream.
Oh my what a great selection of flavors!!! It is a little bit on the more spending your side of things but it's homemade and it's wonderful!!!!

If you're considering Ice Cream today, your search is over. Churn is by far the greatest ice cream around. I take a trip up Central to this little Ice Cream shop at least 2-4 times a week. My brothers and I enjoy the variety of flavors, and the service is nothing like you've ever experienced before. Every employee is an abundance of joy. The second you walk through the door you're always greeted with kindness. Personal favorite employees are Megan and Raymond, they always put a smile on my face. So stop by Churn, because you've found the Ice Cream and service you've been searching for.
These are great cupcakes. Nice and fluffy and good amount of frosting. Wasn't digging the price but great cupcakes. Also, great customer service. Thats always a plus.
Super friendly and informative staff. That's the only reason I'm giving it any stars. Not good ice cream flavor/toppings and choices.

Desserts here are fantastic. Whether it's the macaroons or the eclair, desserts here hit the spot. With covid going on I also do appreciate that that they had face masks at the door in case someone did not bring one. I also had a coffee from here and that was the only thing that did disappoint me that's why it's only 4 stars. I am definitely coming back here soon.
Excellent icecream shop ! Dropped in with my kids last weekend!

My coworker and I needed a chocolate fix and we stopped here to partake in the sinful treats. I was great to finally catch up with Chris (the owner) and congratulated him on opening another location. I decided to keep my fix on the light side settling on a chocolate peanut butter filled truffle and a dark chocolate dipped pretzel rod. The truffle was so creamy and the peanut butter center was ever so smooth!! My coworker decided to go big and ordered a peanut butter chocolate brownie topped with peanut butter icing and a mint chocolate chip milkshake!!! She enjoyed her milkshake and shared a piece of her brownie with me. The chocolate in the brownie overshadowed the peanut butter flavor but the icing made up for what the brownie lacked.

Every time I go to Jeni's the experience is incredibly consistent. The service is always friendly and chipper, the staff behind the counter are ready to give you samples from the second you walk through the door. There are two things that really stand out to me about Jeni's 1) The flavors are so diverse and different from your local ice cream shoppe. If you're in the mood for the regular old lineup, this isn't your spot. It's just so creative. 2) They truly have something for everyone. Gluten Free? Done. Dairy Free? Done. Gluten and Dairy free in one delicious flavor? Done. On top of the excellent product, the shop is cute - I love the neon sign begging you to come in. There is an outdoor patio to enjoy you treat while you people watch as well.
The best ice cream in the burgh!!! My husband and daughter love the simple cones and I always get the brownie sundae.. the brownie is always soft and warm and perfect.

Grew up with this absolute hidden gem of Cleveland food. I can't really say much more than whats been said before. I mean, if every review is basically the same so far... well its basically true. It was made even MORE 5-star worthy with the inception of the Original May Company malt, aka quite possibly the greatest malt in the history of malt-dom, What flavor is it? Vanilla? Chocolate? NO. Just malt. Honey Hut is a bit of a "locals only" kind of place, but once you try it... You'll be back enough times to be an honorary Brooklyner. Sorry, Mitchell's. Honey Hut still has my heart.

Great concept of a two-story ice cream shop in their ice cream factory. The ice cream certainly tastes homemade and the flavors they come up with are always worth a try. The only flavor that I didn't care for was the Christmas Ale ice cream. Way too heavy and decadent for my taste. The staff have the patience of Job with no one being able to make a quick decision. There's just too many good choices.

Very dissapointed, work in the area so have walked by several times,the place always looks busy but actually its not. The counter help and cashiers are just super slow. There doesnt seem to be any real system to get the treats. I get the number system however its not working there. After my number was called and I placed my order my number was called again 15 minutes later,the guy asked what we wanted I told him we already placed an order,he started bad mouthing his co workers. Another seven minutes later our order was ready. So after waiting 22 minutes I got my cannoli and cream puff. Yup waited 22 minutes for trwo items that just had to be pulled out of the display case. The treats were ok nothing to write home about.

Ever since I saw Carlos talking about their lobster tail pastry I've always wanted to try it. We've been to Las Vegas several times before during the weekends where the line was so long I didn't want to wait. Finally went during the week and got 3 cupcakes and the lobster tail pastry. The cupcakes did not disappoint. They were very moist, but frosting was great as well, but a little too sweet for me and my boys. Now let's get to the lobster tail... that was a disappointment. It was a flaky pastry and the filling was creamy but bland and no flavor. I might try out the cupcakes again the next time we're in the area.

Yum yum yum! Tried this place finally today and it was so good!! I had the gooey butter cake flavor and was just so delish! Walk in and it smells amazing, like fresh waffle cones..what you want to smell going into an ice cream shop. The building is just entirely too cute, it's in a great location right off the light rail and within walking distance of so many restaurants, so going there for dessert after dinner is extremely doable. Thankfully since I waited for the summer time hype to die down I didn't have to wait in the long lines that I have seen riding by it before. I can't wait to go back and try some other yummy flavors. :-)

I love coming here and the fact that it's open 24 hours makes it the best late night snack stop! My husband and I come here at the end of most of our date nights. They have a great variety of French pastries. Great dessert spot and super awesome decor.
We have been there a number of times and we also order on DoorDash my children love their ice cream sandwiches with cookies

Me and my family used to love to go here for special occasions (it's a bit of a drive from their house). But since my dad is now lactose intolerant and I'm vegan it's we can't really get anything anymore. Just a drink or a soup every once in a while. I would love for them to have one or two vegan dessert options for those of us who don't do animal products. I'm not picky, I'll take anything!
I had a piece of peanut butter chocolate cake as a present. It was awesome! Enjoyed every bite
Best bakery in Charlotte! Everything is 10/10 and the space is so unique and welcoming. Staff is excellent and helpful in decision making. Especially since they have a ton to offer.
Nothing fancy but best ice cream place in Scottsdale AZ. Recommend the specialty dish with the toasted Marshmallow. Guy working was nice.

I am lactose intolerant. Well, not me so much as my stomach. Not to be too descriptive, but I don't feel well after eating foods/drinks with dairy. For Sweet Republic, I am willing to deal with the pain. Sweet Republic has fantastic Ice Cream, Ice Cream sandwiches, and more. Since it is an individually owned and operated business, the deserts taste slightly different every time I go...and that is great. Unlike chains, Sweet Republic is creating ice cream with unique, and sometimes, slightly changing, recipes.

I love Buddy and his family oriented bakery / T.V. Show Cake Boss so naturally I had to go out of my way and stand in a long obnoxious line to get a taste of his pastries. After doing my homework by reading tons of reviews & browsing through pics I came to the conclusion that the only item worth trying would be their Lobster Tail. I was right. Their cookies/biscotti were basic and insanely overpriced at around $17 a pound. The Lobster Tail pastry alone cost $6 for one so I was good with that. The exterior shell was so crispy as in crunchy, not flaky like a croissant but more like it had a nice crunchy bite to it which I loved. Filling consisted of a mixture of Custard, Whipped Cream and Baileys Irish Cream (Irish whiskey and cream based liqueur). It was divine!!! Tasted better the following day when the Baileys flavor was more developed and pronounced. Great stuff! Hope an L.A. location is on its way...

Super delicious and creative! This used to be my favorite place to go when we would lowride on Saturday nights until the popos shut fun down. And for what you ask? We were just families low riding with our friends, supporting local businesses. No drama just a love for old cars and old music. Really no reason to go to grand now sadly. Everyone is in Glendale and it's not the same I'll tell you that right now

I was in Vegas this past weekend. My party we had a surprised birthday for one of my girl. I was in Vegas looking everywhere for a bakery. I found this on Yelp. When I got to this bakery, I was surprised it was Cake Boss. The service was good. The lady who helped me was very detailed what they offered. The cakes were nice and presentable. I bought a strawberry shortcake for one of my girl's birthday with a beautiful tag. The cake was delicious. The line got busy right after I bought my cake. They had a deal going on, giving out free mug or water bottle.

Since watching Chef's Table I have been clamoring to try Milk Bar in NY, but won't be going for a few months. I was surprised and excited to wander by this one in LV. I do not have a big sweet tooth but was intrigued by Chef Christina Tosi's innovation and passion as portrayed on Chef's Table. I decided to try the ICED CEREAL MILK LATTE and it was sooo good. The cashier confirmed it was not too sweet and she was right. It was not overly sweet but it was amazingly delicious with a slight hint of cereal milk flavor. It was so good I wanted to come back the next day for another one in a larger size.
I had the blondie sundae and it was incredible!! I only wish they had water available to purchase! No inside seating but there were benches outside that were nice

I'm so glad there is another boba place to visit when I'm in Phoenix. I had ordered the iced matcha latte, which was perfectly made the way I like it (you can definitely taste the matcha, but it's not too overpowered by the sweetness of the sugar and milk). The cereal milk ice cream was also delicious. I almost forgot to take a picture, since it looked so good.

I'm a huge fan of Mitchell's. Since moving away from Cleveland, I don't get to have it very often anymore. We were in town visiting my parents and I had to stop here after eating dinner next door. It was my first time at this location. It's much bigger than the one I normally go to. It's very open inside with tables. You can see the whole process through windows in the back. We were in a bit of a rush, but the line went really fast. I love their flavor selection. I decided to go with seasonal flavors this time and got a tasters duo with egg nog and cinnamon. I was expecting to like the egg nog the most, and it was good, but I loved the cinnamon. If you've never tried Mitchell's, it's definitely a go to ice cream place in Cleveland, so check it out!
Cannolis are excellent, of course! Pignoli cookies are just what we needed, too. Delicious!

My wife and I wanted to try this place for a while. She got the strawberry shortcake and I got the dark chocolate mousse. We both enjoyed the items, but I wouldn't say they were great. It had good taste, but for the price of about $10 each I don't think will rush back. Seems to be more about the swag than the pastries.

Two words. CRACK PIE! OH MY GOSH!!!! I had heard about Christina Tosi and watched her on Master Chef Junior so I was pretty excited to check this place out. The crack pie did not disappoint! It was a buttery, sweet piece of heaven. In addition to pie form you can also enjoy crack pie as a milkshake, quake or soft serve. I also ordered her signature compost cookie which has pretzels, potato chips, coffee, oats, graham cracker, butterscotch and chocolate chips. I asked for it warmed up and it was just okay to me. I bet it's delicious fresh out of the oven so if you can figure out when they're baking and get a fresh one do it. My boyfriend ordered a fancy chocolate malt cake milkshake with vodka and kahlua. You definitely won't miss the alcohol in this adult beverage! It was very potent! Given my experience with the crack pie I will definitely come back to try more!

Such a great dessert shop to go to after eating in the Venetian (specifically Canalettos Italian). After dinner we saw Sloans across the way and I've heard about it and heard great things so we thought we'd give it a shot and it didn't disappoint! I got the mint chip and Mud pie and they both were Delicious! Definitely a heavier ice cream comparable to cold stone compared to a lighter ice cream. Another great thing about this place was that, though it was not many choices, they still had 3 vegan ice cream choices which was awesome since we had some vegans in the group and they said their ice creams were also Great! The only slight downside to sloans was pricing. For two small ice creams it was $17.00 which IMO is a bit much but I mean when you're in a place like Vegas I also would expect the prices to be a tad bit higher than a normal ice cream shop that would charge around $3-5 for a small. Covid review- it was clean, staff wore masks, not sure above gloves, friendly)
Not the worst but definitely not impressing. I think it was overpriced for what you get and the flavors were average. It wasn't for me, but it may be for someone else.

85 degrees is great. I used to go to one all the time when I lived in Irvine. The bread is fresh and they were coming out every few minutes to re-stock with some fresh pastries. We got some tarts, blueberrytale, and some mocha bread. Everything was great! Not too sweet, just right. It is so popular that the line to post wrapped around and we waited about 13 minutes just to get too the cashier. They also have an effective computerized ordering system to order drinks andd had a separate room to sit and your pastries.
The desserts were great! But not worth the price. Don't let the long line fool yea it goes by pretty fast.

It's great to have Mary Coyle back in the neighborhood. The iced cream has a great consistency, and is sweeter than some of the artisanal iced creams in the area. Old fashioned iced cream shop complete with milkshakes, sundaes and the lot! It can get busy, especially right when the nearby schools let their students out.

The presentation of the ice cream is cute and fun in the Chinese take out box w the fortune cookie, but the ice cream itself was just ok. I feel there are better ice cream shops in Phoenix. The texture of the ice cream wasn't very creamy and the flavor was a little underwhelming. I got the banana cream pie. Not sure if we will be back.

Uncle Bryan came into Cleveland from LA for family wedding. This was his ode to Mitchell's, sent to nephew Alex.... I'm sensing a little bit of jealousy there Alex, which is understandable for the best ice cream place IN THE WORLD. I'm at two visits and own one t-shirt. Break down: FIrst visit July 22. Wowed by theater-setting, the abundant light from all-encompassing windows, the warm customer service, unlimited spoons and overall cleanliness and well-lit interior. Slightly dizzyby the selection, I tried Lena's lavender honey which was delicate and beautiful. Strawberry jalapeno? The audacity. I went with banana cream pie, and was mesmerized by the fresh bananas, the homemade marshmallow ribbon. And wait, is that homemade shortbread crust in the ice cream. Why yes it. At this point, it is among my top ice cream places ever. Then I am led to the upstairs, where I can watch workers happily working in a spotless kitchen fromalarge window - cutting up shortbread, brownies. Amazing. I took that picture of the setting sun. We sit on picnic benches and enjoy blissful moments of high summer. July 24. Notoriously discerning food critic Xavi attends, and pictures of his utter happiness eating peanut butter ice cream are sent to me. Trip II: Post wedding July 25. I return with reluctant nephews and Topher. Having always placed pistachio as my go-to ice cream, I make the plunge with toasted pistachio. Explosions. Eben marvels as he is given an Eben-sized single scoop filling a waffle cone. We take in the workplace window of joy. Even through the haze of White Claw, the nephews are impressed. I mention at the front slight disappointment that the train is not working. And the guy behind the counter hits the switch, and the train starts moving. Nephews deny ever being reluctant. My only quibble is that t-shirt is not a large, either that or I have one too many Mitchell's.

After seeing other yelpers checking in at this place, we figured we would give this place a try on a Friday night. For ice cream, it is all vanilla base. Then you pick a flavor, a topping and an ingredients and they will create one just for you. You have a choice of having it on a waffle cone or a cup. I picked the waffle cone (and I regret it later because it was too much and messy). They also sell unique drinks that I would like to try next time. Since it was my first time, I ordered one from premade menu (I think it was called Oreo something). It took them at least 15 minutes to make the ice cream, but we did not mind to wait since it was a Friday night. If you want to go in and out of there, just keep that in mind. I also tried a sip of the Strawberry Macha Latte. It has a unique taste to it, but I am not sure if I would order it for me. Overall, the service was friendly, prices are a bit high but once again I love local businesses. I will come back to try something else again

Macaron ice cream sandwiches?! Yaassssss! What a genius concept to take two delicious desserts and then smoosh them together. My mister and I went on a busy Saturday evening and there was a line to the door, but we persisted and it moved pretty quickly. I was worried that there would be slim pickings for flavor options but I was definitely wrong because picking which macaron was a hard decision! Some of the flavor options are more traditional like mint chocolate chip and some are more wild like fruity pebbles or the strangely named play doh. I really want to go back to try that one just by the name alone. Since it was my first time I decided to stick with something more classic - cookies and cream. Whew, was that excellent! Giant cookies and cream macaron mounded with cookies and cream ice cream and then topped with another giant cookies and cream macaron. The macaron was great, but not classically baked. It had the crunch of a macaron on first bite, but the texture was more along the line of a soft baked cookie. Regardless, it was so good. The ice cream also appeared to be house made with huge chunks of cookie in it. For ~$6, it was huge portion wise. My mister and I easily could have split one and been satisfied. Definitely will be back!

Wowwwwww - this is an amazing full service bakery. They have every pastry and cake you can imagine, cookies, brownies, cannolis, cream horns, cream puffs, Italian cookies, and homemade cheesecake. They also have several types of croissants, which is what we chose for breakfast. I had a cappuccino, and my husband had a caramel latte. Both were very good and at a nice value. We would love to return (and might go back today to take some goodies home).

Gourmet ice cream at it's best. I stumbled upon this place in a vacation magazine that gave great reviews & since I was heading down to Scottsdale, I thought why not stop by & check it out. This place makes all of their ice cream, frozen yogurts & sorbets. It doesn't get any better than "homemade" stuff in small batches. The Salted Butter Caramel was wonderfully creamy, light with just enough hint of salt. Almost tasted just like Fleur de Sal caramel. The Peanut Butter Chip was made with organic slow churned Virginia peanuts & chocolate chips. I have to admit, I'm crazy about PB & if it's not organic then forget it! Imagine my surprise when I was told that it was made with organic peanut butter...YUM! The flavor was packed with PB, not so much that it overwhelms you, just enough to tantalize your taste buds. It was sweet & salty at it's best & what can you say about PB & Chocolate? 2 tastes that taste great together! The Basil Lime Sorbet was super refreshing with a tang of lime, perfect for any hot day. I'm definitely a fan of this place, the only downfall for me is that it's 800 miles away. Stop by this place if you're ever in the neighborhood. You won't be disappointed with the varieties of ice cream that they offer & the great service behind the counter.

Uhg so bad we literally had to throw more then half of it away. Literally it just takes like a blob of shit. Salty and bland as the same time To make this clear my Sugar fanatic child thought it was gross and was the one to throw it away We got the chocolate chip with marshmallow and corn chip cookies with the soft serve and sprinkles and cornflakes Ended up Adding fudge to help - it didn't work $17 for a sundae funday What a waste of money and calories Service was okay not bad but nothing special they did the job they're there for however if milk products are so significantly unique and unlike any other and takes a special Tongue to enjoy employees may want to ask questions and engage a little bit with customers Examples of questions to ask knowing the product again is so rare to taste 1. Have you tried any of our products before? 2. What kind of flavors do you normally enjoy? 3. Would you like to sample perhaps? I am aware of the pandemic however many other places are currently again offering samples And if you can operate a business By putting Product in a big cup you can try putting it in a very small cup or a spoon as well

I was very disappointed to learn that 99% of their items are frozen and then thawed or baked then decorated. Certainly not worth my money when there are a number of bakeries in Vegas and on the strip that offer freshly made items daily and don't require a ridiculous wait in line. This place is more of a novelty than a quality bakery. Not impressed with any of the items I've had from this place. Save your time and money and go to Bouchon Bakery instead.
Very good pastries and breakfast. Accommodating to my gluten- free wife. Good coffee as well.

Came here this past weekend and unfortunately they had really bad service. First of all they were all out of a lot of items! The menu was not updated! The workers were very rude and unfriendly! I have been to the Disneyland location in the locations in Hollywood and San Francisco and they are not like this! The worker was rude I asked to change my flavor and he had a smart remark saying that he only had two hands. This is unacceptable behavior as a worker! I will not return here at all!

Got to try the Thai Tea flavor which is only available at this location. Sooo delicious! They are also giving out a free taiyaki when you purchase an upside down ahboong ice cream for this weekend only!
Love this place, cool options and good options for those not too adventurous. Tasty ice cream so fresh and I had the coffee float with sesame ice cream DELICIOUS!

we got the Salted Butter Caramel Swirl which was outstanding. Highly recommend this if you want to get some quality eats while out touring Scottsdale. Admittedly you will get fat from eating this but well worth it in my opinion. Service was friendly and great and will always put this on our list. will go back when in Scottsdale next time.

This place was busy for a Monday dinner hour. Tip: Take a number for service! I missed it when I entered and thought I was going to miss my chance at a cannoli. Luckily, I was able to snatch one and a creme brÃ»lÃ©e. The cannoli was overly sweet and felt dry eating through it. The creme brÃ»lÃ©e surprised me at how not sweet it was (which is a good thing!) The let down of the creme brÃ»lÃ©e is that that I know it's been sitting there for some time because the top doesn't crack as smoothly when it gets torched. It was meh, I would pass for another Bakery. Another tip: $5 minimum for credit card use.

PAGE'S HAS THE BEST SOFT SERVE IN THE STATE!!!! They offer a dairy free oat milk ice cream option, which is absolutely incredible. I got an arctic swirl made with the pistachio oat milk ice cream and cookie dough and it was phenomenal. The prices are great, especially compared to other ice cream joints around the city. The business gives off the perfect nostalgic feeling as you are surrounded with historical information of the business site and the history of the surrounding neighborhoods. Page's is the best local business and I would recommend it to anyone who is passing through Pittsburgh, or anyone who lives here and has not yet had the pleasure of trying their ice cream.

Once upon a time I would say that waking up early and heading to the local donut shoppe prior to opening, waiting outside discussing what indulgences we will enjoy as we waft in the delicious aroma sounded like a scene from some cute 80's or 90's romantic comedy. Well in a world where life inmates art, that is exactly the concept behind the now nationally recognized Donut Bar. I work in a hotel in Downtown San Diego, and people from around the country ask for this place, by name! With a line out the door all the time, arrive early and expect to wait, but don't worry, you will not me disappointed. Its like willy wonka drank a bunch of local craft beer and conceptualized some of these out of this world breakfast desserts. My suggestion is to buy at least 3: 1 to eat immediately. 1 to sit down upstairs and enjoy with some coffee. and 1 to give to someone else.

Here's how I found Jack Frost... I was coming back from a business trip and had been away from home for a few days. I couldn't wait to see my kids and wanted to get them a special treat. Before I even picked up my luggage, I found this gem on Yelp! I purchased a variety like German Chocolate, peanut butter, salted caramel and more. They were more like beautiful little cupcakes. I don't have a sweet tooth, but it was all I could do to keep my hands out of the box for my 40-minute ride home! My kids wanted to know when I was going out of town again! I can't buy donuts anywhere else now. Highly recommend.

I am proud to have this donut bar in Las Vegas! You guys are amazing! If you are looking for a really cool place with an amazing vibe and couple that with some of the most UNIQUE and TASTY Donuts found ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD! Then this is the place for you! May you continue to serve donuts in Las Vegas for next 100+ Years! I would rate this one 10 MILLION STARS!

10/10. I didn't know they have a milk in Vegas and I'm so happy I got to try it hear. I got the build it yourself pint and wow! Not like any icecream ive ever tasted. I'm trying to understand how you get a burst of extreme sweetness and it literally settles in one second and it's not that sweet anymore. Soooo different. Bizarre experience - I love it
They have changed exponentially since my last visit about 7 years ago. This place is fantastic! Glazed donut filled with strawberry ice cream ,

What else can I say that hasn't been said already? I'm weirdly glad that they're not closer ( in fact very far away from me) because I'll be there every day = gaining tons of weight! My baby loved the mango lassi flavor! So much he did the sign for "more " for the first time at the store:) I do want to try the bacon flavor....so a trip soon is in order

I've been wanting to try this ever since our friends were raving about it, I thought it was a bit over rated and I said oh it's just another soft serve vanilla ice cream but Noooooooooo, as soon as you taste it, it's literally like eating cereal and milk! It's not too overly sweet and doesn't have any after taste! I kept eating here like 4 times a week, I didn't know I could do that, usually I get sick of too much dairy. I really am satisfied with this place! It also has so many other things, like crack pie and the birthday cake, they also have gluten free options which I loved coz I'm also gluten free! The crack pie is phenomenal, it's a buttery brown sugar crust, very yummy! It's so good! I had to come for more again for 4 days straight since we were in Vegas, also the birthday cake is this white cake with sprinkles on top! It's also not overly sweet which is good coz you really taste the cake! This is a must try for everyone and kids will love it too! Wish they had one in seattle though! Wishful thinking!

Weekend of firsts! Happened into this place because we tried the sushi burrito place in the same strip mall. Young lady explained the options so went with Minion's Treat (ice cream, Frosted Flakes, banana)...so good! Frosted Flakes are mixed into the ice cream along with banana. Whole think mixed together and topped with more flakes and few banana slices. Talk about decadent in a cup! Wife had the Thunder Buddies (Reese's Puff, banana mixed in and topped with almond slices, bananas and Teddy Grahams). So yummy and fun concept!

I used to go to mary coyle many years ago and loved it. I tried this new mary Coyle. It was the biggest disappointment ever. For starts there are no menus to look at. I had to use my phone to look up the menu before placing my order. I ordered a sundae with hot fudge. The hot fudge was not hot and appeared as if it had been scraped from the bottom of a burned pot. It was terrible. When asked about the hot fudge, the sole employee resoonded "thats all we have". Needless to say i will not return nor would i ever recommend mary coyle to any of my friends.

It's actually been over ten years since I've bought anything here. My work used to require me to make annual trips here and I'd try a few of their offerings while staying at its host hotel the Venetian. I remember it being right by the room elevators adjacent to the breakfast restaurant and the theater (Phantom of the Opera was playing then) as mentioned in the title. My choices then were likely almond or chocolate croissants and they obviously weren't memorable... croissants are meant to be eaten warmed. Recently, a friend who was in Vegas for work kindly presented me with this familiar box (yelp.com/user_local_phot¦). Since I was a little hungry after a Warriors' game, I couldn't wait to try one, so apologies for the less-than-artistic photo of my treats(yelp.com/user_local_phot¦). I can't remember the flavors as my generous friend did not list them, leaving me to do challenge my taste buds/palate. I believe they were chocolate, strawberry, pistachio, coffee or mocha, lemon, and a mystery flavor. They lasted two days as I didn't want to spoil my figure by devouring them in one sitting... again, round is a figure. My local source for satisfying my macarons craving is on Pine and Fillmore but sadly, after their revamp, they no longer make them (now offering choux instead). Haven't searched bakeries in the City for these French treats so can't say who has the best in the City these days; the last local shop I tried was probably the one inside the Ferry Building. Yes, their main and flagship store is only about an hour away, but it shows how much I get out of town these days. Thanks to the generous friend who shared the love (= sugar) from her Vegas trip with me. Hope I get to choose my treats next time I'm there.

Bouchon bakery is kind of hidden behind an escalator past the Venetian food court. We grabbed a couple of their signature macarons, an apple croissant and an americano. My wife is not the biggest fan of Apple pastries but I love them :) Props to Mr. Keller for creating an apple pastry that even my wife was raving over! It was seriously amazing. Minus 1 star for the macarons not being fresh like they were in Yountville.

The BEST ice cream you will ever have! I was born and raised in Youngstown - so Handles has always been my go to. Now I won't even eat Handles because it doesn't compare! The wild berry crumble is SO good!

I have walked by this place for almost a year and never even thought about going in to try it until I saw a picture of a couple of the ice cream sandwiches from here on the Offline app. The one picture I saw was of a strawberry shortcake ice cream sandwich, and then I knew I had to give this place a try. I'm so glad I did! I recently had a friend in town so it gave me the perfect reason to try something local and new, and who doesn't love ice cream. We went in around 9pm, and business was boomin! The weather was beautiful, so lots of people were out and about, and the place had good vibes. My friend tried one of their donut ice cream sandwiches, and it looked delicious! I ended up trying one of the R U Cereal macaroon ice cream sandwiches, because I couldn't pass up the opportunity to have ice cream and lucky charms! Both were delicious. This place is a must try if you're in the university area!
Bouchon's macaroons are amazing! Had one of each and loved every one. TKO homemade Oreo cookie was great. Interesting flavor. Not for everyone. Would have loved a glass of milk with that one.

My boyfriend and I just visited here just at the end of our trip to Arizona and it was absolutely incredible. We were greeted by a gentleman who allowed us to try as many of the flavors as we wanted- which all tasted great. We found out that he was the owner and he seemed really passionate and excited his business which was really sweet. The ice cream itself was incredible! They have an ice cream sandwich that's made with a donut which is amazing. Unfortunately they don't sell pints online or I would surely order! You should definitely stop by if you're in the area- it's something you won't want to miss!

Hands down the best ice cream in the world. Seriously. We move a lot and always make a point of finding the best ice cream and this outshines them all. Get the four scoop sampler and try the graham canyon and whatever else suits your fancy. You won't regret it and will probably find yourself buying a pint to take home like we do!

Looking for a place that delivers creative and delicious donuts?! Look now further because this is your place !! I hope they bring this a little closer to the strip because that would be a game changer. I went to brunch a couple of miles away from this location and thought - I'm on vacation ... I need donuts. This place did not disappoint. Make sure you get there early if you want a lot of options because this small joint is so popular that it sells out quickly. Oh and guess what ?!?! They have vegan donuts tooooooooo and a selection of coffee to pair your sweet donut with. I actually tried a cinnamon roll and it was the bomb dot com. Okay moment of truth, I actually ordered from here two more times during my stay from Uber Eats because they were just that good. And guess what else ?! My favorite donut actually turned out to be the began creme brÃ»lÃ©e!!! Please visit this place and try as many donuts as you can- you will leave stuffed but wanting more.

This place is amazing! My little family and I were visiting Las Vegas and Yelp this donut shop. Based on the great reviews I told my husband that we got to try this place. When we arrived we were greeted by all their friendly staff. The ladies also asked if my children wanted to take a complimentary cookie monster donut. They gave us one for each of my kids. I thought that was very sweet of them. They even went the extra mile to give my kids each a balloon. We ordered a french toast donut, nutella filled donut, the birthday oreo donut, and maple bacon donut. Let me tell you these donuts were so delicious.
