The service here is great. The guy who helped me greeted me with a smile, and was very pleasant and helpful. This isn't a walk in restaurant. You walk up to the counter and place your order from their selection of desserts that include cookies and whole cakes. The birthday cake is their most famous cake and the only one the sell by the slice. The birthday cake costs a hefty $16. I got it, and I regret it. It did not live up to the hype. It was a decent cake. It wasn't bad, but for the price I expect more. The milk they soak it with makes it similar to a tres leche (but not quite as wet). It's on par with a grocery store cake at best. I'm a cake connoisseur and i've had far better for far less. Maybe the cookies are better. But don't waste your time or money on the birthday cake. Just go for the cute appearance and nice service.

While it can be quite difficult to find due to the fact that these mega hotels are so huge that you can literally get lost for a solid 10 minutes and still be somewhere in the middle of the hotel. However, once you have found this place you can rest assure that it was well worth it. We have tried multiple thinks here from the macaroons to the almond chocolate croissant. Maybe because we had worked up an appetite finding this place. But our favorites were the vanilla cold brew for drinks and the almond chocolate croissant.

The baguettes are good and they'll have a food item or 2 I can eat. The drinks and coffee are nice plus they stay open 24/7. When I say 24/7, like remember the snow storm the last couple of years, well d@mn it, they were open. They should get 5 stars just for that!
They have a huge choice for desserts. Perfect place for a nice cup of coffee and dessert.
Sooooo freaking great. Butter pecan ice cream, vanilla, hot fudge, butterscotch, whip cream n cherry. Nuff said.

The cookies are amazing. The same can be said for the lemon sunny. The galettes though, are gross. Slightly overdone on the outside and not quite done enough on the inside. The choco/pb/banana mix is great in concept, but this execution is not good. Stick to the cookies.

I like Amelie's. The food is great. The coffee is great. The atmosphere is great. That said, they need to get their sh!t together with the line. It's slower than a TSA security check. I just want a cup of coffee. Why do I need to stand in line for half an hour while the person behind the counter patiently explains all 300 f'ing macaron flavors to every individual in line in front of me? Oh, look! The cashier is just standing there, staring off into the distance, thinking about how much more rad the world would be if Kathleen Hanna were running for president while the infinitely patient person at the pastry counter runs through the macaron flavors AGAIN! Please, for the love of all that's good and decent, make a dedicated coffee line. And maybe make some little signs or something for the macarons? Amelie's is an awesome place and I'm glad they're killing it but often enough I find myself not going because I know it's gonna be a hassle. The macarons are great, by the way. When you hear them listed 200 times and find yourself spending the better part of an afternoon, slowly inching past them, more often than not you end up getting a couple. Gee, I wasn't hungry when I got in line. I just wanted coffee. How did I end up with these six macarons, a lemon tart and a f'ing miniature chocolate cake? I just wanted coffee! I JUST WANTED COFFEE!!!

This place makes homemade fresh ice cream with unique blends everyday, along with homemade waffle cones. Five stars isn't enough of a rating. I'd easily give it six. I chose the Taro and Rhubarb Streusel flavors. They also serve dairy free options (they had four at this particular time). I'm from Utah and I can only wish that we had a replica of this place where I lived. Super friendly staff, superior customer service by Jesse (not the Mason Jesse), and easy transactions. The ice cream is classic and beyond delicious. It is not too sweet and has the right amount of flavor to satisfy your palette. The atmosphere is a combination of nostalgic, traditional, and trendy.

The French bakery of note in Charlotte, this place offered a robust selection of pastries, which I bought to share. They were very strong on nuts, which make for filling sugar bombs that at least have some nutrients in them. The person working there didn't quite get the pastries right that I pointed to, but with others waiting behind me in a socially distant line, the difference between chocolate and hazelnut wasn't something I wanted to make a hassle over. The place does offer curbside pickup; their current model is all takeout with no indoor or outdoor seating. The nutty pastry I took from the pack was certainly delicious enough to be worth the stop.

The selection of flavors that constantly change. The concrete and blizzards, shakes and Sundays. Fresh backed cookies. Tokns of topping to choose from. A super retro old school wall of old kickass candy that has Kong gone been forgotten about I am obsessed with this place and go about 4-5 times a week
Great and unique concept! This place is worth trying but I thought the flavors of the ice creams and macarons were just OK. Overall though, A for effort. Lots of potential

Positive, they let you sample as many flavors as you want. The almost famous cup was good but if you have tried the ice cream and macaron sandwhich at pho43 they dont compare. No marshmellow there but the quality of the macaron is much better. This place is not worth going out of your way for but its still decent. If I didnt have something better to compare it to I would have given 4 stars.
By far the best cakes I've ever eaten. Each had its own unique decoration and taste! Definitely dine in if you can. Take a look at all the cool details and how perfectly curated each piece is.

One of my favorite places in Charlotte. Great for studying, relaxing, or hanging with friends. They have great food, great coffee, and great atmosphere. But the thing I like the best? They sell Sprecher sodas, which this Milwaukee girl didn't know she could get outside of Wisconsin. Plus, it's open 24 hours a day! What's not to love?!

I visited Carlo's Bakery while in Las Vegas last weekend. The desserts behind the counter looked scrumptious so I ordered one cannoli and a lobster tail. The desserts were a disappointment. I won't be back!
The ice cream was delicious, the flavors were creative without being too wacky, and the portions were generous.

There's been a lot of debate as to what the best ice cream shop in Phoenix is, I don't think Churn is it, but they have my favorite ice cream, hands down. Their cookies and mint ice cream is absolutely delicious. My go to order is 2 scoops of it in a waffle cone, in a bowl. Other places may have a better variety of ice cream, but Cookies and Mint is 5 stars!
Hhtgh Gia}/11aqqqq-- The donut bar .. These are the BEST donuts in the entire world .
I really liked all the chocolate things I've tried. The brownie was delish and the little chocolate hazelnut thing. The other pastrys were pretty good as well. Great cup of coffee too!

I came here on a Sunday afternoon wanting to try the carrot cake cookie but they were all sold out by 1pm. The guy working there said people buy them up 5 or 6 at a time. I guess that means they're pretty good. So, I tried one of their chocolate chip cookies -- huge, about the size of 4 normal sized cookies. The flavor was good, not intensely sweet, but I've had better. It could have used larger chunks of chocolate. I also tried the TKO (Thomas Keller Oreo). Loved it! Although is was bordering on being too sugary and sweet, the chocolate cookies were soft and chewy (but not too dense) and the creme was fabulous. The place is a little tough to find, but it's worth the trip.

Cute place with lots of treats; I'm a big fan of DC Cupcakes so I had to try Sprinkles to see if they were just as good or better.....oh and to see the Cupcake ATM lol¼ I chose the Chocolate Marshmallow cupcake....it was yum, taste like a "ho-ho"...id eat it again and try their other flavors with no issues...Sprinkles is comparable to DC Cupcakes taste wise but they are a little pricier...hence the 4 stars.
Ice cream was amazing! Chocolate chunk. Drove all the way to Summerlin and the ice cream was worth it. Very friendly too and not too pricy.
Worth the hype, delicious ice creams with great flavor combinations. I love the following flavors: brown butter almond brittle, goat cheese with cherries and bramblecrisp.

This is one of my favorite bakeries on clt. It has such a hippie vibe to it and it's always crowded but the pastries are so worth the long line. I usually try to get in before 6 pm otherwise the line wraps the whole store. I love the napoleons! They are my favorite. The macarons are okay too, a bit pricey but to try doesn't hurt. Everything is sweet but not so overly sweet. A great little place to study with friends and enjoy the day just socializing while having sweet treats.

I came here because I wanted coffee. Brunch. Something sweet. Oh man, I loved it. The variety and options were unique and they all looked good. I had a hard time deciding what I wanted because I wanted all of it. I ended up choosing the half sandwich mushroom deauville, lavender cafe au lait, passion fruit macaron, and creme brÃ»lÃ©e. Cute cafe, wonderful selection. So good I went again the next day before heading back home!

I don't give 5 stars often. 1. This was open with no line about 3 on a Saturday. 2. They had honey lavender ice cream. 3. They had honey lavender ice cream 4. Did I say...okay, okay. They also had other awesome selections which we were able to sample. They were all good! . Donut ice cream sandwich! My wife loved it with the bourbon toffee crunch ice cream. They are all creamy and just the right amount of sweetness! Can't wait to go back. Must try!

This is by far the best ice cream I have ever had! My favorites are salted caramel truffle and the pretzel caramel ice cream. If I lived close to this place I would gain an extra 60 pounds. It's that good for real lol! I won't eat any other ice cream here in Las Vegas. Hands down #1 in my book.

Went for a surprise date in Cleveland the other weekend: I wanted to get something new to try and I heard rave reviews about this place. Thankfully it was quiet when we arrived so we didn't have to wait. Most of the donuts had already sold, so there wasn't many left. After carefully deciding of 6 different donuts we took them with us to eat over the course of the next few days. Let me tell you, folks: delicious. Not overwhelmingly sweet or oily, the flavor is honestly really good. I think lemon lavender was my favorite: sweet, with a tart aftertaste and even almost savory! I was a big fan of all of these. I'm not sure if the business is black-owned, but the staff was all Black and I am honestly HERE for more black-owned vegan businesses coming about! Give this place a try, PLEASE.
Great ice cream...orange blossom is the best. Today had Turtle Sundae is to die for pecans are so fresh it is amazing.

I love pumpkin season and especially when I can get to Sprinkles! As I was walking to dinner along the Linq Promenade I saw Sprinkles and their ice cream shop next door, which always puts a smile on my face. It was late at night but I stopped in anyway to see what they had left. Thankfully, they had my favorite two flavors. My go to is always the red velvet cupcake but the pumpkin gives it a run for its money. The red velvet is perfect, one of the best versions of this flavor that I've tasted. And the pumpkin? It has just the right amount of cinnamon, spice, and pumpkin flavor. Sprinkles has nearly mastered the cupcake and their consistency across stores around the country is impressive. Each time I bite into one I'm amazed by how fresh, moist, and soft it is. The only two things I don't love are the icing, which is a little thick for my liking, and the prices...of course.

Let's be honest, it's pretty hard to screw up ice cream...but you can tell Honey Hut definitely is good quality. But beyond that, this place is definitely a staple of the Old Brooklyn area and a legend in it's own right. I only go once every couple of years but it definitely never disappoints. Best part about this particular location is it's outdoor seating area.
not very impressed. 12 for 3 cupcakes. not too bad for vegas but the variety sucks qnd the cupcakes were dry and bland to me. my son asked if they were sugar free. fell apart and hard to eat

So this place legit earns all of its amazing reviews! Really fun eclectic interior, from both the furniture to the chandeliers! But the main showpiece is obviously the treats! It was hard to pick only two things, but the almond tea cake and the raspberry lemon tart were both to die for. Hands-down everything you would expect and then some! With some good coffee you'll feel like you're in Paris, even if just for a few minutes.

No cap this place is bussin. That's it. Bring your friends because Novel never misses. Make sure you get the donut sandwich though. The waffle one is not amazing ( not bad but not game changing like the donut). YOU HAVE TO TRY THE LAVENDER-something. I forgot the name but that ish phenomenal

My wife and I love Sweet Republic. It's a must try for our out of town guests. I stop by frequently and get pints on my way home from work. So many flavors, such variety. I also work in food service and am picky about health codes (can't help it) and I've never had any problems with SR! Side note: Too many people on here complaining about the prices. If you're willing to spend $5 on coffee, but not on the best ice cream in town, there is something wrong with you.
Great coffee and baked goods. Also a nice place to get some work done outside of the office.

To be completely honest, I wasn't impressed or blown away. I wish I would've ordered a cupcake and left the rest at the door. Unfortunately I didn't even order one of the cupcakes. I came here participating in small business Saturday and Pittsburgh Shopopoly. We purchased a container of cookie dough and brownie batter and one of the hot chocolate balls/bombs. The hot chocolate ball broke before we even got home. That was unfortunate but not entirely their fault. Although packaging doesn't give much support in preventing this from happening. The cookie dough and brownie batter tasted like butter and brown sugar. There really wasn't any other flavor. I've had other edible cookie dough brands and did not have this experience. There wasn't much of a flavor distinction between the two separate flavors in the container regardless of one being "cookie" dough and one being "brownie" batter. The service received was okay. The girl working had little knowledge of the days intended event of Shopopoly and we didn't receive the advertised free chocolates with purchases. Maybe we missed a detail about spending a specific amount but either way, the employee didn't have a clue about it. Cupcakes looked absolutely to die for but I've seen other great cupcakes around the city. I don't intend on returning as there are so many other options for sweets and baked goods.

This is my favorite place for ice cream in Phoenix! Carefully made, super creamy, and delicious! AND, the people who work here are very nice, and know what's special about the produce. AND... waffle and donut sandwiches!! Try the spiced pear!

This place is retail at its lowest. Saturday night here with a huge line. They had one person behind the bakery desk who was singing along while 20+ guests are waiting. Clearly nobody understands the importance of expediting the long line. Terrible. Where is the manager on duty?

Jeni's in south end is a MUST to end the night. It's my go-to dessert stop when I'm around the town. What I enjoy about Jeni's is that is they have dairy-free options for people like me . There's time where they have more options than other times, but the Texas Sheet Cake is always an option! It's chocolatey, delicious, smooth and has cake chunks inside. SO GOOD! The Local Scoop is my other ice cream shop in Charlotte with dairy-free flavors I can enjoy, but after giving Jeni's a few shots, I think this one one my heart over. Despite the long line, it goes by fast and gives you time to think what flavor you want to taste. Yes, they let you taste the flavors before you order since some of the flavors are out the of the usually, especially like Goat Cheese and Cream Puff. Jeni's has two other locations as well, and also have pints available in stores. That shows how good it is. I think the price of ice cream is pretty high, but it's worth it.

Don't want to go to the restaurant but still want a chocolate croissant? Well here you go. After walking off our brunch, we headed here for a snack to go as we made our way back to LA. I got my requisite croissant, but what caught my eye is their homemade nutter butters. Which are really two large cookies with a creamy peanut butter filling. Basically a large peanut butter cookie sandwich, which tastes just like a Nutter Butter! Bouchon, you've proven your worth. You know your pastries and I will be back to put more of them in my mouth.

What a horrible set up to an ice cream shop. They have a doorman to let you in. A doorman! Seriously?! It's ice cream, not a club. Once inside, the staff is very confused about who has been helped, their area to work in is incredibly tiny so they are constantly running into each other and moving quite slow. Then once you finally get your ice cream, the cashier has to call you up by name to take your money. That last part seems easy since the door guy only lets about 7 people in at a time, but apparently its brain surgery. Definitely not worth the ice cream or frozen yogurt or whatever it is. Go to Cold Stone or buy some at a grocery store or make some yourself (even though I have no idea how to do that). Any of those options would be better than paying for some here.

Tried the union utopia and blue moon flavors (both flavors of the month!) and they were creamy and light. The union utopia had stripes of caramel and peanut butter, which was a traditional combination that mixed together well. The blue moon was reminiscent of cotton candy so a little too sweet for me, and left classic blue-stained teeth. Wish there was seating in the shop itself but we opted for the open lounge area.

85 degrees is always a good spot to curb any of your doughy sweet bun cravings. This location is hard to beat, situated in the heart of Spring Mountain is a newly developed plaza. Inside is clean, organized and spacious...I could only wish the full establishment was open to experience. Of course, because of our friend COVID, all the buns are individually packaged which is not the same experience we are normally used to. For going towards the closing minutes, there was still plenty of buns to choose from. And with that said let me tell you which ones I picked... Strawberry Cream Tart (3.5/5) - The tart was a good size, just that perfect mouthful. Simple enough to curb your fruit tart craving, but not enough wow to give the full 5 star review. The crust was tasty and had a good crunch, maybe a little too much if I were to be picky. Strawberries were perfect rip with the perfect amount of glaze. Wish I had a couple more strawberries to compliment the abundantly cold cream. I did appreciate the nice little box they used to package the individual tart. Sugar Cream Cheese Brioche Bun (4/5) - this bun is soft, airy yet doughy. The cream cheese is the perfect compliment with the hard sugar sprinkles. Probably something I imagine pairing with coffee/tea, not so much a dessert bun. Coffee Milk Butter Bun (4.5/5) - nice airy, soft, chewy texture. The flavors hits you on all side. Sweet, savory, with a espresso follow up. Good amount of filling and the chocolate chips are always fun. Ideal treat for the coffee lover. Strawberry White Chocolate (5/5) - if you like that old school strawberry shortcake flavor, this is it. Barely has a white chocolate taste. Bun it's soft, fluffy and buttery. Definitely would be my first pick of buns. Taro Swirl Bun (4.5/5) - If you ever imagined a perfectly baked bun, this is it. The bun has a nice crisp top layer married to a nice fluffy body encompassing a sweet taro custard. If you're a taro lover, you will love this. And if you're not a taro lover, this will make you a believer. Chocolate Croissant (3.5/5) - just your standard chocolate croissant. No eventful "wow" presence. The dough is a solid buttery croissant but I'd only call it a step above the ones from Starbucks. Would I get it again? Probably, but not any of my top 5 choices. Overall a 4.9 so I'm rounding up to an easy 5-stars. I'm happy and so is my stomach.

Amelie's is such a fantastic little bakery. I am writing this review having eaten something from Amelie's in NoDa 5 times, but never stepping inside once. My girlfriend has stopped by and gotten me macarons from Amelie's a few times before and they have been nothing but amazing every single time. Even the weird flavored ones that I haven't enjoyed (birthday cake, cotton candy), you can tell they're made perfectly and if you were a fan of the flavor, you'd be EXTREMELY satisfied, I guarantee it. The macarons are just that good. If I were to recommend three I would say 1) pistanchio, 2) raspberry, and 3) salted caramel. I don't even LIKE salted caramel but somehow it is stupid good. The only other thing I've had here was a bacon, egg, and cheese on a croissant that was DELICIOUS. I'm not sure why I haven't gone back for another but it's something I need to do in the immediate future. I know my girlfriend gets croissants, coffee, lemon spritzers, pie, and other things from there and she's always enjoyed everything she's purchased! I have nothing but good things to say about Amelie's. 5 out of 5 would go again and again.
I really enjoy Amalie's! They always have the best quality desserts that are not just delicious, super pretty too!! They also have AAAAAAMAZING coffee!!!!!
The chocolate is out of this world! Tried the bacon chocolate and pretzels they both were amazing!
Here to visit Cleveland and Mitchell's was highly recommended. They did not disappoint! Best homemade ice cream ever!

I almost had a coronary when the girl in front of me ordered the 'Kanye Amen.' No one bothered to correct her, thankfully, because it was a line of about 8 deep, I was next and truthfully, the extra seconds of pleasantries weren't really going to make a difference. I mean if you go around calling pastry, 'Kanye,' there is no hope for you. So without comment or expression from either me or the cashier, I ordered my kouign amann--pronounced 'queen a-mon'--and it was awesome. The crunch from the caramelized layer of sugar that lined the bottom, the buttery sweet layers in between and the pastry with just enough give to make it soft yet light and decadent at the same time....I should've ordered this everyday; how often do you have Bouchon just an elevator ride away.

Pastries are better than most. They don't tell you to take the ticket you just see the line, however they will not take you if you didn't get the ticket first. Between the prices as well as the time you have to wait in line (total 1 hour 14min with packing and paying time) my money might be spent better elsewhere.
For the occasional sweet cravings - this is the place- expensive but, definitely worth to go there. The varieties what you get and what you can try is simply amazing. You will not be disappointed.

hire more help! line is ridiculous every night, you are losing customers because of this. you need someone taking orders, someone scooping, someone doing toppings. you serve ice cream how hard can it be to be fast??

One of my favorite places in Cleveland! - Probably due to the fact that it's impossible to have a bad experience here! Whether it's ice cream or ramen season the flavors are always amazing. A great small business that is conscious of their community. Key Words: CHURRO AND MACARON ICE CREAM SANDWICHES! Get a side of churros! They are made to order, perfectly crisp and chewy every time.

Love this place! Great place to relax and read or study or chat or just surf the web on your computer or iPad. Food is great only gripe is how crowded it gets but that's just testimony to how good the place is! It's open 24/7 which was a tremendous help being a single mom who was in nursing school!

Always a treat! Great service- your one stop shop to soothe your sweet tooth. I always enjoy a good Cookie Monster, but just be prepared for your mouth to be blue the rest of the night. Give Novel a try for your next dessert stop.
I'm just not into so so pastries , treating your help badly and spending too much money and not getting a seat.

Took over an hour to get some okay cookies. It's not the product although just okay but the service. Only two people helping customers. Sure buddy could afford a little more help. As my wife stood in line I watched the operation behind the counter. OMG one guy waited on approximately 4 customers in an hour as he walked around lost and took over 10 minutes to put on some latex gloves. The cashier leans on the counter when she rings something ever 5 minutes. Get some more help and upgrade your staff they are awful.

OMG! I love 85C!! This place is always busy and there is a reason for that! Every single item I have gotten here was outstanding! Be ready to stand in a line at any time of day here. It's worth the wait!
Great little ice cream shop with old school candy and toys on the inside. Friendly staff, super clean and amazing treats!!

Everytime I visit Churn, I get to re-live my childhood! Super cute ice cream parlor that carries most of your favorite childhood toys + candies! The staff are always friendly right when you walk in. I'm sold on their Vietnamese Coffee ice cream! I've tried other flavors that they carry, but nothing compares to their coffee ice cream. I love taking out-of-town family and friends here because it is such a fun and quirky parlor. The only problem I have is that parking is limited and I always find myself circling their side lot for parking.. but when I do find parking, it's worth the wait for great ice cream!
Some of their options are strange, but they're always well made and delicious. A bit pricy but definitely worth it. Try donuts with their peanut butter whip mix and chocolate frosting.

I was craving something sweet and came across this cute bakery with many sweet treats inside. I can't remember the exact name of the pastry bought, but it was filled with whipped cream with powdered sugar on top. I also bought a strawberry cheesecake.

LOVE this place. Very European (as I am told). Very laid back, friendly, artsy, community driven place. No worries if you are counting calories! They have elegant bite sized treats that won't wreck the count, so enjoy. I often enjoy a pastry and coffee when I visit. My average length of stay is 3 hours. I'm either working , meeting friends, reading or writing.

This place is amazing to say the least. So many french options, so little time, and not enough money :( Their cheese danish, chicken and waffles, and most breakfast items are the most popular. They cook great lamb and will leave you with a full stomach wanting to come back the next meal. Drinks are amazing Location, atmosphere, service, and music are all amazing. The prices are worth what the food is. There's almost nothing wrong with this place. Extravagant in every which way. Go here and tell me if you don't want to come back. Boucon does french food to perfection. It's all authentic baby

Came to Villani's to get some sweets after lunch. The establishment allows 2 customers in during COVID. Staff is extremely knowledgeable and helping. The place is really clean and smells exquisite. Gilbert assist me and he was really nice and provided a great recommendation. Will return soon!!!

Loved it! Ever since watching the show on TLC I have wanted to try their things but they were located on the other side of the country. We went a litter overboard with pastries but I have no regrets! There are a ton of people there so be sure to get your ticket quickly so that you are not waiting too long. It was about 20 minutes from the time we got the ticket till we got what we ordered... not to shabby for a place this popular!

Overall 4/5: Nice for a little break to cool off while walking about the Linq in Vegas. Dessert 4/5: Yummy and warm. Portion was okay. Both the ice cream and brownie were dense, kind of hard to eat. Still delicious though! Environment 4/5: Small inside, but great for a little pit stop. Nice and cool inside. Limited tables, but they free up pretty fast. Service 4/5: Fast and friendly service. Didn't take long for us to get our order taken even though the cashier was also making the desserts. Thank you Ghirardelli!

Have been wanting to trying this place for a while! Came on a Thursday night and there was a pretty long line, but it moves quickly. Luckily we found a parking spot. I got the Nancy B Chocolate Fudge Sundae! Wow, was it huge! The chocolate chip cookie was nice and warm and they did not skimp on the fudge. I truly enjoyed every bite! They have so many options to choose from, so I know I will definitely be back. My friend got an arctic swirl and enjoyed it as well. Their portions are huge, so come hungry! Overall, a great place to satisfy your sweet tooth craving! Prices are super reasonable as well!

So very disappointing and not up to Bouchon standards! My family and I have been to Bouchon Bakery in Yountville California many many times, and this Las Vegas location is inferior. We are not quite sure why they aren't keeping up with quality control, but after going out of our way to get pastries there on our one day in Vegas, we felt obligated to write a review. We had butter croissants and almond croissants, and they were all stale and awful. They seemed to be day old at least. We have not only been to Bouchon Bakery many times in California, but we have also eaten at Bouchon Bistro in Yountville for various special occasions. We have never been disappointed there, and have always loved our meals. Perhaps the Bouchon Bakery in Vegas is under different ownership?
The quality is so good. The downside is the wait, and they get busy sometimes, but they're nice here and the flavors and quality of the ice cream are worth it. We're addicted now!

It's hotter than blazes outside so naturally I needed to try the ice cream place that everyone raves about. I was told by many people to try the chocolate chip cookie sundae so that's what I did. And wow! First off it's huge. Definitely was not expecting that. I knew right away that I would not be able to finish it all at once. Second, it was less than $7 which is awesome in my book especially because it's too big to eat in one sitting. Third, it tasted like heaven. I know how busy this place can get so I tried to go closer to opening time and there was still a line. Will definitely be back and can't wait to try more things!

Dropped by Churn on a Sunday night around ~8:00 pm and was met with a bit of a crowd/line. It went by quickly so yay! I opted to go for the vietnamese iced coffee flavor on a sugar cone while my friend got the same thing in a cup~ We decided to sit down in the seats in the front and chow down on our ice cream and boy was it good! My ice cream had a great coffee flavor with the perfect texture and the sugar cone was awesome too! The interior of the store itself is really cute and there's even seating in the back~ This place is located right next to Windsor and across the street from Federal Pizza so definitely swing by after eating at either of those places! There is parking in the front and on the side so you should be set if you drive over! When the night wound down and they had to shut down the outside patio, they were super nice and gave us cookies as a nice "sorry we have to ask you to leave" gesture -- which we super appreciated! Definitely going to come back from some sweet treats in the future~

I just ate a bowl of cereal in the form of ice cream. I was very curious about Milk Bar especially because their ice creams look pretty good in pictures. I'm glad I tried it but probably won't eat it again especially with the $6 price tag!

Milk Bar is Located in the Cosmopolitan on the Las Vegas Strip. This is a small counter that serves some sort of soft serve, cakes and cookies. The thing that is popular are the Milk Quakes. The Milk Quake has added broken dessert added to it. Desserts are very EXPENSIVE$$$$$$$$$$$ A 6in Malted Milk Chocolate Cake will set you back $56.00! The Milk Cake cost $10.00 (2017 pricing). We love watching Master Chef and we like Pastry Chef Christina Tosi so we thought we wanted to try something from Milk Bar while we were here. The person at the counter seemed helpful and we tried the Strawberry Corn Milk Quake. It might not be Milk Quake's Fault but when we were there they don't provide a counter or any seats for you to enjoy your treat. I note I have only been here once and have only tried the Strawberry Corn Milk Quake ($10.00). The frozen confection was served to me very melted and tasted sour like yogurt. It didn't take like strawberries. The milk quake also had lumps of broken corn bread in it. Both of us thought this Milk Quake tasted HORRIBLE! Two taste and the Milk Quake was in the trash. The Milk Quake was high in price but turned out to be very low in Calories. :(

We ordered the Cereal Milk Soft Serve with cornflakes and two other shakes. I fed my 2 year old son the Cereal Milk Soft Serve at 12:30 am. He woke up at 5am vomitting. He threw up three times since this morning. We are on our way back to California to bring him to Urgent Care. I also noticed this morning the guy handing out the orders really smell funky. Severe bad body odor. Should they be putting some attention to their staff's hygiene specially they are handling food. Traumatic First time experience here. Not coming back for sure.
It was morning delight. Chocolate almond croissant and cream cheese danish are Fresh, crunch and perfect sweetness.
Had a ball I truly enjoyed it all, and the wall of cassette tapes is also great touch

After the Yelp Hash House event all my Yelp friends wanted to check out Sprinkles for dessert. I'm not really a sweets person, but I knew Joel would want something. It's kinda confusing because they have a separate line for cupcakes and separate line for ice cream. Both lines can merge if it's busy and it's hard to tell who's in what line. They also only have certain flavors on certain days when it comes to their ice cream. Since it was super hot out we picked a small scoop of Triple Chocolate. It set me back about $4. The taste of it wasn't that great. For that kind of money I'd rather have gone to Yogurtland. They do have a cupcake ATM that is a cool feature. The staff was friendly and it's not their fault they are gouging people for subpar ice cream. Do yourself a favor and skip this place and save the money. I sure wish I had.

On my very first visit to this Carlos Bakery in Las Vegas inside The Grand Canal Shopes at The Palazzo/The Venetian. The wait to get in was really no wait at all because I came around the slow part of the day. I got a cannoli which I had always wanted to try. It was extremely delicious and fairly priced too. I also purchased A souvenir metal coffee mug. I love the food their and next time im in the area im going to come back for more for sure. If you want awesome desserts that's delicious in your stomach and good on the wallet come to Carlos Bakery the worlds greatest bakery.
Gilded. pretty on the outside, bland and cardboard on the inside. I'm talking w out their pastries here.
The crack pie is no crazy delicious! I've been wanting to go to Milk Bar for a long time and it did not disappoint. Coffee was excellent and strong as well. Perfect for a late night sweet craving.

Customer service was good and the milkshakes were very tasty. It is a little expensive for my taste. I can get a larger milkshakes, with pretty much the same ingredients for less money other places. I cannot take points away for price though. Since it is a mom and pop shop, they have to make money.

My buddy was super disappointed when the mobile food location at the zoo was not open after our visit to the zoo so I jumped on yelp to find the closest location. My buddy swears that this is the best ice cream on earth so I'm down, I'm not big into ice cream so I imagine it will be just ice cream to me. The place is very tempting with so many interesting flavors and when I was asked what I want I said I need a minute to take it all in. My buddy went full on with two different scopes on a sugar cone that looked good but I really only wanted just a dish of one scoop and Mackinac island fudge would do because it's a flavor that I would not normally order. My first thought was that it was very soft and creamy with hard chunks of fudge and swirls of something softer with a caramel Ike texture and good but is it the best ice cream in the world, I don't know.

One of my favorite places to go! Whenever we are downtown, we make a point to stop here. Every flavor is great and change often, so ask for a sample before you order...or don't, I'm sure you'll love whatever you order!
Wow this place is good!! Try anything with the buttercream frosting .... it's perfect sweetness. And awesome back patio!

The peanut butter donuts are sooooooo good but now I think the cinnamon sugar-Carmel apple donuts are my new favorite. I ate it in the parking lot and automatically wanted to get more. They have a huge variety but get there early before all the good ones are gone! The new lady behind the counter is super friendly also.

I went to Fatty Daddy's last year and loved it!! Good ice cream flavors and unique cookie cup. I went back this year with friends and was so disappointed! The cookie cup price didn't change but the lady said the "menu changed". I got two tiny scoops and one cookie instead of two. Once my friends saw how small the portions were they didn't order anything. The flavors weren't as good this time either. I don't plan on going back! I can get a DQ blizzard for half the price and triple the ice cream. Don't waste your money!!

Ok, I am sure you are surprised to be seeing only 3 stars, but let me clarify. There stuff is downright yummy! However, their service is horrible...they are ridiculously slow and rude. Additionally, what's with the crazy hours? They close way too early. At the end of the day the yummy factor is outweighed by all the other factors so it will be a long while before I go back.

A restored, adorable building full of delicious ice cream flavors. Famous flavor: caramel fudge brownie (And you bet I got it.) The decor is girly and chic, and there are other great-sounding, chocolate-filled flavors such as peanut butter cup and chocolate fudge brownie. There are plenty of spots to sit, including a row of cute, colorful seats for little kids to sit in and look out the windows. This ice cream shop is also located on a trendy street with loads of food options as well.

Seriously good ice cream and customer service! I tried a few flavors (sweet corn, meyer lemon, peaches n' cream) before settling on one scoop of peaches n' cream and meyer lemon in a waffle cone and of course a toasted marshmallow on top! My boyfriend had the Toffee Banofi and it was fabulous. We will be coming again to get a cool treat soon!
Wow wow wow! What a great area at University area. A glazed doughnut filled with ice cream then deep fried?!! Wtf???? Why does it have to be soooo good! Well done, great area and a line out the door!

Handel's....Yum! My girlfriend and I ate here every Tuesday for $2 buck Tuesday and my husband brings home a quart or pint every other week or so. My absolute favorite is the coffee chocolate chip. I seriously can't get enough of it. Maybe a rewards card would be nice.

I always love this place. The consistency is on par. The desserts are just so good, you'll go back for more. Macarons are the best here, but really, everything is good. Every time I'm in NY, Napa, St Helenes and Vegas...I have to - seriously just have to go here.

You want it to be awesome. You have this building sense of excitement as you walk the Grand Canal Shops, like when you were a kid running down the stairs on Christmas morning. Then you get there.....and it's all downhill from then on. Now I grew up with these bakeries on Long Island, it's more than red and white string tied around a box that's makes an Italian bakery an Italian bakery. Buddy....what happened???? I watched my wife wait an hour for her ticket number to come up, and she had only 25 people ahead of her. Yes, you think a 3 minute wait time per customer is good right? But not when you have 3 workers on the counter assisting! Not only that, the bakery service area is about the size of a small Starbucks. Yet right across the hallway is Buddy's signature restaurant, and not only is it absolutely massive in size, it's absolutely dead inside. I saw 3 four tops, 2 bored hostesses, and a line cook that probably regrets applying for a job there. Why in the world did you not make a massive bakery area and a cute cafe type dinner place is beyond me. Seriously, you have Mario Batali just down another hall, and that's good damn Italian food. You're a baker Buddy, you should have just stuck with that and made a killing with a large, quick paced bakery cranking out our East Coast patisserie memories. Not a closet bakery with a huge show window with a guy filling cannolis. Remember, a fish may love a bird....but where would they live? BTW, the cannoli was great for what you can get on the West coast...but barely on par what I can get at my old bakery out on the Island.

The "custard" at this place is good but definitely not the best. I found their custards to be far too sweet and the serving size to be a bit small for the price. It's a good place to go to with friends after dinner or a movie but it's not any better than Culver's or Coldstone.

I'm in loveeeee! The people are amazing and so are the sweet goodies. I found out about Mason's Creamery from the night market and boy am I happy that I did. So far I've had the flan, black sesame, Vietnamese coffee and jackfruit (all great flavors btw). Can't wait to try more flavors along with the sandwiches. Coming back soon!

We've been a couple times now and there's some definite pluses and minuses to this bakery. Pros: Great location with a huge variety of baked goods, especially cheesecakes and harder to find Italian baked good options. The service is very prompt and friendly. Their hours are longer than nearby bakeries, making it great to snag a late night nibble or coffee to go. Cons: There really is no place, either inside or outside, to sit and enjoy your food. Since their business seems to be oriented to couples and families walking around the neighborhood for the most part, it's odd that there aren't benches or picnic tables at least to sit and eat. The quality of some of the items does not seem to be as consistent as Sunflour a few blocks away. For example, the cream/custard filling of certain items looks almost pudding-like and the cinnamon rolls sit open air, making them look dried out. The other issue is pricing. I'm sure since they are new to the neighborhood, this may hash itself out, but as of now, they are significantly ($1-2 per item) more than nearby bakeries (again, Sunflour, and Nova's). $4 for a muffin or chocolate chip cookie is hard to swallow (though the baked good not so much :-). Look forward to popping in every once in a while to see what's new, but will probably wait and see before making it the go-to bakery in the 'hood.

Absolutely Phenomenal. As an ice cream connoisseur, I can say that this is one of the best ice creams I have ever had. The Toffee Bourbon and Madagascar vanilla were absolute heavenly masterpieces. Stop by and you will not be disappointed. A bit hard to locate , but they are next nestled next to third space on Grand avenue.
Friendly as always, long line as always and good eats, too! Always feels like something special. However 14$ for a slice of cake with nowhere to sit is a bit bonkers. I'd stick with the other items.
Always good ice cream & they have something my choosy kids love. A very nice ice cream place in Old Brooklyn, close to Cleveland. Delicious!

We went in there before Christmas in hopes of finding a new type of bakery for this area. There seems to be a trend in town of cranky people working in bakeries. The lady at the counter seemed to be inconvenienced by our questions about the products. She didn't even know the types of cakes that were behind the counter. Secondly, we inquired about the "party room". Literally it's just a long table within the seating area for guests. They lost our business because they do not provide this service on weekends or after 530. The chocolate chip cookie was delicious the first time we came. The second time it was not the sane experience. The cupcakes were dry and flavorless. The chocolate cupcakes had a strong coffee flavor so the kids were turned off. They are very cute however. Hopefully the customer service will improve along with the products' consistency.

Went here after having dinner with a few friends to have some dessert. Had really high hopes based on the reviews. They had about a dozen different flavors of ice cream/frozen yogurt/sorbet. I tried about 5 flavors and only really liked 2...the pineapple and mango. My friend got the cucumber one which tasted okay but had a weird texture, more like shaved ice than creamy. Portions are pretty big and each it comes in one of those Chinese to go boxes. Each box comes with a fortune cookie as well. Overall, I probably wouldn't go again on my own.

Everything I've tried here has been wonderful, whether savory or sweet. Everyone working there is warm, kind, and efficient in my experience. What really makes everything shine is the perfection in the pastry. That said, the not-so-plain ham and gruyere croissant is one of my favorite breakfasts ever. Good coffee too.
Great gelato and great milkshakes. Stopped here after Din Tai Fung closed so some dessert and it was the real deal. I ordered the Oreo milkshake but everyone I was with had the gelato and loved it.

i walk in and there's a full grown big dog in the store. Since when? So dogs come before people? I am afraid of dogs, they super scare me and usually I have mace with me to keep animals away from me. This place is too small for patrons and dogs. Service dogs is one thing but this was not a service dog you could tell because it was not behaving and not following its owners commands. I had to leave immediately.

This location is nothing like the Irvine California location. My wife and I were given incorrect information by another employee and when we spoke to Nanz the lead/manager on duty about that issue she had zero customer service skills. Very short in tone and unprofessional. My recommendation is that corporate revisits training at the LV location if they expect to have repeat customers.

If going vegan tastes like this, why aren't we all vegan! I keep hearing about TVDC, today I passed it and made a quick decision to pull over and grab some. I've found a new favorite spot. TVDC is absolutely stunning inside. It's a small in and out space, but walking in feels so magical! Staff was so nice and helpful when picking out which to get. Often times with vegan remakes of food, things often times just feel "off" but not with these donuts. You seriously would have NO idea that these were vegan, which is what makes them to die for. My two favorites I tried were the tiramisu and the strawberry shortcake. Seriously, this place rocks. Go show love to this Female Owned, Black Owned, Cleveland Local, small business ASAP.

We stopped here for our sweet treat after dinner before heading back to our hotel, and the place was BUMPIN'. There was already a line snaking around the building by the time we parked, and we waited about twice as long here as at Primanti Brothers. No worries though; it moved quickly enough and everyone was in a pleasant mood. Our kiddo got birthday cake in a cup with mini M&Ms; one of us got a pistachio cone with rainbow sprinkles and the other got their celebrated chocolate chip sundae. The ice cream here is delicious: super thick and creamy and the perfect soft serve consistency. The pistachio had a bit of a chemical aftertaste, but that's how it sometimes goes with that flavor at these sorts of joints. The sundae was a bit too overwhelming for us, but it was good. Prices are fair. Page's is a charming (and obviously) popular spot, and what we liked most about it was that it seemed to attract characters from all walks of life, which is kind of rare to witness these days. Everyone was just wanting a frozen treat on a hot Memorial Day and it was kind of nice to be reminded that Americans of different races and classes can all enjoy the same thing without any vitriol. We'd definitely recommend this joint and might even come back later this week.

Melt Ice Cream Shop is a hidden gem located in the heart of Downtown Phoenix! They have a wide variety of different flavors + toppings and they specialize in "unusual" ice cream creations instead of the basic chocolate, Vanilla & Strawberry! They have Cookie Monster, Fruit Loops, Fruity Pebbles, Matcha Green-Tea, Churro, etc. They also top each ice cream with a fortune cookie + puts the ice cream in Chinese "to go" containers! I love doing their ice cream flights which comes in a cupcake tin so you get to have 6 different flavors and you get to try a little bit of everything! Definitely a must stop if you're exploring Downtown Phoenix and you have a sweet tooth craving!

Really, really great ice cream. Two of us each went with our own 4 scoop sampler. This is an incredible deal at $4.25, and they have so many flavors that it would seem impossible to choose just one. We tried the following: Coconut Cream Pie -- Awesome. Really the best coconut ice cream out there. Cake Batter -- Just cake batter ice cream. You can get this anywhere. Though, it does have a large amount of sprinkles. Chocoholic Chunk -- Tastes remarkably similar to Haagen Daz. Also good but not my favorite. Butter Pecan -- Tons of pecans. They really aren't cheap with their additives, which makes for great ice cream. Buckeye -- Real mini buckeyes make this a good ice cream. I could use more of a peanut butter swirl or something, though. Spouse Like A House -- Too malt flavored for me and not enough pretzel. This was my least favorite. Salted Pretzel Crunch -- So good. You have to love caramel and love chocolate covered pretzels. Luckily, I love both. Graham Central Station -- By far my favorite. I don't even like honeycomb, but it was perfect in this ice cream. This isn't the best location, and it would be cold in the winter to eat your ice cream outside, but I would definitely make the sacrifice in order to eat this ice cream.
Homemade marshmallows are to die for! Great creamy ice cream with plenty of choices. Go for the s'more ice cream sundae. Cute spot with some board games too
I've been going here for as long as I can remember!! Always friendly workers!! It's a Old Brooklyn staple!!

The cannoli cream was good the cookies were nothing special. The peanut butter cupcake was moist and very good, but need frosting in the center of the cupcake. If that was to happen then hand down a truly amazing eating experience.

Best coffee ice cream I have ever had, and everything else I tried was unique and delicious. The staff is top notch, the offerings are amazing, and the prices were very reasonable. It's super clean, and you can tell the family takes pride in every detail. I love the kids room. We will definitely be back.

Every time I went here, I spent at least 15 minutes holding up the line and getting in people's way just sampling ice cream and trying to decide which flavor(s) to get. They have a good mix of our traditional favorite flavors and the wacky ones that sparks your curiosity. Phoenix needs more ice cream shops like this one for people to escape the summer hell.

Honey Hut has some of the best ice cream around. I personally like it better than Mitchells (though I love Mitchell's too!). My favorite is the orange blossom ice cream. They have two scoops for $3 and three scoops is $4. It's a great price compared to other ice cream shops in the area. We've also tried the milkshakes and they are huge!!!

Ever since seeing pictures of all the Matcha Soft Serve treats, my husband and I decided we needed to try (just 2 short days later). We headed on over and did curbside pickup, which went seamlessly. We got each of our kids (toddlers) a swirled cone, Matcha and Black Sesame. They loved it! But these things are huge. The kids were eager to accept the challenge and spent maybe 40 minutes trying to eat the whole thing. I had to talk them out of it. My husband and I split the special, same swirl. I am absolutely won over. It was delicious. Black Sesame was probably my favorite part, along with the bean. Also ordered a chestnut cake for my husband. I took only one bite, trying to limit my indulgences, but it was heavenly. My husband has been dreaming about that cake ever since. All in all, everything was great. Check it out! We will be back.

Oh wow! Stop what you're doing right now. Just stop. Walk away. Get in your car and drive to Sweet Republic and order a Toffee Bonafi sundae. It will blow your mind. Best. Sundae. I. Have. Ever. Eaten. The contrast of flavors and textures...the salty sweet caramel...the crunchy toffee...the decadently rich ice cream...*drool*...this may be the best sundae you've ever eaten too.
Churn is definetly a popping place and the staff is always upbeat. My favorite ice cream is their 21 and over delight.
The zanzamint is probably the best mint-chocolate I have ever had...

Apparently this is Tom Hank's favorite place, how do I know that? I don't know, someone told me he visits the area and it's been declared so. Anywhos, I had never had a custard cup before, who knew in the college town of Champaign hid a custard cup place that would be as addictive as nicotine. I went 2 out of the 3 days I was in town visiting. Coffee Oreo Snowstorm on the first visit and Strawberry Shortcake Snowstorm the second trip, both costing a reasonable $3.75. Needless to say, I polished off both cups of custard each time. Supposedly 90% fat free, but I don't believe something that good could ever be fat free. The menu is huge and every combination flavor imaginable is up there, it kinda looks like a McD's Flurry, but NO IT DOES NOT TASTE LIKE ONE. It gets really packed on the weekends, I kinda want one right now, it gives me something to look forward to when I visit.
The donut was a little stale. Not hot or fresh as I would've expected it. The location was cute, restaurant was cute as well.
I bought some cookies, all of which were stale and extremely dry. It's such a disappointment that they sell goods past their sell by date. Perhaps this isn't the best location to visit

Just went in for coffee and really enjoyed it! Wait wasn't too long (for waiting to get inside and getting the drink) The coffee was smooth and not bitter at all. I'm a big fan of sea salt anything so I was very eager to try this.

I know they're super busy in the afternoon but everyone was asking if their drink was done or not and they totally forgot about my drink for 20 minutes and didn't even apologize for forgetting about it. Usually most companies would upgrade the size as an apology but they just gave me the normal size. it's super crowded too and for the first time I've come, I realized that i'm not coming from now on.
Excellent Macarons. Rankings (Best - Okay): 1. Chocolate 2. Coffee 3. Vanilla 4. Pistachio 5. Raspberry 6. Caramel The staff and the service is excellent. Must visit!

Been going to this place once a week, I've been there 5 times so far. My favorite is the honey lavender. I like their sorbets as well. Yummy! Also, make your own dough melt, so worth it. Brandon and Jennifer are just wonderful people, always friendly and constantly getting everyone to try all the flavors. Customer service can't get any better than that.

One of my favorite place to grab pastries and dessert. Grab a few pastries and sea salt coffee with boba. Tried the aussie pot pie with impossible meat and that for sure was tasty. The bread compliments the meat flavor. The sea salt coffee with boba was made exactly how I want it. It's a straight up coffee no cream beside the foam on top so you can definitely taste the coffee. They always have new pastries to try.
best ice cream hands down!!!! they even have a honey lavender ice cream and the cutest cat who roams the tables!!!
You can't go wrong here. Their ice cream and desserts are the best. You get huge portions and leave feeling satisfied.

Perks of being in Vegas is everything opens hella late. Who would think that I'd be able to satisfy my sweet tooth at 12am on a Thursday night with options that expand from the standard Mcflurry. I mean, we knew I was going to stop here for ice cream during this Vegas trip right? Regular hours are 9am to 1am, extended to 2am on Friday and Saturday. So on this rowdy thursday as we sat on a bench watching people getting boozy, we were getting hyped on sugar from Milk. More of a novelty stop if anything, to have the privileged right to declare that I've tried David Chang's infamous Milk Bar. Did it live up to expectations? Yes and no. Taste wise 100% tasty, soft serve was velvety smooth and the option to add cereal flakes on top of my Crack pie makes me feel like a kid again. Cereal milk was equally delicious, not as sweet as Crack Pie but more subtle. Prices are on the higher side, but it's the name that brings them in, cute Milk cups make up for the price right? Couldn't justify a milkshake at this hour but I'll be keeping my eyes wide open the next time I'm in the same Zip Code as another Milk Bar. Cereal milk $6 Crack pie $6 corn flake crunch $1
Ice cream good. Service not so much. The young lady that served us this evening was much more interested in continuing her conversation with her co-worker than anything I had to say.

The customer service here is shameful. I went in yesterday with a friend to finally try their ice cream and after asking for the manager all of the girls working were staring at me and gossiping. I sampled the red velvet, coffee fudge almond, salted caramel, and peanut butter cup. All of the flavors were under developed and a few didn't taste like the flavor advertised. The red velvet ice cream was basically an icy vanilla ice cream with red velvet cake sprinkled on top. I was expecting cream cheese ice cream with red velvet cake mixed inside or some type of rendition of a red velvet cupcake. The coffee almond fudge ice cream tasted like a very strong coffee with no hint of fudge or almond. Salted caramel was the best of the 4 but it was too sweet. We didn't want any of the ice cream but the cookies in the display case looked good so we ordered the snickerdoodle cookie. Instead of taking the cookie out of the case, the girl working took out a prepackaged cookie from below. The cookie was hard as a rock and was much smaller than the one in the display case. Everything about the cookie was suspicious so I returned the cookie and when I was getting my money back I saw ants crawling on the floor. I told the male manager at the register and he says " thanks, I know" with an attitude. If you know, why aren't the ants being cleaned up off the floor? Sprinkles Cupcakes employees are extremely rude and the ice cream is sub par. I will never step foot in this location again.
Not gonna lie, the donuts are good. However, the parking is terrible and how are people supposed to stop in and pick up donuts for the office if they don't open till 7am?
I should have known how good this bakery was by how busy it was on a Friday night. Delicious variety of Italian pastries and desserts. You won't be disappointed!

I did not like the canoli and the the tiramisu tasted like a lot of whip cream. We tried the red velvet and it was just okay. The brownie with walnuts were good but basically with what we got, I wasn't wowed enough to really go back. Carlos really must be a favorite on the east coast but at the prices of the bakery items I just wasn't impressed.

It's good ice cream. I'm just here to rate the rotation of flavors. New vegan ones! So I had to have my tried-and-true praline pecan. The pumpkin spice was too gordy and the autumn apple was an acidic big miss.

Color me impressed. I moved to the Valley two years ago from Manhattan. I have had the good fortune of living in some of the best culinary cities (Chicago, San Francisco, NY, Hong Kong) in the world. Needless to say almost everything has been a disappointment out here, until the day we tried this ice cream parlour. How refreshing to find quality artisanal products in a city populated with chain restaurants and unoriginal cuisine. For the first time moving here, I finally felt we found something that would do well anywhere in the world. This ice cream is that good and lives up to the hype. I have read so many glowing reviews about different establishments in the valley only to be disappointed, I was worried this would be another one of those experiences. Thankfully, this place lived up to all the hype. Exotic flavors aside, even their simple flavors are done incredibly well. Their belgian chocolate ice cream is one of the best chocolate ice creams i have ever had and their espresso ice cream is amazing. You can taste the freshness in all their ice creams. I can not wait to go back and try more of their flavours. One other thing I really loved about this place. As a mother of a 3 year old with a horrible peanut allergy, there are not many ice cream parlors you can go to because of cross-contamination with the ice cream scoops. (unfortunately, we have experience with this first hand.) Before going, I called ahead and spoke to someone who told me they are well aware of allergies and have a separate scoop and cleaning well for their peanut ice cream. I thought that was extremely considerate and a sign that they truly care about their customers. I highly recommend this place to anyone.

Absolutely loved this place. Drove 20 minutes to get here after hearing about the donut creation. It was perfect. I worked at a fancy artisan ice-cream shop for over 2 years and this had them beat by far. Our new favorite place

It was just okay. I had been to the Bouchon Bakery in NYC which was great, so I had high expectations. The pastries weren't memorable and there wasn't really a place to sit except for around the corner in the food court. I would go back to Jean Philipe at the Bellagio over this Bouchon Bakery.
Wow, this place was great! Loved the ice cream flavors and the shop was nice with board games to play. They will definitely need to move to bigger place!

With all the good reviews I thought this place has to be good. We thought we hit the jackpot when we went there for happy hour. We purchased a whole box of donuts for $10. They put as much donuts that they could fit into the box. We got a good selection of donuts but we were not wowed. This was shocking to me because the hubs loves donuts. It was just not our cup of tea.

Honey Hut: a staple of my child that I blame for my ice cream addiction to this day. 10-15 flavors of 'hard' ice cream (by hard, I mean that the ice cream can be packed into a cup, unlike a frozen soft-serve), my favorite is orange blossom. The ice cream is good and has a different taste because it's made with honey (it's a positive taste). Plus, there's 'special' ones that rotate each month [graham cracker ! pumpkin !] My only complaint on the ice cream is that the mint has chocolate chips in it :( The lines can be long...My sisters complained the cashiers have become slower over the years (they used to work there) but I haven't noticed although they were flighty my last time there. The prices are reasonable. A 'single' is actually two (large) scoops for 2.65 or so and increase every summer. (full disclosure: I worked there for one summer making the ice cream, almost 10 years ago. I realize reviewing such a place is technically against yelp rules, but I want to add this place to my list of Old Brooklyn places !) (This review is only for the Old Brooklyn location).
What a fun experience not to mention tasty. Long queues shows what an experience this is . Imagine a waffle shaped as fish filled with flavor and ice team Astounding good dessert

I went to Mason's for the first time this week to try their Korean corn dog and ice cream, and felt that I had a good time. I think the best thing about Mason's is the customer service. All of the employees were super friendly and helpful, especially after I told them it was my first time there. I got many recommendations for both my corn dog and my ice cream, and was able to try several of the ice cream flavors - I would literally go back just because everyone there was so nice and patient. I thought the ice cream selection was weaker when I went. I don't fault Mason's for this, but I would advise that you check their Instagram before making the trip to see the flavors beforehand since they rotate frequently. I ended up getting black sesame and chocolate butterfinger. It was good, but because very few flavors were super appealing to me, I felt I didn't get a true Mason's experience with my relatively safe and not-interesting combination. This was my first time having a Korean style corn dog and I thought that it was fun. My friend got a half cheese corn dog and I got a regular all beef corn dog and we really enjoyed them. We got them with panko and tried with ketchup, mustard, gochujang marinara, and buldak yum yum. The yum yum was good but I don't feel like it added too much. To my surprise I really enjoyed the gochujang marinara. If I ever got another craving for a Korean corn dog I would get one with the marinara, along with ketchup and mustard. If you've never had Mason's before, I would say it is worth a visit. They have unique flavors and it is overall a fun experience.

One of the better bakeries I have ever been to. Villani's has just about every sweet baked good you can think of, and probably a few you can't. I have been a few times, and sampled their croissant's, chocolate chip cookies, key lime pie, s'mores cookie and a black and white cookie to name a few items. My favorite by far are the croissants, they are huge, and full of flavor and a healthy amount of filing. You really notice the heft of the pastry; basically an entire meal of sweety flakey buttery goodness! If you want a tasty treat, you really cannot go wrong with costing this place!

Churn is always a perfect ending....whether you just stuffed your face across the street at Federal Pizza (like we did yesterday), while you are winding down after an amazing day, or if you really just want ice cream. I wanted to try something new so I had the coconut lime sorbet. It was refreshing and a little tart. Just about perfect. The kids each had a kids cone, which come with a fun little ring. Hubby had two scoops, one of which was a half scoop of two different flavors since he couldn't make up his mind (double chocolate, peanut butter, and banana...YUM!). We redeemed one of our punch cards (buy 5, get 1 free....awesome deal) and the total came to $10. Next time I am going to get an ice cream sandwich (your choice of ice cream in between two cookies for $4). In addition to the wonderful ice cream, the nostalgic candy and toys are also a great find. Last Christmas I picked up a bunch of stocking stuffers here and I know this will me my go to place again this year. Let's just hope I make it back there before then.

Phenomenal ice cream flavors delight your taste buds!! I decided to live on the wild side, waffle cone with three scoops--one dairy free double chocolate coconut ice cream, two dairy flavors--goey butter cake ice cream with cake bites & salted peanut butter with chocolate ice cream! Salted peanut butter was wonderfully delicious! Imagine your happiest creamy ice cream flavors with buttery notes and rich delicious textures. I loved them all and they're amazing! Truly worth the price and the quality flavors! I parked on the street, pay to park. It was afternoon so the line wasn't long.

The Crepe deserves 10 stars - it's as good as street crepes in Paris. It's the only one in North America which is. The service deserves minus 10. They're about as joyous as Thom Yorke Radiohead trapped in a Medieval Torture Device during a family bereavement. And you're a weirdo! That's why you keep coming here! Even though they treat you wrong here I sang that out loud last time I was here. You should have seen the dirty Luxe I got. I'm giving them a 5 star rating despite them having the worst service - perhaps that I've ever experienced. And if you have a problem with that, I don't give a crepe. It's one of the worst customer service experiences of my life, but it's also the best crepe in North America, so I'm giving it a 5 when they deserve a huge 0 (a zero, not an O, no way) for the enormity of their attitude problems. Anyway if you read this far, thanks for giving a crepe.
Probably the best ice cream I've ever eaten and I love my ice cream! The cereal flavors like Fruity Pebbles and Cinnamon Toast Crunch were delicious.

Awesome awesome ics cream! We did the 4 flavor sampler. Strawberry cheesecake, cinnamon Graham, cookie dough and asked the guy manning the store for the 4th flavor! He gave us blueberry cobbler and MAN! IT ROCKED!

Wowza! We heard about Donut Bar and last week I was fortunate to have a weekday off for a change. We found Donut Bar, just off the Strip's northern end, and parked in front at the pay to park. The display is varied and colorful, while not overwhelming and the shop itself is warm and cozy. Staff are very helpful as we had lots of questions. We had already drooled over their photo of blueberry with Meyer lemon topping: amazing. So I, like a socially isolated cave hermit, right away asked "do you still ave the blueberry" while my poor husband was trying to speak. The creme brulee was the next choice, followed by Mexican Hot Chocolate and Oreo. We took some old fashioneds to go. Well, now. I post healthy foods and recipes online, but donuts are an exclusion and we do indulge! All of these donuts were superb!! We sat in the small indoor bench area next to the Donut fish tank. The coffee was wonderful- a good alternative to your run of the mill donut shop. The quality and inventiveness add up to a big 5 BFFDS for me. If you must ask, that's "best friendly fantastic donut supplier". Vegan options are here too, evidently. Check it out: DB Las Vegas is a winner!!

I have been to this place a few times. They have ice cream infused with cereal or milk tea drinks. The cereal-infused ice cream is a pretty neat concept. I don't think I have been to another dessert shop that does this. They definitely give you a lot of toppings. This is a great place for meeting up with friends after a meal and we just want something light to snack on and catch up. The drinks in my opinion weren't as great as other places. I ordered the jasmine milk tea which was a little light compared to other boba shops. However I really love matcha and will have to try their matcha drinks next time.

Yum!! I decided to go here after reading a report saying it was one of the best in the country. Well... I'm not going to disagree! This place has a lot of different flavors, some very creative such as blue cheese honey or their bacon! They have many different types of sundaes, ice cream sandwiches and different cones/scoops. Overall, i highly recommend you come here and try one of the best ice cream places i've ever had!

Wow, I am sad I didn't find Amelie's sooner. After a long day in Charlotte I was looking for a place to grab some coffee and a dessert and there was Amelie's. As soon as we stepped inside the smell of fresh baked pastry welcomed us. Once I saw the fruit tart I knew what I was going to order. My husband choose the chocolate croissant. I was pleasantly surprised when they informed us that they serve french press coffee. The interior is decorated in a funky and eclectic style which is n stark contrast to the refined pastry they serve. The crust on the tart was delicate and buttery topped with sweetened cream and sliced fresh ripe fruit. There was a sweet sticky glaze over the top. YUM! The chocolate croissant was flaky and buttery with just enough chocolate in every bite. I will be back again and again.
Delicious chocolate shake! $7.04 for a small shake so a little pricey but definitely worth the deep chocolate taste!

really nice, spacious, and clean ice cream shop. there is a big seating area for customers to sit at after they purchase the ice cream. they made their ice cream on site and they claimed all the ingredients are fresh and homemade. there is also a large selection of ice cream flavor more than most ice cream place offers. i ordered vanilla bean and mango sorbet. i also tried taste other flavor. overall, its ice cream is really creamy. to me why i gave a three stars instead of five stars bc to me the ice cream is too sweet and too creamy to me. if u have a really sweet tooth then this is probably the place for u. to me i felt there is too much sugar and butter added to its ice cream and kinda over power its original flavor like mango. such as the salt caramel i tried it is on the salty side. overall it is a nice ice cream place but just not for me.

My dilemma coming here is always if I should get ice cream or a drink (and should I get that drink with boba). Today I got ice cream with cocoa krispies (its blended into the ice cream- yummy and unique), topped with graham crackers and honey drizzle - so good! Perfect for hot day too. My husband got the Cookies & Cream which he really enjoyed. The staff here is friendly and helpful when it comes to giving suggestions. This has definitely turned into one of my favorite dessert spots. I look forward to coming back and maybe trying a drink next time.

Trust issues man.... Got the Grandma's Cookies and my sample tasted like snickerdoodle and I saw it had something else in it, but I wasn't sure what it was. And it ended up being.... You guessed it, oatmeal raisin. The descriptions should say what they actually are. My wife loved it, so that was nice.
Everything was presented so well and the staff was so friendly! The place is cute too! I got a milkshake and it was SO GOOD. I will definitely be going back.

I walked in was greeting by the most friendly staff ever. These guys and girl are awesome. Just the service made me want to comeback already. I told him I had eaten a doughnut sandwich in Cali but have never found one in az so I ordered the Cookie Monster doughnut sandwich, (same I had in cali) and I actually think that Novels sandwich is way better! Was so good and will be back forever !
There are other potentially more well known bakeries in town but this place has the best macaroons, Bialys, and biscuits in town. My favorite macaroon flavor: cookies and cream.

This places is very unique, they had very cool decorations and one of the largest selections of pastries and desserts I've seen, which is great. The lines can be extremely long, but it's worth the wait. Everything tasted amazing, I recommend getting some of the fruit tarts, they are my favorite.
You can't go wrong with a egg, cheddar cheese, spinach and tomato baguette!

It gets 4 stars because of the lobster tails & cannolis and because I love Cake Boss. I took off 1 star because of the red velvet cupcake which was just not good at all. I'm a red velvet snob and expected a red velvet cupcake from Carlo's to be like everything else I've tried there.. Amazing. It wasn't. Hard to describe what exactly was wrong but didn't even taste like red velvet to me. Anyway, lobster tails are my favorite, hands down! They're amazing. I literally constantly crave them. My friend wanted them to add some chocolate on top of hers when we went and they wouldn't do it but I'm fairly certain that would be really good. Their cannolis.. Mm so good! I visited the Carlo's in Hoboken a few years ago and had a cannoli so I had to try the ones here. I had the regular one and the chocolate one. Both are great! My friend got a hazelnut covered cream puff in addition to some lobster tails and she said it was really good. It is a must try for me for next time. I spent about $28 (I think) for two lobster tails, two cannolis and two red velvet cup cakes. Also, there were a lot of people there in a small space but they do try to get to the next number (yes, you have to take a number when you get there) quickly. I didn't have any issues with the customer service either.. Everyone was friendly! I would, however, recommend a way for customers to be able to know what is in the display cases before ordering. Even while ordering at the one with the pastries, you're unable to see the cupcakes case as people are standing everywhere while waiting and vice versa. I probably missed out on something simply because I couldn't see it and didn't know it was there. After reading some other reviews, it seems there is now a line to get in which should alleviate that problem.
So, so busy at all hours... It's hard to relax and enjoy the atmosphere with all the people crowding around. Good food and decent coffee, though.

Came in here earlier today with my fiance. Heard about this place through Yelp. Since I love chocolate, why not? Thought the prices are a little too much, however they do serve some delicious shakes and sundaes. The wait was not too long and the customer service was great. Definitely recommend this place for true choco-holics!

Had a hard time finding this place at night but its definitely worth the drive. Parking is also slim but Valet is available. This small place comes with excellent customer service and most of all GOOD ice cream!!! Will be back for more Vietnamese Coffee and Butter Pecan goodness. . .

These cupcakes are delicious and you can tell that quality ingredients are used. There is a reason for the line, they are good cupcakes and worth it and if you don't want to wait in line then go to the atm. Just get there early enough to get the kind of cupcake you like. I had the vanilla and chocolate coconut and it was heavenly. My husband who is not really a cupcake fan loved them too. So if you need a really good cupcake fix and you come here, you wont be disappointed.

I can't tell you if this is the best ice cream in Madison but I can tell you I'm totally happy that I tried it. If I lived in Madison, I'd easily go here all the time. I decided to go with the Alumni Park After Dark Chocolate. It obviously wasn't dark because it was in the middle of the day but I couldn't pass up dark chocolate ice cream. It was dark chocolate ice cream with white chocolate chips. You should know that the white chocolate chips were more like shavings than chips! I IMMEDIATELY FELL IN LOVE! It was also supposed to have caramel. I didn't taste the caramel in my scoop but it was certainly gooey. I decided on a waffle cone. It was a small mistake because there was a hole in the bottom.
