They also have really great coffees and teas. I wished I could have tasted them all. Out of all the reasons to live in Charlotte, Amelie's would have been my primary reason to move there.

Truly exceptional ice cream! This place has fresh ice cream and wonderful staff. The Buckeye ice cream is an Ohio classic and highlights the store's roots. The caramel pretzel crunch is fantastic. You order from the outside windows which is fun in itself. Welcome to town Handel's!

I am an ice cream lover and actually very snobbish when it comes to good ice cream My wife and I in our travels always look for local favorites wherever we go and let me tell you, we both believe Mitchell's by far is superior to any we have tried. We are temporarily living in Columbus and Graeter's is the end all here- not anywhere close to Mitchell's in terms of its creative flavors and good tasting, creamy, and flavorful ice cream. My favorite flavors are Rocky Road and the Bing Chocolate Cherry chunk- never can decide which to have so I always get the Taster's duo. Cleveland's- feel fortunate that you have Mitchell's- some cities we have visited have no locally made ice cream at all- their idea of good ice cream are chains. To the Mitchell Brothers- PLEASE think about expanding to Columbus- we miss you!!!!

I scream for ice cream! After a night out, my pal and gal pals weren't quite ready to go out yet so we yelped up a dessert joint the was close by and still open that we could hit up. Thankfully we found Melt! Melt is such a cute little place, but it does its job. They sell drinks, candy, mangonadas and serves extra delicious ice cream. The packaging is so cute too, it comes in little Chinese take out boxes and includes a fortune cookie. My sister and I each got a single scoop, Cookie Monster and a Cute-cumber. Our total came out to $9.00 even. Single scoops are $4.50, double scoops are $6.00 and triple scoops are $7.50. Cookie Monster was the perfect amount of sweet and chewy from the cookie and cookie dough. Cute-cumber was a refreshing, very light, less sweet option. We both enjoyed our ice creams very much. I really like that they have a lot of different and seasonal flavors, some like zombie brains, pumpkin pie and churro. They do have a roomy outside area to sit and enjoy, none inside. They have tea lights and benches that create such a cozy ambiance. I like it here, and I can't wait to come back to try new/changing/seasonal flavors! Also: Parking is a little hard to find on busy nights, and meters are available.

My husband and I got a "bottom of the cereal bowl" with fruity pebbles. Phenomenal. It was very busy and had a line outside but can understand why because it was delicious and well worth the wait. Highly recommend.
The macaroon is way worse than I expected from a famous bakery. I hope the restaurant is a lot better than this...

The donuts were great! We had the apple crumb and the s'mores pop tart donut. The pop tart donut was awesome! Very cool concept. Unbelievably filling...it was huge! The staff was extremely friendly and polite. Great service.
Amazing donuts and fun staff! Come hungry and with a sweet tooth. Their donuts as so delicious!

I'm a huge coffee shop explorer and this is one of my all time favorites! Big, creatively decorated, tons of fun drink specials and menu options. Everyone is friendly and efficient. We'll definitely be coming back.

I'm embarrassed to say that the employees know me and know what I normally get. Well, actually they know a variety of what I get because I come so often I have to change up the flavors. People always are drawn to the cupcakes but the cookies and ice cream are just as great. I love how they switch out flavors and if you follow them on facebook they have many BOGO offers!
Gooood. Pops chowed down on a banana split and I had a regular caramel apple. Expensive though. 35 bucks for just that.

DELICIOUS but too expensive for what it was to get full stars. I loved the options and I'm definitely happy I ordered the ice cream with the marshmallow and macaroon. However, I feel like the macaroons aren't as great as other macaroons I've had and for the price, I think each component should be delicious on its own. Again, I'm still super happy I tried this out and the marshmallow is a MUST!

This place practically saved my sweet tooth several time during the summer of 2020. It was hot, and my options were low. The fact they operate in a shack actually helped them figure out a safe and efficient way to serve people during the pandemic. The ice cream is absolutely incredible. Novel creates some unique flavors, as well as a variety of classics. I enjoy ice cream with honey and lavender during the summer, and these people had my back. The floral bloom was a subtle high five to the sticky sweetness.
The quality is a bit below the Yountville location's level. I was a little disappointed, but not so disappointed that I didn't enjoy a pudding cup and a nutter butter cookie sandwich.
Amazing donuts!!! They are HUGE for the price. We got them delivered to the Luxor and they were still so fresh when they arrived. This will be a new tradition on Vegas Trips

The ice cream is great and the cupcakes are above average. My lower rating is based on the fact that the seating area outside is always super messy. I've been here 3 times in the past 2 weeks...midweek and weekends...and the table are covered in empty containers and other trash. There are no garbage cans in the seating area. You have walk about 50 feet to toss trash. As I write this, I've been outside for 15 minutes and haven't seen anybody come out to "bus" the empty tables. It's kind of gross to sit outside and eat ice cream where melted dairy has been sitting in the heat.

my friends love Sprinkles and I think they normally get a cupcake topped with gelato??? they highly recommend but today I just came in to get my roomie a cupcake for her birthday so she can open something from me when I get home. they had a small variety and some seasonal items. a very nice guy at the counter helped me out and he had a quirky yet professional approach to selling the items, he's a perfect match to the big pink store. when I went to check out I noticed they had cupcakes for fur babies!!!! so OF COURSE i had to get my puppy lea a treat! the cupcake plus the gift box and the puppy treat were under ten dollars, even though i have absolutely no sweet tooth ill try to stop back in and give this place some business.

Got here right before they opened on a Friday morning! As soon as they opened I was greeted with a smile & Welcome to Carlos Bakery! I called before I arrived to Las Vegas and already received good customer service and had all my questions answered about the cake options & prices. I bought a beautiful white cake with fresh strawberries for my daughters 21st Birthday! It was delicious, moist and the strawberries were sweet! We all loved it!

I've known of The Butterwood Bake Consortium for quite a long time, but as a South Hills girl, this particular spot is a bit out of my way. Finally, I remembered to poke my head in and pick up some treats when I was passing through the area this weekend. Obviously I couldn't enjoy the full Butterwood experience in 2020, but I got to enjoy the important part: the cake! Butterwood is a dessert cafe, meaning they specialize in some of our favorite sweets - think cake, pie, and brownies. Coffee and tea are also served here, so in any year other than 2020, this would be the greatest spot to meet up with friends and catch up. While the dine-in experience is hard/impossible to enjoy right now for reasons beyond Butterwood's control, I can confirm that their desserts are still fabulous. I recently picked up several tea cakes to take home and sample. One was a lavender rose cake with fig buttercream; another was a dark chocolate cake with peanut butter buttercream; and the last was a ginger tea cake. The ginger cake, while good, was actually the "disappointing" one out of the bunch (I use the term loosely because again: all were good). I say that because chocolate and peanut butter always go well together and because the lavender-rose-fig combo is out of this world delicious. I did not expect that one to be my favorite, but here we are! A little more about the cake here: on their website they say, "We bake with organic Beehive Flour, Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Evaporated Cane Juice, Multiple Organics Brand Cocoa Powder, and local butter, cream, and organic eggs, all sourced from Frankferd Farms Organic Foods." Sounds good, right? Bonus points because Butterwood also serves up gluten-free desserts; in fact, my friends who eat gluten-free diets are the people who sing the loudest praise for this little cafe. While 2020 has sadly kept me from comfortably sitting and enjoying the full cozy cafe experience, Butterwood's baked goods are still fantastic and can always be enjoyed at home. Treat yourself this holiday season and stop in to pick up a delectable dessert - you won't be disappointed!

This place is AMAZING. I was in Charlotte for an overnight business trip and had found rave reviews about this place before going... I ended up going because they were open late (this location is open 24 hours!). Upon walking in around 8:30 p.m. on a Sunday night, I was surprised to see a line about 20 people long. Luckily, it went very quickly. Great staff, very helpful. I had a blueberry lemonade, which was incredible... along with some chocolate/cinnamon macarons and the famous salted caramel brownie. It was the perfect sweet treat for a late night. They offer lots of sandwiches and soups as well, but I had already had dinner... I can't recommend this place enough!! Moral of the story, if you walk in and see a line out the door--just wait it out. It's worth it.

This place is the real deal. It's a donut shop that has been around for some 80 years with history and cachet but without the prices and attitude of those trendy donut shops closer to the hip parts of most cities. Jack Frost Donuts is quite a ways from downtown, where Pearl and Fulton meet to form a triangle near the Outerbelt Freeway (I-480) in a fairly nondescript middle class neighborhood. The physical plant obviously doesn't date back to when Jack Frost Donuts was founded in the 1930s. Their store is newer than that and it's modern, bright, and has sufficient parking. Note that there is no seating inside. You can always sit in your car and slam dunk their baked goods down the hatch. Or, like most normal people, you can take their baked goods elsewhere and ingest them in a more civilized manner. The thing about Jack Frost Donuts is the novelty of the offerings combined with reasonable prices. The service is efficient and they don't seem to tire of people asking what's in a particular donut. I'd say some of the donuts approach gourmet donut status, yet they are not priced as gourmet donuts. Again, this place is not that close to downtown. It's on the belt road that skirts it at a distance. You can come here while shopping big box retail nearby, on your way to or from the Metroparks Zoo, on your way to or from a seedy adult bookstore or strip joint on Brookpark Road, on your way to the office, and/or on your way to the airport, for which the exits are about 4 ramps going west along I-480. It is also important to note that there is more selection at the beginning of the donut day. Also, where Pearl and Fulton come together, or near there, there is a no right turn on red at one of the lights. Heed that ... and enjoy these well crafted donuts that are available to you without an ounce of pretense in either the service or the pricing.

The chocolate puddle cookies were delicious. A little messy but definitely yummy. There is seating inside and out in love the velvet couches. How pretty! We waited in a long line right at the opening, so we weren't the only people excited to try out this new spot. The reason for the 4 stars instead of five is that prices are posted for coffee but not food. I paid $10.50 for three cookies. Go check out the yummies!
To die for! Always stop anytime in Charlotte. Carmel brownies are the best! Take time to wait even if the line goes 3 rooms back.

Waited 25 minutes here to grab 1 cannoli to go! No regrets! Very family friendly and date friendly establishment for a yummy treat in Little Italy. Most guests enjoyed a pastry/cake with coffee at tea. Adorable!

The ube ice cream is sooooo good!!! I love the chestnut that they gave, but only ONE chestnut was a little cheap LOL if i knew, I would have added extra chestnuts. Very clean place, and plenty of parking. No dine in due to the pandemic but there outdoor sitting - 4 chairs and two small little coffee table. Cute little cafe, and you can try the ice cream first before deciding what to get.

Ahhhhh!!! I'm so happy I found this place. I went and got a little bit of everything. Lol. Everything was amazing. I went around 9:30 PM and the cashier was so sweet. She went thru every single macaron flavor with me and was patient while I looked around. She wasn't rude that I came in late (usually people anywhere 30-60 mins before closing are rude). I will defiantly be coming back here and I look forward to it!

This is usually a pretty safe bet to get your sugar high. I loved my cookies and cream shake with a chocolate chip cookie blended in. Total cost came to under $10 so not a bad deal for this part of town.

While gelato is my first love, I really enjoy ice cream and Churn was one of the best ice creams I've had in recent memory. I had vanilla and peanut butter with salted caramel topping. My wife had banana and butter pecan. All flavors were excellent. We talked with the owner for a few minutes and he gave us some great restaurant recommendations. Great staff, pleasant location. We were there on a Saturday afternoon in November and had no issues with parking.

WARNING: If you are serious about your diet, are diabetic or have other reasons to avoid indulgent sweet temptations don't read this review! I come from the land of Krispy Kreme- not those foolish boxes of stale doughnuts sold at gas stations and supermarkets but the real deal. I'm talking conveyer belt of yummy gooey goodness available 24 hrs a day and a bright red sign alerting the neighborhood that they are indeed, "Hot Now!" While I remain a fan of the Krispy Kreme I have to say that Jack Frost is in a completely separate category. Maybe that's why they use the different spellings. These are very different tasty treats! My coworkers introduced me to Jack Frost and it was love at first bite. The icing coming out of the top of the donut ads a bit of sweetness without being TOO much. It's a lovely addition, too. I've had a number of flavors and frankly I can just remember that they were yummy!!!! I have had the chocolate donut (a cake-y one that was german chocolate cake themed) and didn't love it. Had I been new to the JF scene I would have said it was great, but; being the experienced JF devotee I knew it wasn't the top product. Jack Frost does the light colored (plain?) donut best. It's almost fluffy and airy when you take a bite so you can really savor the quality flavor of it. Then (if you've chosen one with the poof of icing) you get a nice soft yet flavorful taste of the vanilla or chocolate, etc. that compliments the donut and top layer of icing. One donut that doesn't seem to come with the icing poof is the maple bacon donut. Yeh yeh yeh- bacon's blowing up/ blown up/ is over but you've gotta give this a shot. Seriously. Consider taking a hiatus from any vegetarian/ vegan dietary commitments you might have made. They do maple great in a number of ways. Something to remember: Jack Frost does not take credit or debit cards. They have taken a check (and the dears actually took my out of state check- I can't bring myself to buy a new box because these are perfectly fine for paying rent which is really the only time I ever use them) and they'll take cash of course! A dozen donuts will set you back a little over $8 and you'll get your money's worth!

I have mixed feeling about the opening of a 85C bakery in Las Vegas. Allow me to elaborate... Pro: same great quality pastries and drinks you come to expect of other 85C chains, finally accessible to Las Vegas. Some personal favorites include: any sea salt beverage, taro marble bread, boroh danish, spinach croissant. Con: all of my complaints are not about 85C itself: This is located in yet another Asian plaza with cramp parking spaces, not to mention the number of parking spaces must barely pass meet requirement for the number of shops in the plaza. The entrance of 85C is just another signal that Las Vegas is growing and getting saturated in Asian population. While this is great for Las Vegas residents, this is extremely bad for my belly!!! Why can't you just stay in SoCal so you are nice and far away ?! Ugh!

I personally think that this place is a little bit overrated. Yes, their frozen selections are definitely worth checking out, but I had better ones outside of Illinois. The place definitely had revisit values with their seasonal surprise flavor of the week. Sometimes, the flavor may be so wild that we can the cashier would prefer you to try out a sample before you finalize your purchases. My personal favorite is their vanilla sundae with crushed peanuts. Their ageless classic serves as my control group whenever I want to grasp how good a chill desert place is. It will not disappoint you! They also serves some classic items like frozen custard cake, slushies, banana split, and so forth. The place is almost always packed in weekends, but they have very few seats indoor, so expect to sit outside.

The Donut Bar is Fantastic!!!! What a wonderful way to start your day! The staff are very friendly - the old fashion donuts were great & the cinnamon roll was the best! We look forward to going back before we leave town!

I really wanted to like Hopscotch. The decor and ambiance is lovely, and I really like how you can purchase pieces from local artists and creators. However, the treats are rather lacking. I ordered a butterscotch cookie and a chocolate cupcake with strawberry frosting. For the quality, they are very overpriced. The chocolate cupcake, although pretty, was very lacking in any "chocolate" flavor, and honestly tasted similar to one from Schnucks. The frosting was okay. The cookie was better, but a little bit too tough. My jaw hurt after chewing. In addition, the customer service left something to be desired. The people at the counter seemed quite cool, almost judgmental. I hope Hopscotch will be able to improve their treats and cheer up a bit. Until then, I'll probably look somewhere else for coffee and dessert.

I love this place. I love it in NY, and I love it in LV. Crack pie - delicious. Cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes - delicious. If you have a sweet tooth and come looking for sweet desserts or huge selection of ice cream, or a unique fusion of flavors like other places offer, you won't find it here. But they have cereal milk soft serve that can't be found anywhere else that I find myself craving. They have simple but delicious cookies, like their blueberry one. Their desserts are borderline savory, but I love it like that! (except their crack pie, that's way sweet)

This is the best after dinner desert date spot. Their ice cream is amazing and the staff is super friendly. The let you sample the flavors generously. It's a quaint little hideaway and fun place for people watching and hanging out with your date over a delicious bowl of yumminess.

The ice creams were excellent and there were some unique flavors that I hadn't see anywhere else. We couldn't get a taster bite to taste some of the flavors due to COVID. The staff was friendly though and overall it's a nice place for a post-dinner visit for some desserts!

Went to Ninety's for the first time this past weekend. I came in after indulging in crafty crab across the way. I love ice cream. I love spending too much on hand scooped ice cream with mix-ins to be exact. All that! Anyway, it's a cute little place in university. Cute wall art inside for the best photo op. Due to Covid, line waits outside and a few enter at a time which is smart. I noticed a good sized menu with too many options to choose from which can be a blessing and a curse for me. I stared at the menus outside and still was lost inside. I wanted to get outside of my normal ice cream concoction from a spot closer to me. Anyway, wasn't allowed to taste test due to Covid and boy that sucks because now I don't know what to say about the taste. So I asked for coffee and salted caramel mix which is close to what I order at my local spot. Well the coffee I think was either chocolate and they didn't pay attention or it was the worst coffee ever. I don't like chocolate so it wouldn't be it for me either way. I was irked as I took it to go and got in my car and bounced. It wasn't good. Then, it sucks that they don't mix toppings in. They just throw them all on top. No way to enjoy it throughout. Also, each topping was 50 cents. Idk my preference is Marble Slab. I get to taste test what I want. And it all can be mixed in if I want. I know exactly what I'm getting and what it costs as mix ins are free. It's cute in here but I don't like the ice cream quality compared to other places. Maybe it was just a mess up between chocolate and coffee but either way first impression is the one that sticks for me and I don't want to waste money if I can't test it to see what it's like. People like it here tho. I can tell by the lines! Again still super cute and staff are super friendly and patient with people who don't know what they want (me).
Line can get long so best not to go during peak dessert hours! But it's definitely a good end to your night!

This crepe stand is inside the West Side Market. There was a pretty short line, but the process took awhile because there are only 3 crepe machines for cooking. Can't really blame the worker though he kept moving the entire time. The menu offers good suggestions or you can make your own crepe. I got one with asparagus, ham and brie and really enjoyed it. With both sweet and savory options this is a good spot for lunch or a snack. There's a coffee stand right next to the crepe stand which is convenient as well.

This was my first experience with Thomas Keller creations even though I've been in Northern California my whole life! Sad, because my drive to The French Laundry is basically half the time it takes to drive through rush hour...Anyways, I'm glad Bouchon Bakery was relatively close to me during my latest trip to Vegas. It's located on the side of The Venetian, actually tucked away in a small corner (on the left side of the The Venetian if you're facing it). There's only standing room to look at the display offerings and to purchase, but a few tables outside. Don't confuse this place with their bigger bistro restaurant inside Venezia Tower on the 10th floor. They offer a delicious-looking variety of French pastries, macaroons, and sandwiches. I only tried a few pastries, which included their most popular - kouign aman, cinnamon roll, almond croissant, and pain aux raisin. Normally, I really don't like to eat baked goods, as they're two things I dislike rolled into one - bread and sugar. These pastries were wonderful! They hit many notes - fantastic texture, delectably delicate, and subtle, buttery flavors. They had soo many crunchy, flaky, and light layers folded in the pastries, and I really couldn't pick out a favorite as I loved them all. The kouign aman was unique, buttery, and just a wonderful treat. The cinnamon roll was perfectly coated with a glaze that wasn't oversweet. The almond croissant was texture heaven with the thinly sliced and crunchy almonds. The pain aux raisin was filled with very plump and juicy raisins. This is one of the finest bakeries I have visited - the taste is very mature, as the pastries are more rich, delicate, and buttery than cloyingly sweet. I can taste the amount of thought and time that's gone into the pastries. Eat them fresh, when they're at their best!

I think the donuts are good but service is unfortunately lacking, went there yesterday and seemed like I was being a burden for buying a dozen donuts for 11 bucks! I don't think that's how I should feel after walking out of a place. I do rate them 2nd as best donuts I've had in Cleveland.

This place is such a cute icecream shop! I love the booths and stools- perfect photo ops! Usually if a place has great photo op moments I don't care if the food is that good. I expect mediocre. But their icecream was great! I got black cherry and rocky road in a waffle cone. The black cherry flavor is to die for. I don't even like cherries! I saw the girl getting a scoop for someone else and it looked amazing- asked for a sample- definitely amazing. We went this past Saturday (9/23) and the girls closing the store were so nice and sweet! Even when a couple came in 6 minutes before close and a gentleman maybe 1 min before close- they greeted them brightly and with a smile. I thought to myself "that's good customer service." Friendly staff, great icecream, and cute photo ops... 5 stars for sure!

What could be better in Arizona in the middle of march then ice cream. Churn is a very cute little shop that has great ice cream has well as candy! It's a kid's dream or big kid's dream in my case. The smells waft to the restaurant next door and you can't help but lick your lips and drink your beer faster. That's exactly what you should be doing for fresh homemade ice cream and cones that are perfect for Arizona weather.

We were so excited to finally try out this Italian bake shop, but we were really let down. First, it's a very cute, simple little shop with lots of parking and some picnic tables for outside munching, which I think is great. Inside is cramped--no biggie though. Next, the staff were adequately pleasant--nothing to write home about. They took our order, packed everything nicely and took the payment. But the food was subpar. This is not our first foray into Italian pastries--in NY they rule the pasty scene and everything they make is amazing. Not here. I noticed all croissants, lobster tails, cream horns, and such were far too overcooked--really dark to nearly burnt on top. This really ruins it for me. But here's what we order: Lobster tail: Yes, despite the above comment about being overcooked, I ordered 2 because I love them. I could not eat nearly half of the pastry because it was so hard from being nearly burned, but the cream filling is out of this world amazing. Sfingi: The pastry part of these is done very nicely, but the filling was lumpy, barely sweetened, and had a strong almond flavor. Tiramisu: Probably the worst we've had. The filling is more like a pudding (it's supposed to be primarily mascarpone), the lady fingers were dry, and there was no hint of the lady fingers having been soaked in coffee or rum or anything like that. Quite a disappointment, as tiramisu is my husband's favorite. Napoleon: The pastry layers were barely cooked and were the consistency of barely baked pie crust (kinda chewy). It's supposed to be made with puff pastry, and there was zero puff going on. The filling was again more like a pudding consistency--it's supposed to be a pastry cream. Very disappointing. Overall, disappointing. I didn't expect to love everything, but I thought it would be reasonable to expect something to be great. Too bad.

Buddy I'm calling you out on your lame cannoli. My mom can smoke you any day of the week. I can't believe you put your name on that. I'm Italian, I know Italian pastries, your shop here in vegas is a tourist trap. All hype!!! And dude, you guys break the cardinal sin of cannoli serving........you pre fill them and let them sit for hours. WTH, my man. Like any respectable host, you fill each cannoli as they are served. It takes like 6 seconds. A complete waste of $20. Shame on you my dude.

I don't think I will ever tire of Mitchell's ice cream - at least I haven't after eating it for three days in a row. This location is definitely the most fun for kids and families. It's located in a massive, theater-style building and one of the first things you see walking in is the toy train diligently chugging loops along ceiling. Behind the counter and visible through glass panes from the side and above is the actual factory of magic where workers (no Ooompa Loopmas, sorry!) toil away making batches on batches on batches of ice cream. The window seating on the first floor is all kid-height-friendly, and there are crayons and paper scattered around for the artistically inclined. The room upstairs can be rented for birthday parties and has a nice view of W. 25th Ave. Flavors, flavors. Try a few and then ask the employees what they think pairs well with what you've liked so far because you probably won't have the time to try all of them. Not at night with the line of people glaring at you at least. Some of my favorites at this location are the Black Raspberry w/ Dark Chocolate Chunk (chunk means you might find some HUNKING chunks), the Porter, and the Peanut Butter w/ Chocolate Covered Pretzel Yogurt. And always, always in their homemade waffle cone. The $1 is well worth it - it's got a perfect crunch and light, wafery flavor. You can order in advance and get cakes to go at this location. The blackboards aren't really helpful menu-wise, but you still CAN get shakes and other concoctions at this location. If you're conflicted between flavors, you can also ask for Junior Scoops of ice cream, which are smaller than their traditional scoops. For the die-hard Mitchell's fan, available for purchase are engraved ice cream scoops, T-shirts, or train conductor hats to elevate their fandom.

I had heard about this soft serve ice cream place as a Southside staple awhile ago, so when I found myself driving by I decided to check it out. Parking is limited and we waited about 10 minutes in line. I could have used another 10 minutes to decide what I wanted to order! There are sooooo many options. I ordered an Arctic Swirl with vanilla ice cream and locally made chocolate chip cookies from Nancy B mixed it. My friend got a soft serve mint chocolate chip cone. The prices were average. It's really the selection of choices that left the greatest impression. There is something for everyone with classic choices to one of a kind choices (Belgium waffles pieces anyone?) I can see why this place is still going strong a half of century later. p.s. I didn't take a photo because the photo just didn't do the dessert justice.
$7.57 for a tiny cup of basic "cereal milk" soft serve and cornflake crunch. Crazy overpriced and not even good. Extremely underwhelming.
This is the best place to get ice cream! The ice cream is so smooth and so delicious! My boyfriend and I always get the four scoop sampler and we love it!!

My husband, dog, and I just discovered villanis and now I am positive that all of us will be regulars. The place is easy to get to and has a big lot to park in. There are a few outdoor benches and picnic tables to utilize. We came on a Saturday morning and the place was not crowded, only a few people in line ahead of us. As I entered the shop, I could already tell my indecisiveness was kicking in. So many delicious options. I chose a slice of key lime pie, a s'mores bar, and 2 Italian cookies. The total was about $11. I asked for a "pupacino" which is just like Starbucks whipped cream in a cup. That was complimentary. The s'mores bar is heavy! I love the thick graham cracker crust and the toasted marshmallows on top. The key lime pie was perfectly tart and the filling tasted like it was whipped because it was so light. The cookies were good as well, but being $1/cookies, I don't know if I will get these again. All in all, a good experience.
Best Stromboli and cannoli. Excellent customer service and don't miss the gelato. Parking may be little struggle but you will definitely find a spot. Their cookies is delicious
Fun ice cream selections. I went in for a simple fudge sundae but had trouble sticking to it since there are so many yummy options!

Small space BIG flavor. That's the summation of this gym tucked away in downtown Las Vegas. If you find yourself in the unforgiving desert of Nevada look no further than the donut bar as your oasis flowing with coffee and sugar. This sugar isn't just any sugar, it's sugar masterfully woven into scrumptious fluffy, and sometimes filled, donuts. The picture accompanying this review shows the spread for two that we purchased (and yes we ate all but two in one sitting). Here you will see the elegant body cream pie long john, the hazelnut overload (powdered sugar filled with Nutella), the caramel latte (yes a donut), and the maple bacon muffin. All the donuts surpassed expectations sending us directly into a diabetic coma (in a good way) of the likes you only see by someone ingesting something so spectacular. Simply put, if you find yourself eloping in the little white chapel or simply trying to live it up and win it big the donut bar will provide you a guaranteed win for your money in Vegas. This is no gamble but a guarantee.

Well this is just a kiosk-type place right by the Phantom Theatre at the Venetian. There wasn't a lot of macarons left when we got there, but I did snag a raspberry(?) one. I liked it. It had a lovely texture that was slightly better than the other macarons I've had from other places. We also got some madeleines and a TKO. Oh, that TKO sure punched me right on the mouth with its awesome taste. That TKO was worth all the trouble taking the monorail from our hotel to the Venetian and navigating its seedy casino floor to get to it. That TKO changed my life, and I'm sure it will change yours, too.

I regret not trying every pastry they offered. I just didn't have enough time. I ate here 5 times at least in 2 weeks. They were so yummy no matter what time we arrived. Man I regret not trying every chocolate and pastry they offered.

Great bakery in the heart of Little Italy. Been twice and fast, great service no matter how busy they are. The chicken parm sandwich was as big as my forearm and delicious! Cannolis are must get and the tiramisu is fantastic. Get a box of a pastries to go so you can enjoy the charm of this great cafe from your home.

I visited this location with my family & inlaws. My inlaws are middle eastern. My inlaws were speaking arabic & i noticed the staff making faces towards them. They asked for any samples & staff said we dont give out samples. They proceeded to shop & bought $100 worth of product. Staff did not provide a bag. We asked for a bag & staff said they dont have any WHEN we clearly can see the bags. We all had to carry all the product back to Venetian where we parked & walked from. The next day i called in & asked for a manager. I explained the situation to him & he barely apologized. I asked him about the samples & he said we used to hand out freely but policy changed. We give to whomever asks. Guess my inlaws dont deserve samples. I then asked him if they ran out of bags & whats scenario is somebody spends $100 in the store. He said they had bags & dont know why staff said that. I usually visit this Ghiradelli once a month & used to visit it when it was next door to Imperial Palace. Thats over 15 years of visits. I love ice cream & Ghiradelli was my main choice but no longer. Manager of this location should be ashamed of himself/herself & should replace his racist staff. I wont visit Ghiradelli any longer nor tell visitors to go there. I will share this experience with my friends in SF as well.

5:5 for the customer service!!! Everyone was smiling and helpful and dressed in Halloween costumes. They gave my 4 year old a free mummy donut which stained his entire face black, lol. But it made his day anyway. The donuts- I went with the intention to try the French toast and creme brÃ»lÃ©e, I ended up buy the French toast, blueberry lemon, apple fritter pumpkin filled. By far the best was the French toast. It was actually pumpkin French toast. I would make the 30 minute drive just for that donut, but the rest were a little too sweet for me. I still would recommend this place bc of how unique the donuts are and the awesome customer service.

I had the most delightful experience at Sloans ice cream. I was staying at the Venetian and I just had to check out this beautiful store. I couldn't help the sweet smell coming from the store so I ventured in. I was immediately greeted by the sweet girl by the counter that soon turned out to be the General manager. She offered me some of their most popular ice creams and I was just so excited to try every option. She eventually convinced me to get their luxury sampler which had about every perfect bite size sweetness can offer! Jamie if you're reading this , I just wanted to thank you for your patience and your Pristine customer service!
I loved the breakfast sandwiches and salted caramel brownie. We went to the Pineville location and there was ample seating and no wait.

If you're a Champaign-Urbana native, I'm pretty sure it's a rule (and possibly something in the water) that you love Jarling's Custard Cup. Talk about a C-U tradition. Jarling's has been open (and keep in mind, this is a summer shop, so they're only open from April-ish to November-ish) since 1983 (they began in 1949, but in Danville). They have an incredibly history, one any employee would be happy to share with you (or you can always find more on their website). They've done some renovations in the past few years, giving them a better parking lot (the old one was abysmal, and even though they're still using it, they've expanded to make the drive around nicer). There's also outdoor seating! That's the other thing... Jarling's isn't really an "inside" place. You either get your treat to go, or your stand around outside and eat it as it melts all over you. ;D At one point, the store was completely outside, but they built a small air-conditioned foyer-like surround, which is really nice on a hot day and there are 10,000 people ahead of you! ;D Their menu is so diverse, I think it'd take the most seasoned die-hard an entire summer to get through all the flavors and combinations (and they're always adding more!). The price is steep, but you're paying for quality, here, over something that's so processed and artificial it almost ruins the experience. Seriously,if you're in need and have the chance, get your custard fix at one of C-U's paragons. You can't go wrong.
Nice little dessert spot in Phoenix. All of the homemade ice cream flavor are so good!

Actually I really like 85°C, but when I go this time, I find out they don't have many choices. I mean they only have half menu different bread. The worse is they use paper to wrap bread, not plastic bag anymore. I mean even paper bag is better. When I go back home, the bread come out from the paper wrap...

We decided to check this place out while we were in Vegas. The lines were long and it took a while to get our order placed. We purchased a mini cannoli and a lobster tail. The cannoli was not soggy and was delicious. The lobster tail was excellent as well. I really enjoyed the cream filling in the lobster tail. The only issue I had with this place is that it seems to be run in a very inefficient manner. I have not seen Cake Boss in a long time so I don't know if the original location is run in a similar manner. It should not be that time consuming to take a customer's order, get the items out of the case, and put the items in a bag/box. It was not clear to me why the ordering/picking up/paying process takes so long.
Finally tried bacon cinnamon roll it was amazing and totally worth the wait. Delicious donut flavors, amazing and friendly staff.

Pretty awesome macaroons, especially the pistachio ones. I was disappointed in the small selection of items available, though. It's small and kind of tucked out of the way so it can be hard to find if you don't turn the corner the right way. It's there though, so don't give up and ask around! The cheesy bread stuff was alright. Remember that it's just a bakery where you can pick up sweets and coffee and there's no seating.
We just moved here and this is hands down the best ice cream I've ever had.. Beats cold stone out of the water .. We love Tuesdays it's $2.50 single scoop of ice cream you can't beat it

CEREAL MILK ICE CREAM END OF STORY. was bummed that it was too damn cold to enjoy soft serve on my most recent trip to NYC (ok i lie my sister shamed me and was like eww don't be basic) I don't care if it's basic I love Milk Bar. This 6 dollar ice cream is so fricking good. I don't understand why all of California is obsessed with Salt and Straw -- this stuff is infinitely better. also the coffee drinks sooo good -- not a super acidic coffee which I appreciate. I tried a latte which was great strong but not bitter and an iced coffee both were fantastic my only regret was not ordering a large iced coffee for the heat.

Really great ice cream and food. Very high quality interior and great eye feel. Ice cream has great mouth feel. It does take some time for food to come out and ice cream to be made. Interesting process but don't expect to be in and out with your ice cream.

Wow! Incredible quality for a little ice cream stand. Typical cones, sundaes, and milkshakes. But a menu of burgers, fries, nachos, etc. and items like the raspberry toasted almond tort sundae really set this place a part from competitors. Worth the trip.

I've always been a fan of the 85-degree bakery since my hometown location in SD. So I'm very happy to see a piece of home in Vegas. 85 degree bakery has theee best variety of fresh-baked bread and desserts! The aroma of coffee and bread just perks me right up in the morning. And I love how soft the bread is, at an affordable price of less than $2-$3 each. My favorites: Brioche - rectangle-shaped Japanese style bread with milk and buttery flavor Mango Tale - sweet bread with mango cream cheese Berry Tale - sweet bread with blueberry cream cheese Marble Taro - sweet bread with taro filling - yassss! Ham & Cheese - bread rolled in ham & cheese... mmm perfect breakfast And oh. You can't forget the Sea Salt Coffee! I get the Caramel flavor. Perfect for washing down all these delicious treats!
DELICIOUS ice cream spot. The strawberry is amazing & fresh, and the lavender honey is super yummy. Stoked to have them in the neighborhood!

Cute place! Their tiramisu is delectable, we had it for a friend's birthday and its consistency is so creamy and thick, it's ice cream like. The sides are aligned with light and fluffy lady fingers and it was a joy of a cake! A cake shared between about 6 people came to $30 so more expensive than other small cakes for not a huge party but it was surely a treat. I also always get their cafe au lait and sometimes there is too much milk added and not enough coffee but for $2, it is still a good drink! The outdoor seating is super nice overlooking mayfield and Murray hill. The way the bakery is placed allows plenty of sunlight and I can see myself on a less busy day coming here to read or just sit and enjoy the sun! Try their discounted bakery goods as well! You can get muffins or croissants for just $1 if they are a day old and they have other discounted goods like crostata and Turkey sandwiches.

I love this place! When I came here I thought it was a walk-in ice cream shop but it's actually more like a take out stand. They have such a large variety of ice cream flavored and the four scoop sampler is the best deal. My top flavors are pistachio, peanut butter parfait, praline pecan, and cheesecake. The best thing about their ice creams is that each ice cream flavors have the actual food in it. For example, cheesecake has cheesecake bites and pistachio has actual pistachios, etc. My least favorite ice cream flavor was Reese's peanut butter cups. I avoided getting the Reese's pieces one because I don't like Reese's pieces. I got the peanut butter cup expecting it to have crushed up peanut butter cups but instead, it was crushed up Reese's pieces! I don't know if the girl got my flavor wrong since she only remembered one out of my four flavors and had to ask again, but that was the only disappointing part of my meal. Overall this is my new favorite ice cream place and I would always come back here for ice cream! Especially now that the Vegas heat is increasing!

super cute place ! the outside eating area is nice and perfect on a cloudy or sunny day! the inside of the store is small, so if it is raining, i would wait before going! there is a parking lot near the store which is nice, and the ice cream wall and fairy lights are so pretty! at the time, there was mocha and matcha oreo, so i got a scoop of each! i recommend both, although i really want to try their taro, thai iced tea, black sesame, and other asian flavors! great service, kind staff, and color changing spoons!

Wow. This place is it. Transformed from a movie theater, this ice cream shop is reportedly one of the best in Cleveland, and you can definitely tell why. The lines are long, but move fairly quickly. I got the raspberry crumble ice cream and it and actually tasted like a colder and creamier version of a crumb cake. You can even go up to the second floor and watch the employees in action. I will definitely come back next time that I'm here! There's a reason this place is a must-go-to in Cleveland.

This place, and the people who own it, are awesome. Good vibes and great ice cream. We got two dough melts, one with cookie monster ice cream+ fruity pebbles and one with fat elvis+coco puffs, and a single scoop of honey lavender. Everything was insanely delicious The owners were telling us how every batch is hand made with real ingredients, the honey lavender has real honey and real lavender, and how they take care to make sure they are serving quality items. They were very friendly and personable, we are excited to come back again. You can sample any of the flavors and they are excited to tell you all about what's in it and why they like it. I can't give you a flavor suggestion because they were all too good to pick from. 5 stars!

This experience was not great. We paid $18 for a miniature affogato and a 16 ounce shake- for $11 bucks it should be at least 20 ounces. I got the birthday shake and my dad got the affogato, I chose the b'day flavor for my shake. The shake was below mediocre and tasted like watered down cake batter. The affogato was okay and an okay price but the shake should have wowed me for $11 dollars. It's not somewhere I'd like to go back to and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone else.

MMM-- So good!! I asked John S. for places to go while I was in Cleveland, and he suggested going to Honey Hut. So when my friends and I had some time on Saturday night, I insisted we try Honey Hut. When we got there around 9pm, there were a lot of people lined up for ice cream! I asked one of the workers what is the most popular flavor, and she said Honey Pecan. That settled it-- I ordered Honey Pecan in a cone. For $2.35, you get two big scoops of ice cream! The ice cream was sweet, creamy and decadent, with lots of big pecan halves. They use honey instead of sugar, and you can tell. They probably use whole milk and tons of cream, but hey-- it tastes delicious! You could tell it was quality ice cream. If Honey Hut was in California, I know I'd gain 20 pounds or so. Big props to John S. for the recommendation!

I've been wanting to try Milk Bar for the longest time. I've visited NYC several times and have not made it, so I was excited when I stumbled upon this one in the Cosmopolitan Hotel. I got the combo pack (ice cream, compost cookie, crack pie, and truffles). I could not decide on which one, so why not. I'm not sure if the NYC location makes the cookies and pies fresh, but the cookie I got here was pre-packaged and kinda tasted old. Not gross - just kinda hard, dry, and meh. The cookie tasted like one you would get from your average grocery store bakery. Crack pie - good, not great. Kinda a small piece for the price. Truffles - really sweet, but good. These were probably my fave of the baked goods. The ice cream was my favorite of all. If I came again I would just stick to the ice cream only. It's so weird, but it does taste exactly like cereal milk! I don't know why I thought it wouldn't though. I liked the salty/sweet flavors of the cereal with the ice cream. Overall, I'm glad I could finally try it, but not really sure about the hype.

So, imagine you're me: you think any meal after noon no longer has the right to call itself brunch, you've been known to get hangry (hungry+angry) even when well rested, hangover-free, and in your own time zone and consequently you ALWAYS pre-breakfast before meeting friends for brunch, and you're the only person in your group of friends on Eastern Standard Time. The "Let's meet downstairs at 11am on a Saturday" plan is not going to work for you. Enter Bouchon Bakery. Open 6 am to 9 pm every day of the week, Bouchon Bakery presents the opportunity to grab a snack the night before, or offers you a destination in the morning when you are inevitably awake before everyone else. Craving something sweet? Go for the decadent sticky-bun. Want something a little more basic? An epi-baguette with butter and jam will stave off hunger until it's time for brunch. Flying Southwest (no meals) at an ungodly hour Sunday? Grab a ham and cheese croissant and laugh at the people eating the pathetic airport offerings. Also good: the raspberry filled "beignets" (they're not beignets--they're regular donuts, but they are super delicious), the macarons (especially caramel), the almond toffee and the shortbread cookies (the latter two make a particularly nice present for your significant other that hates cheap crap like magnets and key chains). As I'm sure others have mentioned, it's not cheap, but nothing is in Las Vegas. At least the expense doesn't come with a long wait. It's notable that it isn't anywhere near the Bouchon restaurant. You'll find the bakery on the first floor of the Venetian, under some escalators, which isn't very descriptive, I know, but just find someone in a security uniform and ask for directions. They are all really helpful.
I've tried Donuts at this place after hearing about them from my co-worker and it was totally worth it. These are by far the best Donuts I've tasted. I definitely recommend this place.

The most Gucci donut ice cream sandwich to eat during a quarantine run. The Oreo mint ice cream is so good wolf'ed it down and proceeded to run back home as fast as I can to take a massive deuce from my dairy intolerance. Worth it. No regrets.

Just discovered this little gem recently and am so happy that I did! The gelato is amazing and they offer so many flavors. I really enjoyed the Nutella flavor with the coffee. My fiancÃ© got a cookie cup - pictured below. Was amazing! Customer service was great also. Slightly on the expensive side but worth it because the quality is great! Will be back!

omfg i LOVE LOVE LOVE this place.. parisan macaron's are GINORMOUS and SO cheap. I loved the pistachio macarons and raspberry macarons!!! The bakery was located right below from where i was staying in the venentian. If you ever go to New York or Las Vegas, you HAVE to try this place.. i can't wait for the next time i go to las vegas cause my mouth is watering just thinking about those ginormous macarons. Until then i guess i'll just have to pay for overpriced tiny ass macarons :(. Til we meet again sweet airy delicious macarons. PST.. my cousin tried to eclairs and she said they were pretty good. If that's the case, going to the actual store is going to be on my to do list!

This is a review of their small, to-go locations. There's one upstairs and one downstairs, really close to each other in the Venetian. There is no seating, but there is a shared seating area upstairs. Selection is slightly different at each one. The manager works downstairs, so if you have a 25% off coupon from the Bouchon restaurant, you need to go there to use it. There wasn't a line the times we went. I bought a pain au chocolate (chocolate croissant shaped into a rectangular roll) for breakfast. It was flaky and delicious, however, it needed more chocolate! There were only a few chips...disappointing. However, the other baked goods I got to take home were excellent. First up was a strawberry cupcake. It was gorgeously made and topped with a small chocolate disk. This one tasted like it had buttermilk in the batter. It was moist and ever-so-slightly tangy. Really excellent paired with the strawberry cream. As good as the ones I make! ;) Then, I got 4 different flavors of macarons. The vanilla one was fine, as expected. The chocolate caramel was the favorite. Rich caramel flavors in the filling. Delicious! Strawberry and chocolate were good also. The macarons are about 1/3 larger than the usual. They have a perfect crunchy exterior, the frilly "feet" that are mandatory for macarons, and the right amount of creamy filling. The texture is slightly chewy at room temperature. If you do refrigerate them, make sure they come up to room temp before serving. Overall, expensive, but worth it. Can't go wrong with the cupcakes and macarons.

This place never disappoints me! Their coffee ice cream is my favorite. I've only ever been on Sunday afternoons post-paddle boating. It's super busy each time, but they're fully staffed with friendly folks. It's easy to get overwhelmed by their Instagram worthy treat options, so sticking with a shake or a waffle cone is easiest for me. One day I'll be adventurous with their cereal toppings.

I recently move back to Charlotte from Atlanta for grad school and was happy that they had an Amelies here, but It must be the ambience and the fact that they open 24hrs that keeps me coming here because honestly the food is overpriced, overrated and most importantly, the INTERNET NEVER WORKS!! when I'm here.....EVER! i have to put my hotspot on. I'm done coming here. I am a big fan of coffee shops. I come here to do homework because when i stay home i don't get as much work done as i will at a coffee shop, but yesterday was my last time coming here and spending over $15 for a drink and small pastries that looks like sample sizes. I was taking an exam and the internet failed on me. WTF! this is my first ever review. Get it together.

A long time favorite go to breakfast place in Northridge, CA. Have been waiting patiently for 85c Bakery to open here in Vegas. They're sea salt coffee, taro marble bun, Hokkaido cheese tart, and garlic cheese bun, just to name a few, are broke da mout Onolicious.

The ice cream was great and the customer service was great too. Only reason it's not getting 5 stars at the moment is because I visited at a time when it was super packed with a long line reaching out the door on the other end. So I felt rushed and didn't get time to really soak it in and experience it like I would have liked. Would definitely be back. Hopefully it won't be at a peak moment.

By far the best donuts I have ever seen or eaten In my life. I loved in San Diego for 7 years and was a regular at that location and when one arrived in las vegas I had to make a trip to see if it was just as good, and it was! If you're in las vegas I highly recommend making a trip here and you just have to get there early. They tend to sell out around 11am. My favorites on the menu would have to be the caramelized pineapple, creme Brule and the big poppa tart. Though your safe with picking any flavor because they are all incredibly delicious.

This place is cute, small, and at the heart of downtown phoenix! The staff is friendly, the ice cream is good, and they support local artists. It's quite random. I ordered two scoops of grasshopper mint. DELISH! Jets the random part: they put it in a Chinese food takeout box and garnish with a fortune cookie. HAHA! You go Melt!

Pros: - You gotta try the cannoli if you go. They are just terrific! I'm sure the other baked options are great as well. They looked very good. - My family and I had a spinach bread, cheese pizza, sausage sandwich, and coffee. The food is simple but definitely above average. - Outdoor patio is very comfortable, as is the inside if you prefer some air conditioning on a hot day. Cons: - Nothing food related - if I had to pick a con, it would be that the bathroom is small - but it's a bakery, so no big deal. Overall: a terrific casual spot for a meal and an outstanding dessert.

I was reading all the good review and finally try this place drive thru .The guy who help was not helpful since it was may Firs-time.I order 1 dozen and he fid not even ask me what Flavor I like he just decide for me and charging me $35 bucks .so he gave me the special flavors and regular and the special flavors request punch in but different from the box ..dishonest person .. The cheese cake was good .My kids does not like it..My first and last to this donut place..Nextime ,I just get winchells donuts ..
Good stuff. Nothing else needed. They make good quality ice cream. Ask anyone from Cleveland, and they've been there. I love the peppermint candy cane one in the winter. Really unique.

So we officially have Sloan's and it's inside the grand canal Shops in the palazzo. So before you even see the shop you will smell the heavenly scents of chocolate and ice cream and sweet treats from the hallways leading up to it. I must say that the shop decor is fun and super inviting, it will truly make you feel like a kid in a candy shop and you will just want to buy everything you see So even though everything looked amazing there is no way I can eat that much sweets so I decided on a cookie and brownie and let me tell you there is NO way you can or will be disappointed. The cookie is the best cookie I ever tasted but beware it is super duper rich, the cookies are served warm and they come with big chunk of either chocolate chip or peanut butter cups. I could not even finish the cookie all at one time. Now on to the brownie, it is soft with crispy edges which I love with a moist center full of just rich chocolatey goodness. I had no idea a sweet could be so sweet lol. I would definitely come back again and try those gigantic donuts or some of the home made waffles that smelt like grandmas house or the Carmel apples or homemade ice cream..... fresh there is so many choice that you can't go wrong

I'm so glad I found Sweet Republic with one of my best friends.They have really good ice cream and games that people can play while enjoying their ice cream :) My favorite is the Belgium chocolate in a waffle cone.It is delicious!

People go to Amelie's because it's "cool" and to be frank, it is a pretty cool place. The place is covered in quirky and fun decor from an Etch-A-Sketch art piece to Joseph Ducreux marking where the line for ordering begins. Not to mention there are always a half dozen people on their laptops and usually a guy out in the atrium strumming along his guitar. One might say that at Amelie's you feel cooler than cool. (You might even feel ice cold. Alright, alright?) Amelie's is always packed. ALWAYS. I don't think I've ever seen the place even remotely quiet -- not even during the later hours. Except to wait a while in line to order because yes, it does stretch around to the other room sometimes. While there's no denying Amelie's atmosphere is fantastic, I'm not quiet sure what the hype about their food is all about. Their desserts are pretty hit or miss. The macarons are particularly disappointing. I like my macarons with a hard outer shell and a soft fluffy on the inside. Amelie's macarons have the consistency of hard cookies. I have, however, enjoyed some of their mini cakes and mousse cups. Their non-dessert food (or "non-fun" food if you've got a sweet tooth like me) is pretty solid as well. Be aware that their baguettes are huge and you might want to have a buddy help you out. (Or not. I'm not here to judge.) I'm not a coffee drinker but the my friends that are have not had any issues with the coffee. The tea is also very nice and is loose leaf, not bagged. They also have speciality sodas and drinks that change seasonally. Amelie's isn't too far off in price from Starbucks and while some of their desserts have disappointed me, it's worth stopping here rather than your local Starbucks if you've got the chance. While Amelie's isn't the holy grail of cafes or bakeries, it's worth checking out. Because, afterall, what's cooler than being cool? Amelie's.

This bakery is just a little to-go place, in the middle of the Venetian hotel. They are separate from the Bouchon restaurant (which is upstairs). Their selection is limited unlike their other bakery in Napa. However I make good use of their daily selection of macarons, croissants and pastries. The macarons are huge but their selection is limited with just the basic flavors. When you do have a chance to go to Napa, pls stop by their bakery there. I love their seasonal flavors and my favorite was the Cherry Cheesecake macaron and Monkey Bread. The male barista during my visit was a bit overwhelmed. I ordered chai tea to go and he made me 3, lol. Then he had to deal with the British couple after me, who were angry at him for not allowing them to pay through their hotel bill. WTF? Poor guy. Anywho, their croissants are pretty good and I always order a box to go for my grandma. It can get pretty pricey as these are artisanal baked goods and hand crafted pastries....and of course it's Thomas Keller.

I had higher hopes for Fatty Daddy's based on the reviews here. The good: The fruity pebbles macaroon was nostalgia on my taste buds to the extreme. If I were to come back to this place, it would be for that frigging macaroon only. If you haven't tried this place, I'd say try it once to get a decent macaroon. Also I love that they place a fat marshmallow on top of the whole thing and toast it right in front of your eyes. Amazing. The not so good: Unfortunately, despite the awesome toppings described above, the gelato was lacking. We're from Philadelphia so, FWIW, we know exceptional gelato. This was so lackluster. If I didn't order my own flavors, I honestly would not have known what flavors they were because they were so bland! And they weren't soft like gelato should be. It was weird, hard, flavorless ice cream. I'd say if you haven't been here before, give it at least one try, but maybe keep searching for your dream local cold treat stop.

Oh, Sloan's. Your adorable stuffed creatures and fun decor were enticing enough to reel me in, but your ice cream, though yummy, is incredibly overpriced. A regular 2-scoop cup (as pictured) contains the smallest scoops known to man, and cost me nearly $9. This left me feeling not only disappointed, but still hungry! If I ever stop by again, it'll be to hug a giant Squishable. Even if Sloan's had the most uniquely mesmerizing flavor selection I'd ever encountered, I just wouldn't be able to justify paying this much for such small serving sizes. The other sweets on display seem like they may be more worthwhile, but I'm unsure of the pricing on those; for all I know, it's $20/donut! However, if you're looking for humorous kitchen decor or soft toys for the tiny humans in your life, there might be some value in stopping by after all. The choice is yours, but be sure to proceed with caution.

This is the best soft ice cream. I had the strawberry soft serve in the fish waffle cone which was filled with Nutella. It was warm and rich and so good. You are offered a topping and a cookie or strawberry on the side. So yummy! Highly recommended.

When it's 115 out and you're wishing for something cool, head on over to Sweet Republic! They have a great selection of flavors, sundaes, and shakes. We ordered the Blue Moon & Pineapple Whips and they both left us wanting more please... Thank you Yelp for inviting us to the Sweet Republic Elite function yummmm!

January 31, 2015 Saturday - 11:15 AM snack 2 adults Atmosphere - 5 stars Food - 5 stars Service - 5 stars Background - Walk the Linq promenade and came a cross Sprinkles. I remember now reading that they planned to move in the complex but forget about it until I saw it. Same with the bowling alley. After watching many episodes of Cup Cake Wars with my wife we had to stop here. Atmosphere - Small, Vivid, Clean, and Crisp. No signs of a bakery on property. I did not ask if there was one there, so not certain. Food Drinks - none ordered. My Meal Dessert - My wife ordered the Black and White cupcake and she shared it with me. I can not describe the level of moistness in this cupcake. You just need to try it yourself. It was a ooooeeeeee gooooeeey sponge of chocolate goodness. Side note there was frosting too, but I really did not focus on that. Service - They had two ladies working behind the counter. One worked with my wife getting her food and the other worked with me to settle the bill. Future - Yes, and I will get my own.

Amazing little hole in the wall of of near Freemont. Staff is really quick and efficient at their job as well as just being plain nice. The donut though...they are just decadence in glaze. These things are huge and tasty as all he'll. The bigger ones are bigger than my hand and the smaller ones about the size of a donut from a franchise chain. I'll be coming back in the future when visiting Vegas.

Cute little shop with very creative and thoughtful handmade flavors. The story behind the creation of the Ice Cream Social brand and it's positive contributions to the community makes it so much better. Well worth a visit!

A classic. We have somehow managed to live in Pittsburgh for 27 years, and only discovered Page's this summer. What were we thinking? The line is always long, but it always moves quickly. I stick with the classics -- dip cone, hot fudge sundae-- and I am never disappointed. Love you, Page!

Hands down the best ice cream shop I've been to! They have tons of unique ice cream flavors, soft macarons and top off your creation with a toasted marshmallow. The guy who helped us out (I forgot to get his name) was super friendly and more than happy to let us try any flavor we wanted. My husband and I will definitely be making this our regular dessert place.
Super friendly! Great service! Fantastic flavor options and toppings. Reasonably priced! If there's a line dont worry it moves quick! Worth the drive! Try the dough melt super bomb!!!!

Great food and customer service Went to get some pastries and got the great aspargus spinach leek soup, and a cafe mocha too. Very nice employees, carried my food to my table so I wouldn't spill it. Love that soup and the pastries are always great...
Came here yesterday... I had no idea the donuts were so large lol. My son & I got 1 large each & 1 small. Definitely will be back

The Ice Cream here was amazing!!! A friend, my husband and I took a spontaneous late night trip to an ice cream shop and it turned out to be the best trip ever. Once you get your ice cream you can also take a walk around the area. It's very nice with many other shops around. I come here with my family and friends a lot more.

When we got here there was a line (it was a Sunday afternoon) and it took about 20-30 minutes for us to place our order. We got a salted caramel lobster tail and a red velvet cupcake. The salted caramel lobster tail was great. The red velvet cupcake was okay, I like the red velvet cupcake at Georgetown Cupcake more. But I would go back for the lobster tail! Very limited seating at the bakery.

Definitely a dope spot. Just moved to Charlotte from Florida and I love little coffee shops. Well, this wasn't little and it's a bakery, but it's dope AF. It's in the shape of a snail shell. Lots of spots to sit and have a personal chat. But the best part ... it's open all night!! What a sweet nightmare! I had a latte that had mixed herbs ... LORDT!!! I didn't care that my mouth was burned for almost two weeks after ... and the pastry was amazing. Can't remember what it was called since I was in awe of how pretty it looked... and it tasted just as pretty. I also got lucky because I heard the lines are always very long, but nope. I was the 5th customer in line. Great experience!! I'm definitely coming back here again. By the way, the wall of locks is such a good touch to the spot!

Definitely have to check out their facebook for the flavor of the week! We were there for coffee flavored and it was delicious. I have to go back to check out the lemon, as I have heard wonderful things about it. Definitely worth the drive if you're looking for something different than custard
If you're looking for a spot to bring your kids for a quick treat or if you and your friends want to reminisce about your child hood days, come here and grab a cereal shake

Sweet Treats It has been a very long time since I revisited Mary Coyle's and a few things have changed. Lunch items are no longer offered on the menu, this place had the best BLT sandwich that was loaded with bacon. Even though the lunch items are gone Mary Coyle's is serving up some of the most delicious sweet treats, some of the best ice cream in town. On this visit my lunch companion and I shared the Caramel Cashew "God Bless You" and the "Thick Ol' Fashion Chocolate Milkshake" and both were delicious. The "God Bless You" was the perfect mix of Vanilla & salted caramel cashew ice cream, caramel topping, topped with cashews, whip cream and a cherry on top. The ice cream was smooth, rich and full of flavor as was the chocolate shake. If you're ever craving delicious homemade ice cream, great customer service, and wallet friendly prices, stop in you won't be disappointed.

So many great flavor options there is no way to leave this place without wanting to come back again! Great ice cream, really patient and friendly staff! Hard decision but I went with a peanut butter chip, coconut milkshake! Absolutely delish!! Vote me in for the mayor of the republic

The classic cannoli I had was great! I'm not usually a huge fan of cream-filled pastries but this was delicious, not too sweet or goopy. I also picked up their one pound bag of mixed cookies and biscotti which I brought home to my sister and dad, they loved them. Why the four stars? There was a long line and when I finally got to ordering they were out of lobster tails and it would have been an extra 15 minute wait. Overall, Carlo's did not disappoint and it's cool to be able to say I've tried Cake Boss pastries!

When we first moved to Vegas in 2013 Bouchon Bakery was on our must try list. We've been hooked from our first visit and have been coming here ever since :) Items tried and liked (so far): -Cinnamon Roll -Cheese Danish -Chocolate Chunk Cookie -Oatmeal Raisin Cookie -TKO -Better Nutter -Chocolate Almond Croissant -Kouign Amann -Macaroons -Bouchon Brownies -Bouchon Oh Oh -Croissants -Pain au Chocolait -Pan au Raisin -Coffee Cake -Shortbread -Iced Chai -Sandwiches Usually at other bakeries we try many different items only to be left disappointed and end up liking just a few items. But not here everything we've tried has been delicious and worth every calorie ^-^ Prices are reasonable compared to other bakeries around town. Staff are always helpful, knowledgeable & friendly. Service is quick & efficient. They have a total of 3 bakeries in the hotel but the one located near the Venetian Theatre usually has mostly everything in stock. If they are out of something try one of their other locations. Overall a great place to grab a delicious treat :) I hope you decide to give Bouchon Bakery a try!

Worth the calorie splurge. After longingly staring at this bakery numerous times on our way to our room, I finally decided to induuulge.... Day 1 - Chocolate Almond Croissant. YUM. Flaky and buttery with chocolate and almonds on the outside, and soft and moist with almond filling in the inside. The BF got the cinnamon roll which he enjoyed as well. Day 2 - Almond Croissant. Minus the chocolate and super yummy. In fact, I liked this one better. The BF got the cinnamon roll again. I also got a box of assorted macarons to take home with me. There were 6 of them and they were the biggest macarons I have ever eaten. I loved all of them except for the red one, which I'm guessing was raspberry. Location was convenient since we were staying at The Venetian. Good service and lots of variety to choose from. I can't speak to the prices because honestly when it comes to sweets + vacation, money has no value. There were so many more goodies that I wanted to try. No more longing stares next visit. I'm just going to go for it.

Wish I could give 6 stars! Amazing donuts. We got there around 10 am- rookie move as selection picked over and they apparently don't replenish- what they have is what they sell. Still had enough interesting varieties to make it worth the drive. Don't overlook the glazed- simple but better than any we'd ever had. The kinds with lots of frosting were, as expected, a big hit. Good service, great donuts- what else do you need??

The Mrs. and I stopped by to grab a light breakfast. The coffee was ok and the pastries were good. We split a chocolate croissant and a breakfast sandwich. As others have noted the service wasn't the friendliest. There isn't any seating inside, but have a patio outside with 7-8 tables which was ok since it was a pleasant morning. The issue is there are pigeons lurking everywhere. They will walk right under your feet, occasionally bumping into you. It was incredibly annoying and l couldn't wait to finish up and get going. I know they cannot control nature, but it soured the experience. 3 stars for the food and service, and I'd highly recommend looking for a place inside the Venetian to sit.

So good we almost OD'd on Donuts in our hotel room. I do not think I can actually express in words how much we all loved the Donuts here. I am really glad i live hours away because these things could become a serious problem if they were closer. Also the young woman who helped us was very very sweet (almost as sweet as the custard filled) and knowledgeable about the doughnuts. If I had business in the area i would try and steal her. Next time we are anywhere nearby we will definitely be back.

How could I give bouchon a 3? I've been to the location in Napa and something about this location in the Venetian doesn't cut it. Maybe it's the long lines, slow service, but something about the pastries wasn't 100% satisfying. We had the chocolate croissant, the bouchon (like a brownie) and we purchased a bunch of macaroons (every flavor). Again, it's bouchon so there is a standard here and I am sure you will enjoy it, but given the time tradeoff and plethora of options in Las Vegas I would pass on this location.

When I moved here, Mitchell's Ice Cream was the first thing that I discovered that wasn't just good "for Cleveland," but was good "for the world." It's so delicious. Lots of old standards and nice rotating seasonal flavors. I go here like once a week. It's the jam.

Love this place! Perfect for an after dinner treat while walking around the Linq. Their ice cream is absolutely delicious as well as their red velvet cones! The cupcakes are equally as good and they even offer doggy treats in the form of mini cupcakes.

Definitely not good for kids. Very offensive music playing. I don't think Yelp would let me repeat the lyrics in a review so how is it okay to assault our ears with that shit. It belongs in the club, or at home. I wouldn't take my family here again. My daughter didn't even like her icecream. It was mushy and dripping and she loves almost all icecream. Avoid!
Tried again long line to be expected. But only 2 girls to take orders. One to pay. Really Customer service should be #1priority.

I had high hopes for this after watching Netflix's Chef Table. I really admired Christina Tosi's creativity and hard work but everything we tried were not good at all. I've messed up a lot of cookies but they were edible.. The compost cookie was so hard and tasted like banking soda, we threw it away after a bite. The blueberry and cream was ok and soft but lacking the tasted of blueberry... crack pie was so teeny for $6 but I guess it's The Strip. Buttery but not that amazing. The birthday truffles were ok. The cereal milk with cornflakes was definitely worth it and it tastes exactly what a cereal milk taste like. But other than that.. maybe the NYC location is better.
Great matcha ice cream and even better when it has Ube as the seasonal...although it could be part of the permanent collection. Great service as well and small yet nice store atmosphere

The ice cream is awesome! More recently, i tried that salted chocolate chip cookie.. Oh wow! Melted in my mouth. The salt added this zing of flavor. Ah-mazing The cheesecake brownie was disappointing though. It was too thick and too cakey for my taste. I like a fudgey brownie. Still very flavorful! Next time i'll try the root beer float. They use a fancy bottled root beer. Mmm

Custard isn't really like anything I've tried before. It's rich and creamy. I got chocolate the first time I went there, and I was told by pretty much everyone that I made the wrong choice. Come here for the lemon custard. I haven't gotten into all of the other complicated choices, mainly because the lemon custard on a sugar cone is so darn good! And the prices are extremely reasonable. My one complaint, and it's a small one, is that they don't take credit cards. Oh well, guess I'll have to keep cash around for when the mood strikes!

Love Bouchon! Picked up a chocolate eclair, ham & cheese baguette (heated up on their panini press, yum!), "club" sandwich (also on a baguette, w/ avocado, bacon, sun-dried tomatoes - deeelicious) and 2 macarons - lemon and chocolate. Loved the lemon, which was tart, light and refreshing. The chocolate one was very rich - I had actually ordered raspberry but was given chocolate...didn't discover it until after we left. Be sure to check your bags before you leave the counter! Our goodies totaled up to $30 even - pricey, but a nice once-in-a-while splurge. The bakery is hidden behind some escalators, in front of the Phantom Theatre. No tables or seats, so either head to the food court or to the Coffee Bean on the second floor - not the one right above the bakery (tables are right in front of the counter), but the one around the corner and on the way to the self-parking lot. You'll find 4 or 5 tables that are hidden away from the counter, so you can eat your goodies without feeling embarrassed about being a total squatter.

When in Airport, pitstop at the vending machines! Grabbed a box on the way into Las Vegas for a meeting and the cupcakes were a MASSIVE HIT. Surprisingly fresh...I just assumed they had been up in that little box for a couple days...but I was VERY wrong. Fresh and not at all stale. You aren't going to get all the seasonal and super fancy flavors of a store, but you CAN get a box of all the most important favorites like red velvet.

Ah, Jeni's ... it was hard to buy into all the hype when this upscale, Ohio-based, creamery opened it's first shop in Charlotte's trendy South End. After all, how can a fancy ice-cream shop make any headway in our diet-conscious, calorie-obsessed, fro-yo world? But fear not ... if any ice cream shop is worth all this attention, it's definitely Jeni's. After a couple of recent visits, my kids and I would easily put their flavors among the best we've ever tried.
