BUDDY you need to look at this team and have them take some guest service lessons....it stems from the mangement and flows downhill. If I was going to drop money on over priced desserts because of your Name. ...I'd rather not if getting treated like this

I'm a fan of 85 degrees in general and have visited locations in other states. I had a problem with my order yesterday from this Vegas location. But when I called and spoke with Edna, their manager, she was very quick to help me resolve the issue. She was apologetic for what was a mistake and tried to offer resolution, which I kindly dismissed. The fact that she acknowledged my inconvenience and corrected the problem was more than enough for me. Her pleasant attitude and willingness to ensure customer satisfaction speak volumes. And it is for this reason that they receive my 5 stars.

Cute spot and tasty flavors. If you're downtown for dinner swing by for dessert. Good price and good quality. I got the chocolate and vanilla in the waffle cone. Huge cone -you could easily split with another person.

Love this place! We come here on the regular. Their ice cream is delicious (strawberry shortcake is my fave) and their jasmine milk tea is pretty good too. A HUGE plus that they also have a non-dairy option.
Yummy!!!!! Parking was tough, but that's just the way it is in that neighborhood these days (lots of good restaurants in the ara.....). Good stuff!

I read recently that they were going to clone an Amelie's in the Hyde Park area of Tampa. While I was back in Charlotte, I figured a quick visit to the original Mecca of the Carmel Salted Brownie was in order. This way I could compare and contrast when I searched out the clone. All is quite well with the original. We shared a Turkey & Brie sandwich, a Brie & Apricot tartine, and the obligatory Carmel Salted Brownie. We both left quite content. I'll tell you about the Hyde Park clone soon......

I can't wait for this place is opened in Vegas & they made it. It is one of my favorite place in California with so many location. They are always busy. They have so many bakeries which are hot & fresh made. I came here for birthday cake & bakeries. Everything is so tasty! I always get a good experience with the birthday cake from this bakery. Highly recommend !

My little brother's wife was determined to take me to this French bakery, and I must admit it was my speed. I ordered a mini lemon, raspberry tart and a "create your own" sandwich. I chose the croissant for bread, the turkey for meat, and mozzarella for cheese. Although the sandwich was not filling and there was not an opportunity to order anything with it other than French pastries, I could not complain. Everything was fresh, and I spent $9.00 including my bottle water. The atmosphere was quirky and no two things seem to match which emphasized the quirkiness. The lady who served the pastries was well-educated about the pastries, friendly, and full of "I love my job" kind of energy. By the time I arrived with my party of three at 11:08 pm, the line had snaked to the back of the establishment. Even though the line was rather intimidating, it moved fairly quickly, and that was impressive to me. When my turkey and mozzarella croissant was ready, a server was calmly walking around looking for me. Once again, impressed. Final thoughts: I will go back the next time I am visiting in Charlotte, NC.

A great refugee after galavanting around the downtown area! Housed in the transparent, Scandinavian style interior, you can find amazing decadently smooth homemade ice-cream made here. I recommend trying the Black-Cherry flavor! In comparison, with SF Bi-Rite ice cream, this place has its place on the world's must try ice-cream as well!

My BIL suggested Amelie for dessert after a lovely dinner at Cajun Queen. It's a lively, eclectic space with more seating than it might first appear. That's a good thing, as it seems they're always crowded. Overall, there were things I loved about Amelie but some significant shortfalls too. Menu: A French-inspired listing of sandwiches, salads and soups. There's a daily quiche too and really creative drinks like lavender honey soda. Five stars here. Service: Though its crowded, the line moves fast and the staff is nice. Five stars. Presentation: Just TRY and walk past that pasty case and not order a thing. It's not happening, friends. The devil's winning this round because the offerings are are beautiful. Four stars. Actual taste: Sad trombone noise. For all that the space is cool and the product is beautiful, if it doesn't taste great, well - we have an issue. Sadly, my raspberry rose eclair was the size of a long John and frankly, was overbaked and tasted of neither rose nor raspberry - just sugary sweet donut icing. Sad face. The dessert stuff is all about twice as big as it should be but half as tasty. One and a half stars. I like the 24/7 hours, the space, and the concept. I'll be back to try actual food since it sounded great but I'm a hard pass on the sweets for now.
Now that it is Fall, give the seasonal flavors a try. The pumpkin and pumpkin pecan are scrumptious.
HOLY MACKEREL -- this is the best bakery I've ever been to. Huge con: It's only two blocks from my house, which means I'M GONNA GET FAT.

Yay! A new Somi Somi location! I have been to their Spring Mt location a couple of times, so happy there's a closer one now! They have soft serve with rotating flavors (everytime I go they have had at least one unique flavor!) This time they had Boysenberry/mango swirl, which I'm not sure what boysenberry should taste like, but was super fruity and sweet! I always get the custard filled taiyaki on top of the cup! If you are coming here straight after a meal, be sure to leave some room because it is fiiillling!

Quite possibly the best donuts in Las Vegas. Donut Bar creates super fun & delicious donuts like their maple bacon bar, huge big papa tart or the creme brulee just to name a few. Make sure to come in early because they will sell out, FAST. We've had their donuts in our office multiple times and they're always a nice tasty treat. My favorite is the PB&J. It has real peanut butter in it which I love & the dough tastes just like a cloud. I also have tried some of their coffee before. They use local brews like Vesta which I'm a fan of. If you're a sweets lover this place is a must visit! Also a good hit for impressing your coworkers.

Amelie's is my go-to for French pastries and macarons! I needed several dozen pastries for a work event a few weeks ago, and I was able to place my order online in advance and pick them up at 7:30 - and they looked (and tasted) amazing! I always love trying their seasonal offerings as well - they have great hot drinks and even small meals, and each of their cafÃ© locations has a great quirky vibe.

I drove up on a Tuesday at 6:30pm from Chandler. Easy drive and easy to find. I opted for a waffle cone with Banana, and Mint Chip scoops. The ice cream itself was good; not too sweet, didn't give me indigestion, and was overall good quality. The cone was good, too; light and crispy. My only complaint was that the scoops were extremely small for the price. Overall it was good and I would recommend it.

HOLY VEGAN MOLY, YOU GUYS! FOOD: It's donuts, how special are donuts, right? WRONG. These guys do it big and I mean, BIG. The flavors are unique and tasty and each donut is easily the size of two. Did I mention they have a bunch of vegan donuts too (not just the plain, boring flavors)? Couldn't even tell the difference (being vegan, doesn't make me biased, I swear!). SERVICE: Best service. Everyone was nice and was happy to chat us up. I was with my sister and it turns out two brothers were working there together. NEAT! Also, my sister didn't like the coffee drink she got so a nice woman came over to make it different so my sister could enjoy it. No extra charge and she was totally understanding. PRICE: Who cares? Worth every penny! OVERALL: Like I said to VegeNation a couple blocks over: I love you guys, come to LA?

Obsessed with Churn! Such a perfect ice cream parlor, complete with homemade flavors and cones, a plethora of toppings, fresh baked cookies, expresso bar and tons old fashioned candy. This place is sure to satisfy any sweet tooth. It feels as though you are stepping back in time, to an era when grabbing an ice cream cone was a full throttle experience that encouraged socializing and indulging. Besides the perfect ambiance, the ice cream is unbelievably delish! My favorite is Butter Pecan, but you can't go wrong with any choice Churn! (Great chocolate milkshakes too!)
Two dollar Tuesday's is what it's all about! All their flavors are to die for! You must check this place out if you haven't already. Service is always friendly and fast too!

Cute decor with tons of space and varied seating. The array of macaroons is out of this world. They don't have Green Tea Matcha Latte's which is quite strange to me personally. They do carry a variety of green tea options. I had a breakfast sandwich once which wasn't appetizing. It was supposed to be an egg sandwich, however it tasted like the plastic variety they serve at McDonalds.

After watching the Christina Tosi episode on Chefs Table, I knew I had to try that crack pie and birthday cake. I was already planning my trip here the next time I'd be in Vegas. We drove all the way from San Diego for the Super Bowl weekend, and this was our first stop on the strip. I love walking around the pretty Cosmopolitan hotel lobby already, and so it was a bonus that this place is here. My husband wanted to try the cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes, and I got a slice of crack pie and a slice of birthday cake. 1. Birthday cake: it was OK - not something extraordinary or out of this world, it it tasted just like a boxed funfetti cake mix, but elevated to culinary pastry chef standards (which was what she was going for). I'm just not a fan of that particular flavor of cake, but my favorite part about it was the cream cheese frosting in between layers 2. Crack pie: good, but in my opinion WAYYYY too sweet! It would be a good pairing with some strong black coffee to cut the sweetness a little bit. I was looking forward to trying this the most, but sadly it was way underwhelming. 3. Soft serve: The surprise of the day. I didn't think I would like it, but this was my favorite thing I tried. The cornflake-flavored milk in the ice cream really did take me back to my childhood and it was just the right amount of sweetness If I ever come back again I'd get the soft serve and maybe try the birthday cake truffles.

Visited the bakery and tried the famous lobster tail. It was delicious and I was bummed I didn't buy more. It was one of the best baked goods I have ever had! Also purchased a Carlos Bakery mug and love using it for my morning coffee! I didn't buy as much as I hoped here and completely regret it now. I can't wait to visit Vegas again and come back to the bakery! Next time I definitely want to try the restaurant too!!

Warm doughnuts stuffed with ice cream? Wow!! The ice cream scoop in a waffle cone is delish. Friendly, teeny tiny place. A variety of sinful ice cream flavors. There is WWII history about the hut. You can enjoy your novelty on the patio with your dog.
i freaking LOVE this place! The employees are so nice. the environment is clean and everyone seems so delighted over their cute little treats!

Is the heatwave burning up your body? Well, this place will bring a wonderful cool breeze to your exhausted soul. I personally had a banana split and it was absolutely amazing. I would recommend these icy treats to anyone who is in the mood for a dessert.

Wow! This is my second time here at Handel's and it's just as great as the first. The flavor section is vast and delicious. I tried the 4 scoop sampler (great deal) and ended up falling in love with the New York Cheesecake. If you like cheesecake, you will be hooked. Seriously, it's to die for. I want to eat for breakfast and pretty much any meal. Not only are the flavors rich, but it tastes fresh. You can tell they aren't playing around with the ingredients. The line is always long, but you know it's because of the high quality product. Don't be discouraged of the line because the staff is quick. Not to mention the window staff is friendly and courteous. On top of that the prices are amazing! Don't hesitate-check out Handel's!!!!

Easily the best ice cream I've ever had. I love their Campfire S'more Sundae, complete with homemade marshmallows, but most visits I just stick to the salted caramel. It's pretty much the perfect ice cream. Everything they make is high quality, delicious, and they always have new flavors to try. It's become my go to when I want something sweet. Why bother with something that's not worth the calories? Can't recommend them highly enough. Cute little store, great ice cream, great service. Not a single complaint to be found. Great work.

Love this place! My mom and I go every time we are in Vegas! Usually not long of a wait and the pastries are always up to par! I recommend the Rasberry linger cookie and the lobster tail, some of the best pastries I have ever had!

Amazing little gem, doughnuts stuffed with locally made (in house) ice cream. You really can't go wrong but they excel. Tried both the lavender honey I've cream and the cantaloupe sorbet, both winners. Support local! And check out wayword Taphouse in the same complex or a grab a new plant at Pueblo nursery across the street.

I came here on a rainy day because why not right? I got the black raspberry chocolate chunk in a waffle cone. It was delicious! The chocolate chunks were nice and soft and the ice cream had a great black raspberry taste. There was a line when I went but it went by quickly. There are many flavors to choose from. I asked two guys in front of me if they had any recommendations and one of them said that the black raspberry chocolate chunk is one of his favorites. He was right.

Ok first off, this place SMELLS like heaven! (What I imagine heaven smells like, anyway) The line was quite long for pastries. I waited about 20 minutes before it was my turn but it was well worth the wait. There's so many desserts to choose from, but I chose a regular cannoli, chocolate cannoli, white chocolate mousse cake and a hazelnut cream puff. I really wanted a black and white cookie but unfortunately they were sold out for the day. Everything I chose was delicious! My favorite would have to be the white chocolate mousse. At $9.95 I was a bit skeptical on whether it would be worth the money but I'd happily pay this again. I may have eaten the whole thing by myself.............. Not sorry. The cannolis were awesome. They tasted homemade, as they should. I preferred the regular cannoli over the chocolate covered one. I recommend letting them sit out like 10 mins before eating them because when they're straight from the fridge it's a bit hard to bite into. It tasted better when thawed out :) Good thing I don't live near Carlo's because I'd be super fat if I did (but I'd be happyyyy)!

I am so happy that Mary Coyle has returned to the valley! Their ice cream is still super tasty, but I'm sad that their new location has basically no ambiance whatsoever. All the personality of a hospital cafeteria. But what's really important is that a Phoenix staple is back in business- and just as tasty as ever! I can only assume that updates to the restaurant will come with time.
Handel's is so worth the wait. There's almost always a line and for good reason. The ice cream is so good and there's such a wide variety. I've never been disappointed.

Amazing donuts for affordable prices. I went in around noon, and they had a special of buy 1 get 1 free OR buy a box for $10. I'm not a huge donut fan because bread + lots of sugar makes me feel sick so I only got 2! (They close until all the donuts are all sold) FOOD 5/5: -Creme Brulee ($2): This is what their famous for because INSIDER FOOD showcased this particular donut online and it became a hit! I LOVED it, I'm a fan of regular creme brulee, and they did an amazing job of filling the cream inside the donut & having a sweet/crunch on the top. -Old Fashion Glazed (Free): This was fantastic! If your not into all the sweetness and bread, I strongly recommend this donut. Simple but very good. SERVICE 5/5: -Right when you get in your greeted by smiles and whoever is working is more than happy to recommend what they're most famous for & what flavors you like!

Woohoo! What a treat by UIUC! They feature a new custard flavor every week, and last week it was cake batter, although the sample I tried of it tasted like french vanilla. The custard texture is smooth and creamy, and not too sweet. Their menu houses a variety of frozen treats, from custard, to snowstorms, to floats, and cakes. I got the coffee oreo snowstorm, and it was delish! Don't underestimate the sizes! I got a 12oz, and it was more than I anticipated. The snowstorm wasn't as thick as a DQ blizzard, but it was light and creamy, easy to finish. They also have a drive thru! The building itself looks like a diner, bringing with it an old school charm. Jarling's you are darling. If you're looking for a cool treat in the humidity, think no more and come to Jarling's!

This place is super mediocre. I had one of the cookie cups, and while I do appreciate the care behind the freshly toasted marshmallow on top, the macarons were nothing special, and the ice cream was really, REALLY sugary and not creamy at all. The texture of the ice cream was far too watery. I will not be back.

MACAROONS!!! 4 days in Vegas and I made it a point to stop here just for those delicious macaroons I keep reading about. There's no secret, macaroons are just simply heavenly and to die for but these were probably the best I've ever had, no lie. The filling was a little more buttery which I loved because it contrasted with the sweet crispy cookie perfectly. I splurged and bought 2 gift boxes, one of the mini's and one regular sized. At first glance, the prices may shock you but for the size of the cookie and quality in taste, it's well worth it. I didn't actually get to eat most of them until I got home since I was stuffing my face with everything else on the strip haha. Scared that the cookies would lose the crispiness, I literally scarfed down my macaroons in a few days. I was surprised though on the fourth day, the cookies were nearly fresh still. From experience, I haven't had any macaroons stay edible for more than one or two days (if they weren't eaten yet!). Next time I will try the cupcakes and such and hopefully not stop by on a full tummy. Be back in a few months maybe??..

Came here after dinner to have ice cream. The special flavors like pistachio ate delicious and the portions are very generous. My friend had the vanilla and chocolate and they were really rich and tasty.

Really great place to go came in got some ice cream with the fiancee. Kimmy behind the counter was very sweet and nice. She was very helpful with letting us try some samples before purchasing which was a really cool. Definitely check this spot out when you are in Scottsdale
Delicious treats, eclectic decor. They have a good selection of gluten free dessert options and sandwiches.

I love this place so much I'm always here getting some fresh bread and treats weather it be breakfast or a snack it's definitely a go too place for me and they also have the best teas and coffees here they are always so refreshing and fresh tasting definitely my favorite tea and bakery

There's no such thing as a "lucky" blood sugar crash, but while walking around the Linq and riding the High Roller, my blood sugar took a sharp dive. Now, there is definitely no shortage of options, but I insisted on going to Sprinkles and fortunately there wasn't a line. A blueberry cupcake and some milk helped me make a delicious recovery. The cupcakes here are fantastic, the only problem I had was deciding which one to get, I wanted to try them all, sadly there's no way of doing that and maintaining your dignity. But I did take a four pack home with me, the cupcakes stayed good during the long summer drive and when I had the last one 5 days later, it was still delicious. Sprinkles' fame and reputation are well deserved!
Awesome flavor options!!!! We opted for captain crunch fatty daddy. Loved the ice cream and marshmallow but didn't love the macaroons. Will for sure be back to try other flavors.

The cookies, cakes and cereal milk soft serve are to die for at this window kiosk establishment. Lines can be long and it is sometimes difficult to read the menu and specials with so many people around. But the desserts are decadent!

Great bakery inside the Venetian (there are two locations). Coffee is very good and baked goods sublime. We did take out breakfast here a couple times ... the croissants are buttery and flaky. Also had the almond croissant, blueberry muffin, cinnamon roll and a little pastry that I cannot remember the name of ... all were delicious and a quick bite to tide us over between buffets and large meals!

We've been to to the Amelie's uptown on College St and on Pineville-Matthews Rd (51) and both are very good. The food is good and the desserts are excellent. Not a fancy restaurant but who cares, the food makes up for that.
Best frozen custard in town. After a visit to Hessel park we always get Custard Cup. It's a tradition. Also love the nostalgia.

Great place with some of the best croissants I've had since France. The cookies are equally as good. I haven't had the fruit tarts yet, but they look amazing. The space is fun and comfortable. It's an old warehouse building in Noda that has been renovated. This means I'll be by there everyday on my way to work! :-) But seriously, the croissants are super...light, flakey, and you can taste the butter!!!!

This place is worth finding! Up an escalator and down a hallway that leads outside is where you'll find Carlo's. Small? Yes, it's very small, but kust the right size to get in and out. A little pricey IMO, but everything was fantastic. I would go again, but i'll leave a trail of breadcrumbs to find my way back to the casino.

I stopped in for a sweet treat and picked up a pint of almond buttercrunch and peaches and cream. I also got two scoops: one strawberry balsamic and strawberry cream (???). The strawberry ones were delicious, although I would have liked a bit more balsamic swirl in the first one. The light, sweet, creamy flavors in both were well fresh and flavorful. It was a nice change from chocolate. I devoured half of the almond butter crunch in one sitting and could've eaten the entire pint if I hadnt forced myself to put it back in the freezer. The abc was creamy with nice hints of butter and delightful crunchy toffee bits. I love their merch and almost walked out with a hat and tee. Maybe next time when I run out of ice cream!!

Bit of a disappointment. I got a single scoop ice cream cup and a lollipop for my son. Came out to about 9 bucks with a tip. Call me crazy but 9 bucks for a scoop of ice cream and a freakin sucker is crazy. I will say the ice cream was very good and the feel of the place was really cool. Cool idea having a ice cream parlor with an old school feel to it. Too bad the prices aren't on par with the old school vibe. Churn is not for me.
Unbelievably delicious and unique. I've been to VooDoo donut and this place tops it in deliciousness. Not only that, but the staff and owner were so friendly and welcoming!!

I was so excited to finally see 85 coming to Vegas! Unfortunately my last visit left me missing the california locations. Most of the staff is new so they are really slow in packaging the items and checking out customers. I noticed one cashier had to constantly stop and ask what code was for each item. I understand it's a newly open shop but it was almost ridiculous how much time they'd spent chatting or doing other things before taking the next customer. The lines were out the door and there were only 2 cashiers servicing the entire night. As for the food, it's 85! It was tasty but not worth standing in a line for. I'm glad they're open but there's a lot of room for improvement.
MOST delicious milkshake I think I have ever had. I loved the shake with Glenlivet in it. I loved it so much I had it every day I was in Las Vegas. Be sure to try at least one cookie.

Coffee was good, but the almond croissant was the best almond croissant I've ever had. Crispy, flaky, buttery and worth every calorie. This is a great place to run in and grab a pastry and a coffee to begin your walk down the strip. I want to go back and have every pastry on their menu.

I love everything about this ice cream spot. I love it's central neighborhood location which makes it great for walking or biking too. I love the vibe of its pretty large patio on a summer night. And I love the ice cream. The flavors change frequently and there certainly are unique ones on the list. There are vegan flavors as well and unlike other popular ice cream places they change frequently too and there are always a handful of options. I've had vegan ice cream at various places around town and I would rate the texture / consistency of the vegan ice cream here #2 in town. But because of the flavor variety and rotation this place is my #1 go to for ice cream.

This ice cream is AMAZING!!! The line to get ice cream is always out the door...sometimes around the corner. It's that good!! They have so many different flavors and types - dairy and non-dairy. Don't be fooled - the non-dairy is just as good as the dairy! The smell of the homemade waffle cones draw you in and prepare you for an experiencel! The location is great - in the middle of SouthEnd on Camden. Parking is located in the street, but it may take a while to find a space, as there are many other establishments around. Uber or scooter is easy. Must go to Jeni's!

Honestly... I ordered the b-day cake because the cashier said it was the most popular item on their menu. Walmart b-day cake tastes better! Their cake was dry and the butter cream was extremely sweet. Also ordered a cereal milk shake and threw that out after a sip. Wasted $45 including tip. I did it so you don't have to.
Great ice cream and not overly pricey, great place to come with the family. The Yumee Buns are delicious.
Bold statement: Mason's has the best salted caramel ice cream I've ever had. The staff is helpful and vibrant, and the flavors this week (including Thai Tea) won my heart over.

Every time we're in Little Italy, we make a trip to Prestis. We love the antipasti and the pre-made hot items. Particularly the breads and Stromboli. But the real star: the sauce and the cookies! They have a huge selection of baked goods and Italian cookies. My Italian boyfriend was like a kid in a candy store. We ordered cookies for his family and they loved every single one! If you're ever in little Italy, Prestis is a must visit!

It has a small indoor space, but is ideal in the summer. It's a bit pricey, but the ice cream is delicious. It isn't as good as honey hut, but it's very high quality. The staff is friendly, and I definitely recommend trying a few flavors before deciding!

Great quality and great concept! The Butterwood Bake Consortium has decorated the space nicely and would be the perfect venue for coffee, team, and sweets while catching up with a friend, holding a business meeting, or celebrating a success. It's a great (and cute) alternative to your typical coffee shop or happy hour. My friends and I tried the pumpkin bread mini loaf, chocolate cake with peanut butter frosting, and pour over coffee. We enjoyed everything, and I'm looking forward to my next visit! My one criticism (and the reason for four instead of five stars) is the lack of posted coffee menu paired with an employee's pretentious attitude. The baked goods are all labeled, but there is no posted menu of their coffee/tea/drink options that I saw. This led my friend to ask for a regular coffee, to which the employee responded that they only offer a "regular espresso menu". I wouldn't consider the definition of that to be common knowledge to the average customer. When my friend replied "drip coffee", the employee repeated that they only offer a regular espresso menu. My friend and I had to ask what the options were that would be similar to a drip coffee in order to be given some options. She never ran through the options and could have definitely handled our interaction in a less condescending manner. I'm sure employees get tired of running through the menu over and over, and think that a clear posting of the entire menu could easily avoid a repeat scenario!

The two employees we dealt with were surly. My chocolate croissant was kind of dry. My partners Croque Monsier was delicious as was our French Lavender Lemonade. We would go back, but I definitely think a refresher of customer service is in order (old lady at register, and younger chick with braids running food I'm looking at you..)

My girlfriend was hungry for dessert after a D'Backs game on Tuesday, but it was almost 10pm. I wasn't optimistic we'd find a dessert spot downtown that late on a week night. But low and behold, Yelp saved the day and helped me find this place just a few blocks from my apartment. They've only been open about 2 months, but per the Yelp reviews already seemed to be garnering a fan base. The place sits in a historic home pretty much in the heart of First Fridays territory. In case you get lost looking for this place, just look for the neon "Munchies" sign. When we walked in it was just the owner (who also happens to be the owner of JoBot Coffee). Super nice guy. They don't make their own ice cream, but rather have it made by a local co-op. Their flavors range from Chocolate Raspberry to Chips & Salsa. After sampling seemingly every flavor, I went with a scoop of Cinnamon and a scoop of Vanilla Birthday Cake. When you order a cup as I did, you don't get a cup but rather a Chinese noodle box complete with fortune cookie. Random? Yup. But freaking awesome. She got the Chocolate Superfarm and the Raspberry. There's no seating inside, but there's plenty on the front porch. We were the only ones there (not surprisingly since it was so late on a Tuesday), but thoroughly enjoyed the ice cream and overall experience. Great way to cap off the evening.

I was super excited to try the pastries here but I was so disappointed. The pastries look ok and taste like the typical grocery store pastries. I was hoping to try new flavors. Nothing special just waste of money! Won't ever go back!

Shall we Dance? (*) There's a huge difference between self-love and pity... So, if you ARE going to spend Valentine's Day by yourself eating ice cream directly from a pint - you might as well make those calories count with great ice cream. In which case, you can't go wrong picking Sweet Republic (consistently on the "best ice cream shops across America" lists) as your dance partner. There's an art to selecting your partner in tango. You can't simply send a cheap "You up?" text message. That's a different game... In Argentina, the process is called Cabeceo (Spanish for 'head', again: your mind. gutter. Keep out of...). Respecting tradition, I followed the proper process on Valentine's Day: First, I surveyed my available options. Gingerbread (hmm: a flavor I usually love, but this one lacks boldness). Apple pie (better, but mainly due to Caskwerks Distilling Apple Pie liqueur than chunks of pie). Pumpkin Spice (Nice: cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, allspice, cardamom, cloves...). Huckleberry Swirl (Great: wild mountain berries from Oregon). But, the day demanded something extra special, and so my attention turned to the Coconut Cashew Curry. But, before I made flirtatious eye contact, I quickly pondered whether my attraction was prompted simply by the exotic flavors that have been tempting me lately (Earl Grey Sriracha? Everything bagel?). So, was it just the charm of something very different from what I'm used to? Or, does the flavor itself have substantive merit. No other way to find out than a quick whirl. Ahh... like a sultry siren, there's a mystique and depth to the Coconut Cashew Curry. The curry felt more Japanese than Indian. There's enough cashew mixed in to unveil a sweet but nutty profile. The heat builds up slowly but doesn't burst into flames in your throat. Leading to a complex, sweet-heat finale that's both satisfying and yet leaves you gasping for more. More! More ice cream... Every addict should consider whether he/she is spiraling downward to a situation where one needs a stronger dose just to get the same satisfaction. Well aware of my ice cream addiction and preference for complexity, I decided to mix things up, going with a flavor I haven't had in years (but highly recommended by co-owner, Helen Yung): Brown Butter Pecan. Personally, the desserts I like best, are the ones that make me both feel AND think. And they usually remind me of a pleasurable moment from the past (That Proust guy was on to something. But, poor guy only had Madeleine(s) to tempt him...). In my case, the Brown Butter ice cream reminded me of my favorite Indian dessert: Ras Malai (milk, corn flour, sugar, saffron, pistachio) - which is the highest compliment I can give Sweet Republic, given my impossibly high standards for the Indian dessert (there was a year when I tried Ras Malai at 100+ different shops and restaurants in NYC). But, the association was prompted by the elements: milk, cream, sugar, nuts (pecan in this case)... and mostly the texture. To me: a great Ras Malai straddles the borders of solid and liquid states of nature, and just surrenders completely to the tongue upon contact. Similarly, I think the best ice cream is also one which is slowly melting, and doesn't have to be coaxed to become one with your soul. Completely enraptured by the ice cream, the tango morphed over time to the meditative abandonment of the ego in the Semazen - performed by the whirling dervishes... So, what I mean to say is: Yes. I got completely carried away and ate more than half a pint of the Brown Butter Pecan. But, dessert should never make you feel bad. Even if one gives of oneself completely on a first date. For, you can always walk away your guilt later - and be thankful, that it's no walk of shame... (*) Sharu wi Dansu (Japanese, 1996) - not the pathetic 2004 remake with Richard Gere and J-Lo

There's a lot of hype about this place, and as far as I can tell, a lot of it is undeserved. Maybe it's just that Phoenix has such a lack of locavore / foodie joints that people are so enthusiastic about its arrival, but the ice cream is decent at best. Definitely better than Coldstone and the like, but compared to the other ice creameries it aspires to, the ice cream is just not there. The flavors are REALLY one-dimensional: everything takes like a sweet cream base with maple / mint / chocolate / whatever else mixed in.
I'm not sure how people like this stuff, it's like uncreamy artificial flavoured ice cream. Worse than a tub of supermarket icecream, I guess the appeal is the location/variety?

OMG I really thought they only served ice cream that tastes this good in heaven. 'Who'd a thunk' of putting REAL mint in Mint Chocolate Chip Ice Cream. Ben and Jerry....you've been replaced by Jan and Helen! Give them a couple more years and these former New York Stock Brokers will be ringing the bell on WALL STREET when Sweet Republic goes public! My only complaint is that I just wish they were located across the street so I could walk for ice cream....every day!

Disclaimer: I want to try this place at the right time and redo this review! Came in on a Saturday night and there were literally only 6 flavors in the ice cream freezer (all of which were near empty) and a lot of other products were sold out. My friends sucked it up and got a Peanut Butter & Jealous shake mixed with other flavors I can't remember and the other got two HEAPING scoops of a berry ice cream for himself. I must say, they looked good. So 1 measly star for having so much out-of-stock, but I will visit again and I will have ice cream! Hopefully.

I am SO hooked on this ice cream! I had the blueberry soft serve a few years ago with a friend, and loved it! I hadn't been back until a few weeks ago when I was bike riding on the trail nearby. Over the train tracks I spotted the Page's ice cream cone sign. I couldn't figure out how to get off the trail and over to the ice cream shop until I saw a man cross the railroad tracks eating an ice cream cone. Apparently other people had the same idea as I did. I left my boyfriend with the bikes and ran across the tracks and over to Page's. I got him a blueberry soft serve and I tried the toasted coconut. OMG the toasted coconut is unreal. It tastes like a toasted coconut donut. I am obsessed. When I posted photos, I got so many responses asking if I got the dairy free. I didn't even realize they had that! When we went yesterday, I ordered the dairy free (oat based) made into toasted coconut and dipped in chocolate (shoutout to Angie C. for the suggestion). My boyfriend tried the raspberry cheesecake arctic swirl and my brother tried the warm Nancy B's chocolate chip cookie sundae. Everything was great (and huge portions). The warm cookie sundae was enough for 2-3 people to share. The dairy free ice cream I got was perfect. This is absolutely my new ice cream order. We waited in line for about 20 minutes, and when we left the line was much longer. Side note- they do accept credit cards now. This place is worth the wait!

Ok, let's just face it, I'm staying fat forever because it's not worth giving up places like this. I'm a huge ice cream fan and Mitchell's did not disappoint. Had a triple: Rocky Road, Salted Caramel and PB Cup. Favorite was PB Cup! Looking forward to bringing the kids here!
Out of the birthday cake when I arrived. Tried the birthday cake truffle instead and was not impressed--just overly saccharine, nothing interesting about it. Over rated!

I was a bit disappointed. I love the show and been waiting to travel to New Jersey to visit this place. I order the Lobster Tails and Crumb Cake. Either didn't actually move mountains for me. For the price I paid for 2 lobster tails and 1 crumb cake $20bucks seem to be very expensive and I was surprised at the flavor....didn't seem fresh....a total disappointment. The ticket system they have seems to help keep the massive crowd controlled but I have to say the wait time to order is a bit long. Hopefully things are better at the actual venue in New Jersey. Gonna give them one more chance. Still love the tv show though.

Don't miss their waffle cone. I've never had a better waffle cone. It has flavor and texture and it's really the only time I've ever liked a waffle cone. Also the butted pecan is the best pecan ice cream I've ever had. It's rich and sweet and creamy and full of pecans. I loved it. I also got a scoop of the black sesame seed ice cream. It wasn't great. Not a lot of flavor. That Japanese grocery store in Tempe sells black sesame ice cream that is better than this. The employees were wearing masks and super helpful. They have 6 foot markings designated on the floor. They seemed to be acting cautiously. Anyway, I'll definitely be back for more pecan ice cream.

I wanted to try Sprinkles for years before I actually did. So, when I finally bought a couple cupcakes from a location in L.A. at first I was like, that's it? That is because I tried the vanilla first. Later I had the red velvet and fell in love! I was so happy when I heard we were getting a location in Vegas. Finally! It def makes sense. Our location is the best. It's located at The Linq. Usually when something is on the strip, it seems like a hassle to make a trip to just the one location you need but the location is pretty convenient. If you park in the lot behind the high roller, it takes a couple minutes to walk there, so you can be in and out in less than 15 minutes if there isn't a crazy long line. The store is set up with cupcakes on one side and ice cream on the other. I tried the ice cream once, but found myself eating around it to get to the cupcake that was on the top and bottom of the scoop of ice cream lol. My absolute favorite flavor is Red Velvet. It's the best I have ever had. They have plenty of other flavors that change daily, but I stick with what I love. Another bonus, is the cupcake ATM. If the location is closed or if it's late and they are out of a certain flavor, you can go to the ATM! Not to mention, it's super cute buying a cupcake from it. It's a little more expensive, maybe fifty cents, because they charge for the single cupcake box. It's so worth it though. Sprinkles also offers delivery and curb side pickup from their app or website. I haven't tried either, but it seems like a nice option!

If you're looking for a sweet spot that truly captures the heart of what Pittsburgh is, look no further than Page Dairy Mart. Is there a long line? Don't worry. It goes fast, and besides, you'll need the extra time to decide... There's just about any ice cream treat you can dream up (and more). To start, there are a zillion flavors of soft-serve, from Pistachio to Toasted Coconut. Just try to think up a topping or Arctic Swirl mix-in that they don't offer! There are even several sprinkle varieties to choose from. We can't not talk about their incredible lineup of unique Pittsburgh-inspired sundaes and seasonal treats. Page Diary Mart features local baked goodies too--like blondie brownies and cookies from Nancy B's and the famous Burnt Almond Torte from Prantl's. This is the REAL Pittsburgh: a legendary sweet treat tradition. You can keep your fancypants lavender and green tea flavors, your rolled ice cream novelty... take me to the ice cream joint by the river with the neon signs and the 900 flavors and the oversized servings I can share with my favorite people.

My wife and I went to Postinos and were given a flyer promoting this place. A few days later we were going to go out for gelato when we decided to try something different instead and drove over to Churn. The parking situation was a hot mess with valet or parking down a residential street being the only two options. I am sure the neighbors are not impressed with the ramshackle of cars cruising up and down their street looking for a parking space. We were one of many looking for a spot. My wife convinced me this was worth the effort so I continued to look for parking. After a few tries we parked down the street and made our way inside. The place is tiny, with an old style ice cream shop look but no "feel". The place is kinda sterile, but from the reviews others find it charmimg. Not sure why, the place is landlord white with glass candy jars filled with candy. Someone compared it to Farrell's but I would have to completely disagree. This place lacks the utter feeling of immersion of someplace grand, different, exciting that I remember when I walked into a Farrell's. This was more like blank ice cream shop with candy jars on display. Also if you get cold easily then bring a sweater, my wife was chilled after waiting in line for 15 minutes to get served. The service was friendly, my wife ordered chocolate with salted caramel topping. The salted caramel topping was waaaay to salty for my taste. It tasted like caramel for a second, then you were hit with nothing but pure salt taste - like licking a slab of salt - literally. This ruined both the chocolate and the caramel. Her scoop was just plain awful and had that been the extent of our experience I would have given the place 1 star. Seriously, it was that bad. I ordered the Vietnamese coffee and Madagascar vanilla 2 scoop in a cup with no toppings. They were both good, although nothing special. The two stars is based purely on the two scoops I ordered. Also I did have a bit of the ice crystal problem in my two scoops. I am not a big fan of ice crystals in my ice cream. It reminds me of the old box of 1.00 bargain ice cream one forgot was in the freezer but eaten anyway to cure that sweet tooth six months later. I will also say my wife's one scoop was as big a serving as my two scoops. I was not a happy camper. Over-all Churn is ok, nothing less-nothing more. My wife's ice cream was a disaster of flavors. Mine was small and good but nothing out of the ordinary. 2 solid stars. (See the potential 1 star review above) In all fairness my wife would have given this place 3 solid stars based on my two scoops.

Been wanting to try this place forever! Finally got a chance and it didn't disappoint. Cute little storefront inside Cosmopolitan. It's right between the Juice standard and momofuku just in case you pass it. Everything is pretty much cereal based. Soft served ice cream, cookies, cereal toppings, and different pies. Plenty of options to choose from and different ways to make it. I had the milkquake which is soft-served ice cream with pie or cookie chunks blended in. I had the crack pie which is a salted caramel flavor and it was spot on for flavor. Only thing I would ask is to make the chunks of crack pie smaller. For me the milkquake size was big enough for two people. My husband and I shared one and we didn't even finish it. I would definitely recommend this place!

My husband heard a lot of good news about this place so we decided to check it out. Maybe we went at a bad time but I was left unimpressed. Two of our donuts were dry and the other three were pretty forgettable. I ate half of mine (the maple cake) and threw the rest in the trash. Almost tasted stale! The other one (rainbow sprinkles) was pretty average. My husband enjoyed his donuts but didn't think he'd be coming back again. Maybe donuts just aren't my thing but I don't know what all the hype is about.

This place exceeds expectations, the customer service is phenomenal and the donuts were HUGE!! I tried the delicious raspberry iced with pistachio nuts, it looked fake, like a Homer Simpson donut, but the taste was as far from 'fake' as you can imagine! It was moist, sweet (not overly sweet) and melted in my mouth. I know this place is very popular and sells out quickly, so thankful I got to try one!!

I don't come to Vegas without stopping here first! After eating here I never eat donuts anywhere else. Great service, charming location (their back patio is lovely), and THE DONUTS ARE SIMPLY AMAZING! They live up to the hype! Creme brÃ»lÃ©e and peanut butter cup are probably my two favorites but any donut they have is soooo worth the calories! Also, if they still have donuts left later in the day sometimes you can get a box for $10 but those are rare occasions!

Went here twice while visiting the area. Got the Turtle, loved it. Next time I got the double trouble and loved it as well. Ice cream has great flavor. Staff was attentive and good both times. Strongly recommend.
Today we were in this place and it has been great experience. You can see the factory trough a glass and the ice cream is delicious. My favorite berry chocolate chunk.

I have ordered cupcakes from this bakery twice through DoorDash and both times I get cookies. I want a refund for both orders but they are closed. No answer by phone. DoorDash won't respond either. Every time I call this bakery they don't answer.

What a truly unusual place. In another town you'd see this place and say "they are trying too hard to be funky/cool." Here in Charlotte I'm here to tell you is the real deal. They walk the talk and just serve up great baked goods and coffees/teas. 24/7. Didn't expect to find something so authentic to itself while on a short trip but this is it. Don't miss it if you come to Charlotte.

I got mint chip and hazelnut chocolate ice cream, with a lemon macaroon and toasted marshmallow and it was soooo good! Portion sizes were perfect imo & staff was friendly. I also like how it's kinda hidden - feels like only locals know about it.

I've only had their macarons and I already love this place. They are so big and chewy. I love it when macarons have a chewy texture instead of being too soft. My favorite flavors are vanilla, coffee, and the salted caramel. Definitely worth trying!

This place has really good ice cream! They use real fruits and make it in front of you! They give you a lot too! The atmosphere is really nice with a weird Japan/Hip vibe to it! It's super cute! They also have board/card games available to kill time and have a good time!

I've written a review of Donut Bar in San Diego. Well, we were visiting Vegas and stumbled across the Donut Bar while driving around and exploring. I had my husband stop immediately and I got out of the car and checked the business hours. We were staying at the Aria and planned to wake up early to ensure I didn't miss out on the creme brÃ»lÃ©e donut that I missed out on while in San Diego. The next morning, we drove to Donut Bar and there was no line. Talk about excited!!! Again, the employees were warm, welcoming, and patient. The service was cheerful and the employees were all smiles. On to the donuts. Needless to say, these donuts are great. This time we bought the strawberry split (our fave), the apple crumb (hubby barely tasted it last time cuz I ate it), the salted caramel, and of course the creme brÃ»lÃ©e. The strawberry split is our absolute favorite!!! The donut is light and the filling is light and airy without being overly sweet and the fresh strawberries brings it all together. The apple crumb is more like a light cake that has a hint of apple. The salted caramel is like a glazed donut but the glaze it caramel. This donut was good but I think a little more restraint on the salt would balance it better. It wasn't my favorite but it was good. Now on to the donut that got me up early in the morning, the creme brÃ»lÃ©e! This donut was actually really good but I'm still partial to the strawberry split. At first glance, it looks like a typical filled donut with a hard glaze. I cracked the glaze and opened the donut to expose the creme filling. Creme brÃ»lÃ©e is my favorite dessert and I was pleasantly surprised to find that the custard was spot on. Without a doubt, I will be returning to the Donut Bar!

Normally, I love SomiSomi. So much I wanted to get gift cards for whole bunch of graduates and birthdays. When I walked in, I asked if I could buy some gift cards. The person at the register said they don't do gift cards, but they have a QR code. I asked how can I give gift amount if I don't have email addresses? She responds that she is sorry and she has never done it before. She let me just walk out. This store lost some money from me. So I went down the store front to Brew Tea and bought some gift cards. Wish I could have given SomiSomi business, but nope. Just a suggestion, it's nice to have gift cards for customers to just pick up. One star less for not having gift cards and another star less for the person who didn't know how it works to purchase a e-gift card.

I had a single scoop with 2 flavors, vietnamese coffee and mint chocolate chip (or whatever the mint flavored ice cream was called). And both the glavors wee not that memorable to me, there was nothing that made them special. In fact, the vietnamese coffee had pieces of ice in it, like it had previously melted and re-frozen. Probably not a place I would visit again even if I were in the area.

Lemon custard how I love you - it's you, that I adore! I know Jarlings offers lots of flavors, but I can't try any more! All cities should understand custard and the difference between custard and ice cream. The world would be a kinder, gentler place.

The decor inside this place is beautiful. One you step in you're greeted by comfy chairs, big spacious mirrors and cute little iron and glass tables. The big display case is set back in the space with plenty of selections with a majority of them being vegan friendly. A couple of sweet ladies were running the store making coffee and serving treats. I chose a non-vegan blondie which was served on a cute little (prob antique) pattern plates like grandma had. The blondie i had was rich and soft with that typical brownie crust on top. I didn't order coffee as it was later in the day and i wasnt in the mood for any joe. About halfway into the blondie i needed a drink and the server hooked me up with a small glass of tap water. All in all a nice little bakery, really nice atmosphere, tasty treats and good service. It would have been nice for them to have a water cooler for an alternative to coffee, but other than that very nice.

I got the chocolate marshmallow cupcake and a strawberry ice cream cone. The cupcake was moist and beautiful to look at, with dark chocolate ganache covered marshmallow cream above the dark chocolate cupcake. The ice cream was super creamy and the scoop was considerably large! They are open late which made satisfying my sweet tooth after a Vegas show possible and fulfilling. I am anxious to try the other flavors of cupcakes and ice creams! I did sample the dark chocolate ice cream and found it to be exceptionally rich and creamy. I also tried some of my wife's red velvet upscale, moist and flavorful for sure!

Came to bring my niece to Carlo's bake shop she's a huge fan of cake boss and since she was in town she asked me to bring her here (she's 11yrs old) it was a little difficult locating the store but managed to find it. There was a long line but not as bad we did take a number and within 10 minutes we were taken care of. My nieces face was wowed with all the beautiful desserts. We ordered a large cannoli, a mini chocolate mousse cake and a mini red velvet cake. The texture of the cakes were very good and very moist and spongy. I loved it and most importantly made a highlight of the day with my niece. Would definitely be back to try out other desserts (:

I had been wanting to try Bouchon Bakery for years, so when I went to Vegas recently I finally got the opportunity, and I was really impressed with the freshness and quality of the pastries. I got a chocolate chunk cookie, a plain croissant, and a peanut butter and jelly macaron. The cookie was huge, chewy, and loaded with chocolate chunks, exactly how I like my chocolate chip/chunk cookies. The macaron was awesome (and I'm particular when it comes to macarons!) - beautifully and perfectly made, chewy with a well-balanced filling of peanut butter to jelly. It wasn't too sweet either, which some macarons can be. The croissant was flaky and buttery with lovely lamination - simple but delicious. As many others have noted, it is not easy to find, but it's worth the search! Can't wait to visit again next time I'm in town!

Smelled amazing in here. Couldn't help but go in and want to buy almost everything. My kids where craving donuts so got them each a chocolate donut. Didn't realize how big the size was. But they both enjoyed it and pretty much finished it. We where planning on going back to have some ice cream but didn't get the chance. Hopefully next time.
Got a few different things today. Slice of red velvet cake, Napoleon, a black and white cookie, and slice of pineapple upside down cake. Treats were very good and I will visit again in the future.

I had been so used to just having Mitchell's all the time that this was such a pleasant delight and truly a Cleveland gem! I don't hear about it often, maybe because I live on the East Side and there are more locations on the West. I personally like their ice cream better than Mitchell's. It's not only more of an old school alnd nostalgic feeling environment, but I also feel it's slightly less sweet so the flavor isnt overpowering, making your cone easy and pleasant to manage. I got the honey graham flavor, of course I had to pick something with honey in it! I see this as my favorite ice cream shop in Cleveland and would definitely enjoy it as a special treat I would venture out for in the future.

I have been following Ice Cream Social since they started as online only business in 2020. I absolutely loved the story behind the shop and their stance on social justice. The owner, Katrina, donates the money from her weekly ice cream sales to organizations in the local community fighting for social and racial equity. Not only is the story amazing, but the ice cream is beyond delicious! It's made from scratch in Madison. They frequently switch out their unique flavors and all the ice cream is gluten free (not that you can tell). So far, I've only tried the monster cookie ice cream. It was absolutely amazing- m&ms and cookie dough in every bite. The ice cream base is so creamy and delicious on its own as well. I can't wait to go back and try more flavors! The shop itself is SO cute! If you've followed Ice Cream Social on Instagram, you know Katrina put her heart and soul into every detail. She hand stained the ice cream bar, designed the sign, picked out all the different paints (possibly painted the shop too) and more. The shop has accent colors of dark blues, yellows, corals, pinks, and whites. It's such a cute combination of colors and works perfectly with all the LED signs and hanging pendant lights. Their official opening date is on Friday, March 11th. You NEED to check it out!

Delicious. This is the best donut store I have found since moving. The store has so many unique flavors and designs that anyone should be satisfied. On top of all of this the prices is great. One suggestion I would make is that if you want to get donuts from here be prepared to get up early. The donuts sell out quickly.

THE TOASTED MARSHMELLOW! I had a few friends in town today and we were in the mood for something sweet but something that wouldn't leave us full to the point that we wouldn't want to do anything the rest of the afternoon. Fatty Daddy's was just the spot! We each tried the toasted marshmellow on top and it was hand fired in front of us with a hand butane torch. As for the ice cream they had everything from a fruity pebbles and sorbets to coffee and hazlenut, and they were all amazing (we tried at least 5 each). The place is very clean and the owner was very sweet as well as patient as we tasted our way to the perfect flavor.

This ice cream shop is super cute and I love that it's open late night. It was highly recommended that I check this place out, so I did! I arrived 30mins to closing, and ordered the peanut butter and Vietnamese coffee. We ate on the picnic tables outside, and I enjoyed every minute of it.

Do yourself a flavor and have one of Amelie's Breakfast Croissants! I gave into the bacon, egg, and cheese croissant last night & it was divine! SO GOOD, it made me want to slap my momma, smoke a cigarette, and speak French! Oui Oui! Vive Le Amelie's French Bakery!

Decent ice cream. Good selection of flavors and generous with the mix ins. Lines can get long and sometimes they seem understaffed with only one window open. The guy I think is the owner/manager could use a refresher on his customer service skills. Can be pretty short with customers. I go there when bored with Ben & Jerry's flavors.
All hype. The cookies were crunchy and had a weird texture. The ice cream/milkshakes were nothing special. I'm would not go back there.
OMG this place is worth the drive! I came from South Phoenix area and I loved it. And now that they have the Sea Salt Carmels sold in a bag it's a sin. You HAVE to try this place!

Nah...not worth it...I heard about Milk coming from LA and was disappointed my first time trying it while staying at Cosmo. Ordered the milk bar pie for $6. Got back to my room and tasted this underwhelming oat bar that I definitely know I can make myself.
Its amazing matcha place ! Must visit if in chandler , variety of matcha item on the menu

We stopped by here on a hot day based on friend's recommendations. This place is great. Everything is so fresh and the flavors are so bright! I haven't had ice cream this good in a long time. We'll be stopping by here quite a bit. Lots of different flavors to try out.

I don't know who taught y'all how to make a cannoli but oh goodness it's clear that no one has ever shown you how to strain ricotta cheese so that you don't have to cut it with cream cheese. For a cannoli that costs over $6, it's pathetic. Do better. Secondly, over $9 for a cake that is no bigger than a chocolate lava cake from dominos. Again, you can do better. It's absolutely shameful that you would charge that amount for that tiny piece of cake. Im not discrediting the time, effort, and cost of ingredients by any means. Pictures for comparison with a diet coke can, a butter keeper, and a McDonald's bbq sauce cup. Don't waste your money. You're better off going literally anywhere else.
Amazing online customer service!!!! We ordered a GC for a friend (little boy) who had a tonsillectomy - they sent it out asap and he got it the very next day. Thank you!!!

OMG. Came here from a recommendation from a coworker and was not disappointed. Ice cream here is delicious and generous! I can't say "best ice cream ever" but it's definitely worth a visit. ITS WINDOW SERVICE ONLY so don't get confused and try to open any of the doors. I got a double scoop of Oreo and cookie dough. Food was creamy and sweet. Definitely high quality ice cream. Overall, great option if you had a great meal and need something sweet. Highly recommended.

The first time I tried Jeni's, I really didn't like it. I thought they were trying way too hard to be different and to stand out. BUT now I really really like it. Their flavors are different, but such good quality. Their waffle cones are hit or miss. Sometimes they are really good, and sometimes there's a weird taste like the batter is old or something is off. Staff is always friendly. It is a bit pricey, but for quality, homemade ice cream, it's a treat!
We got pumpkin, apple, and cherry for Thanksgiving, along with their dinner rolls! Made our Thanksgiving dinner complete!

Great place open day and night for your sweet tooth fix! The food is pretty good here and it is all very "pretty". I have been about 9 times and always had good quality/tasting food here. The coffee is not bad either. (wish cups were larger).

No! Never again! I stopped in last week to pick up a few things, but mainly some chocolate jalapeÃ±os as a gift for a friend. The shop had a decent variety of things to choose from, but nothing overly impressive. I gifted the jalapeÃ±os to a friend and she ate one immediately and said it tasted good. That evening she sent me a photo of the other jalapeÃ±o with the chocolate pulled off and it was covered in MOLD! I emailed the shop and Abby from their marketing department was quick to reply, but said that even though the jalapeÃ±os are prepared fresh daily, some things are out of their control. In my experience if it was prepared fresh daily, mold would not have had a chance to grow. Abby did refund my money, minus the tip I left, but this is just too gross not to share!
The best ice cream shop in Phoenix! Such creative flavors that were all delicious. The owner was very welcoming and was generous enough to give us several samples. Will definitely be returning!

Firstly, I just LOVE LOVE LOVE the atmosphere of the place! It has a real vintage feel to it, with all of the old furnishings and decorations. Secondly, the staff here always have a big smile on their face while they are helping you at the counter! THIRDLY, obviously we cannot forget about the yummy desserts that they serve! There is a wide variety, so anybody who comes will be sure to find something to satisfy their taste buds. :) They also serve sandwiches for lunch and dinner, and stay open every day for 24 hours. This is a good place to just go hangout with friends, enjoy a quick bite, or even go to study! I always come back, and I plan to soon.

An east-sider, I make it to the west side of Cleveland only occasionally. This morning, I made a run over to buy pierogies (got family coming in to town, and there was a request), and stopped at Jack Frost because it was on the way, and hey, I've got family coming in to town, right? These are company's-coming donuts for sure, good for breakfast, snack, after-pierogie-dinner dessert, another snack. The staff is helpful, and while labels might move the line along, it's good to talk with the folks who made the food you're going to eat. Choosing a dozen is part of the fun - salted caramel, Boston cream, French toast, maple bacon, chocolate something/everything, and a raspberry zinger - and they taste as good as they look!

This ice cream was good but I'm not sure if it was really worth the hype in my opinion. You can get good ice cream without standing in a 25 minute line. Definitely worth stopping if the line looks short but not really worth the huge wait.

We got the cookie monster special which is the blue ice cream with mini cookies and oreo crumbs, and a cone with fruity pebbles mixed in and topped with marshmellow charms. The marshmallow charms were stale. The blue ice cream was noticeably less cold than the vanilla ice cream and had a paste like consistancy, but the cookie monster tasted good.

We had to stop in here since my husband and I loved the other locations (Monterey, San Francisco & Hollywood). The other scoop shops in this chain offer dine in options with glassware, but this location only allows you to get your ice cream in plastic containers. Not a big deal, just pointing out one of the differences that I noticed. Prices here are a bit high (as are the other Ghirardelli Shops), but the quality of the ice cream is quite great. My husband was a bit disappointed that the peanut butter sauce sundaes are no longer on the menu, but there are still many great choices. Service was good, it took a bit of time to get our malts, but not unreasonably long. Pretty tasty, but there are probably more cost effective options to take a family too.

It was very cute the way everything is set up I see why sprinkles is so popular I did not try a cupcake I was more in the mood for ice cream so I got the root beer float which was decent..Nothing spectacular.from an ice cream perspective this place was OK and very cute but as far as the best dessert ever....not so sure

I have lived in the area of Page's Dairy Mart for about 40 yrs. I have always enjoyed the ice cream until" this" day. I ordered an artic swirl (chocolate ice cream with chocolate chip cookie dough) I have ordered this same item over and over again. When I took first taste, no chocolate chip cookie dough pieces, second taste, same thing, third taste, same thing and so on for approximately 5 or 6 tastes. I took the cup with remaining up to counter and asked them to remake, I was denied told it would waste "their" money, nothing about mine, what I had ordered was more expensive than plain chocolate ice cream. They dumped what was in the medium cup into a small and handed back to me. Well it wasn't even a medium desert, since it fit into a small cup. I even tipped the girl $2 when I first received my desert. I will never return, to make any other purchases. I will however return to express my disdain to the owner when I can find him there. I hope he reads this.
If I ever had to choose a last meal before death, it would consist of Villani's crÃ¨me puffs and a slice of chocolate peanut butter ganache cake
If I were you... Order literally anything and you'll get an amazing treat that's 100% insta-material. I have nothing more to say.

Fatty Daddy's is the hidden gem of the ice cream cave. Small and quaint, but very clean and hospitable with a relaxed atmosphere. My family and i went here last night and were soooooooo impressed!!! I got the Strawberry Cheesecake ice cream, with an in house made, fruity pebble macaron, an oooey-gooey-melty, homemade marshmallow with chocolate on top- was it absolutely AMAAAAAAZING and worth every single calorie???? YES MA'AM!!! We chatted it up with the sweet and friendly owner, Lala i believe was her name and just had a really enjoyable time. I loved the glittery spin art on the wall and tgeir adorable little penguin. I really like the fact that they have what is available listed and the different types of cups and sundaes you can get. Next time i would like to try their bubbly waffle and i will ALWAYS get that toasted marshmallow on top. It is a little hard to find and you won't see it from the main street so definitely look out for it!!! I will definitely be back! (:

They have the best croissants in the entire city, hands down. Art Mart is a distant second. Even Hopscotch's butter croissant is amazing; as good as one would find in France. I actually think this place has stepped up its game even more since Covid.

Ok. For 17.56 I got 2 macaroon salted brownie and eclair small coffee. My wife wanted a vanilla latte one pump of vanilla she does not love it very sweet. She asked the man for the one pump and he said no it must have three pumps and they can not change it... customer service is a basic requirement now and losing a customer for such a senseless issue is a problem. And honesty people it's way to expensive for the common person. I think it's somewhat snotie. Also coffee was not that great. Duncan donuts had better coffee and service and that is a problem.

I went to the new Milk in Vegas after hearing the hype and I must say it wasn't worth it at all. I got the cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes and it didn't taste like anything at all. I ate the whole thing and felt like I ate a cone of air. There was zero flavor - you could hardly call that cereal milk. I also sampled the sweet potato pie soft serve, and while it had a lot of flavor, it didn't exactly taste like sweet potato pie. There was something a little off about it. The only thing it was good for was a cute photo of the ice cream in front of the neon sign. Milk is definitely all hype, overpriced, and not worth it.

Extraordinary customer service from the guy and gals at the counter today! It's consistent too. Every time I have been here the service has been great! Today's candy cane shake was cool and refreshing in a pepperminty type way. The salted chocolate chip cookie was fantastic, and not too heavy on the chocolate like some chocolate chunk cookies are. Be warned: Churn is not cheap, but they're definitely serving up high quality ice cream and baked goods. It's a good place for gifts too (they had very nice make-your-own cookie and hot chocolate sets, plus little toys and unique candies). If you're willing to fork over a few more dollars than DQ further down the road, you'll be pleasantly surprised. Don't forget to use the newer, super convenient parking lot next to the Windsor/Churn/Hub building!

Wow! This place is a little gem in the Roosevelt neighborhood. We had some lunch at Wilderness and then stopped here for dessert. This ice cream was DELICIOUS! It was the most perfect consistency! All of the flavors were amazing, but I would highly recommend the espresso and the nutella. I seriously can't wait to come back!
Enjoyed the caramel brownie. My friends had said to stop in to try it before leaving town and one of the best brownies I have ever had in my life. The line was long, but pretty much worth the wait

Me and my friend ventured here one day while we were on the strip because i finally wanted to try a cannoli. We made it before close and while we were standing in line, we heard the worker behind the counter tell another patron that there were no cannolis... I'm pretty sure that my heart sank a little because i specifically went to try a cannoli. we ended up spending like forty dollars on two cupcakes two lobster tails and a strawberry shortcake. i felt that everything was extremely overpriced but because of where we were thats the reason why. i told my self that i shouldn't buy anything else, but i had to. everything was okay and i wasn't super impressed like dying to go back, but maybe i was just disappointed that i didn't get a cannoli. the staff was very kind and helpful other wise but had no explanation as to why there weren't any cannolis.
One of two cupcake shops that my picky husband likes. Online ordering and curbside pickup won me over. 5 Stars!
The chocolate coconut milk ice cream is the best I've ever had!! My mom raves about you caramel pecan (vegan.) We are both allergic to dairy products.
10/10 would recommend! The staff was very nice and the ice cream choices are endless! So many different flavors, and signature flavors! Will be coming back again!
Found this place on Yelp. We tried the cookie cup and it was more than we expected. We chose banana and mascarpone ice cream with a red velvet macaron. It was delicious.
My daughter liked it. Pricey, small portion. Located at the Cosmopolitan Check it out.
Dutch chocolate ice cream in a pretzel cone=divine. However the said cone is too thick, dry and hard to eat once the ice cream is gone.
Introduced a friend to the goodness of Sweet Republic. Had the Madagascar Vanilla, and the Eggnog. The vanilla was good, but the Eggnog tasted like Christmas! I don't visit often enough.

Blah, stale donuts. For $17 I got 3 Donuts 2 coffees. Selection was small for 10:30 on a Monday so I had to pick what was left or they offered me an ice cream for breakfast.... apple fritter was rock hard, strawberry cheesecake donut tasted like a regular jelly filled donut, and birthday donut was a regular sprinkled donut... nothing special. Very disappointing. Used to newer donut shops were donuts are made fresh per hour (sidecar, dough donuts)
This is some life changing ice cream!! I've been here twice and it's amazing! This time I had the carrot cake and it was awesome! I wish I don't live 150 miles away!

Pastries were fine. It doesn't' even matter because of the god awful service we received. At first, I thought maybe the guy behind the counter was trying to be funny because he was being such an obnoxious di@#. He was not funny, he was just an ass. Everything he said, other than " would you like a coffee" was rude. He swung the bag with my pastry on it as he gleefully skipped to the register. He insulted How I ordered, he insulted how I inserted my credit card, and he got my order wrong. Is this guy family? Because he shouldn't be working anywhere near the public.

I'm tempted to not share how amazing this place is because it is one of those gems you want to keep to yourself. This is the best ice cream I have ever had in my life. I tried a doughnut sammy with Fat Elvis ice cream and cocoa pebbles. I can't wait to go back to have something else. The peach habanero was hard to not get as well but I will next time. Bottom line is you have to try this place because it is amazing.

I think the "Brand" makes them taste better than they really are. Don't get me wrong, they're good, but the price doesn't justify the taste. We came in tonight (a Tuesday) 10minutes before they closed. We grabbed our cupcakes 1st. The girl (Might be named Patricia, because that's what our receipt said (asian/Filipino)) at the counter seemed miserable. She slouched, didn't smile and was just such a downer. That was a bummer, because I was really excited that we made it in before they closed. I had promised my toddler a cupcake after dinner, but he ended up falling asleep before we got to Sprinkles. Anywho she kind of killed our excitement, but luckily the girls (Z Cupcak) over on the Ice Cream side were SOOOO nice, and got us back into an excited mood. They were so friendly like the Sprinkles staff we're used to. Our local shop is in Newport Beach and they are always great! We ordered the Capt'n Crunch flavored Ice Cream. The 1st bite was amazing, but unfortunately the Cap'n Crunch flavor didn't last through out the whole cone. I dont know if it was just me, but it ended up just tasting like vanilla after a couple bites. All in all it was a good visit because my son was happy with his after dinner late night treat. ............ Thank you to the girls on the Ice Cream side for being so "sweet", and making us feel like valued customers.

So, past me is not a good person, obviously. I've changed my mind about Batch. Realistically, I probably ordered the wrong things, as in, wrong for my palate. My favorite is probably the honey almond tart, or something like that. There's also the tiny derby pie that I love. I would not be opposed if someone were to get me a cake from here for no specific occasion. I've had a slice of chocolate peanut butter (I think) and it was wonderful!
Tasty and fun to sit in with a friend. I wish there was a list of all the macaron flavors because I had to have her keep repeating what everything was so I could make up my mind which to buy

This is such a cool and unique donut place. We stopped in on a Saturday morning to check it out. They gave a free character decorated donut to our son which I believe they do on saturdays. My wife and I tried the Nutella, pop tart and Oreo birthday donut. They were all very good and very filling. The donuts are a bit more expensive than a store donut, but they are worth it given the quality and size of the donuts. Give it a try if you're in the area but go early they sell out most days.

Never thought you could make bad ice cream but the people at this place managed it. It has to be, by FAR, the worst ice cream/soft serve I've had in my life. The cheapest, generic ice cream sandwich at a gas station is much much better. Maybe I had a bad batch but based on the other reviews I think it's just bad all the time. If you enjoy flavorless, not sweet , but extremely salty "ice cream" this is the place for you. And then they go the other way and use ONLY sugar as an ingredient in everything else. I have no idea why there is a line here.

We waited in a hefty line on a Saturday night. It looks like there is seating during non-Covid times that is cute and cozy. The bakery could have benefitted from air flow and low volume music to create a lighter mood. Now for the food: 1) The chocolate ganache mousse cup was to die for 2) The mini key lime tart was okay-the crust is what killed it for me. I was most looking forward to this item. 3) I had a taste of the entremet. It was like a springtime meadow with hints of lemon. Next time I'm definitely trying an entire serving of this item.
$3.95 for about two bites of ice cream. WAY OVER PRICED. And it's $6.95 if you want a little cookie on top. Keep driving. Too little for too much $.

Worst customer service ever. DO NOT use a Credit Card here (SCAM). Was there on Saturday Oct 3, 2015 evening with my family. We decided to buy a few pastries which should have costed under $20. Gave the credit card to the cashier and she charge me $60. Only then, did she noticed that she charged me for one TRAY of lobster tails instead ONE lobster tail. Fine, I asked that she just cancel and recharge my CC and I will on my way. Her reply was "No, it was our store policy to only give store credit. But if I paid in cash, I could have given you cash back. You must take store credit" Then I asked to speak to Josh the manager. He was the rudest and most incompetent manager ever. Every time I would try to put a word in, his responds was "No it was our store policy to only give store credit." This must have been his respond for about 10 times like a robot. So I asked if him, "if he was to have shopped at another merchant, and was missed charged $5000, how would he like to be given store credit only?" This is a matter of principle not the $45 that was over charged. I asked, "if you can not give store credit, can you give me back $45 in cash?" This is when Josh's incompetence comes in to play.
